The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$
be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable, meaning
that $F$ is Fréchet differentiable at each point of $U$ and
$x\mapsto F'(x)$ is continuous in operator norm. The input consists of an
initial point $x_0\in U$, a datum $y^\delta\in Y$, a positive noise bound
$\delta>0$, a discrepancy factor $\tau>1$, a forcing fraction $\sigma\in(0,1)$,
a range-approximation margin $\gamma>1$, and a finite update budget
$N_{\max}\in\mathbb N_0:=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. Assume an exact solution $x^\dagger\in U$ exists
with $F(x^\dagger)=y$ and $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$. At every state
$x_n^\delta$ before the discrepancy stop, the admissible local range condition
is
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)(x^\dagger-x_n^\delta)+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y.$$

For $x_n^\delta\in U$ and $\alpha>0$, define $h_{n,\alpha}$ to be the unique
global minimizer over $h\in X$ of the regularized linearized least-squares
objective
$$J_{n,\alpha}(h):=\frac12\|F'(x_n^\delta)h+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y^2+\frac\alpha2\|h\|_X^2.$$
Equivalently, it is the unique solution of
$$\bigl(F'(x_n^\delta)^*F'(x_n^\delta)+\alpha I_X\bigr)h_{n,\alpha}=F'(x_n^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)).$$
Here $I_X$ is the identity operator on $X$.
The forcing rule selects any $\alpha_n>0$ for which
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)h_{n,\alpha_n}+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y=\sigma\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y,$$
and sets $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_{n,\alpha_n}$. The displayed range
condition is a sufficient condition for the forcing rule to have such a
parameter; it is not an input to either linearized minimization problem.

For a finite run, inspect $n=0,1,\ldots,N_{\max}$ in order. If
$x_n^\delta\notin U$, return $(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{domain-failure})$. If
$\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\tau\delta$, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{discrepancy})$. If $n=N_{\max}$, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{budget-exhausted})$. Otherwise request the exact
regularized minimizer and a positive parameter satisfying the forcing rule.
If the exact minimizer cannot be certified, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{solve-unverified})$; if the parameter selector cannot
return a positive parameter satisfying the displayed equality, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{forcing-unavailable})$. After both exact calls succeed,
set $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_{n,\alpha_n}$ and continue. Each return is a
triple of state, index, and status. No convergence claim is attached to the
failure statuses or to a budget-exhausted state.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $T:X\to Y$ be
a bounded linear operator, let $r\in Y$ be nonzero, and let
$\sigma\in(0,1)$ and $\gamma>1$. Suppose that a fixed $v\in X$ satisfies
$$\|Tv-r\|_Y\le\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}\|r\|_Y.$$
For each $\alpha>0$, the functional
$$\Phi_\alpha(h):=\frac12\|Th-r\|_Y^2+\frac\alpha2\|h\|_X^2\qquad(h\in X)$$
has the unique global minimizer
$$h_\alpha=(T^*T+\alpha I_X)^{-1}T^*r,$$
where $T^*$ is the Hilbert adjoint and $I_X$ is the identity on $X$. Moreover,
there exists at least one $\alpha>0$ for which
$$\|Th_\alpha-r\|_Y=\sigma\|r\|_Y.$$

Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let
$F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at every point of $U$ with
$x\mapsto F'(x)$ continuous in operator norm. Let $V\subseteq U$ and let
$c>0$ be such that, for every $u,\tilde u\in V$,
$$\|F(u)-F(\tilde u)-F'(u)(u-\tilde u)\|_Y\le c\|u-\tilde u\|_X\|F(u)-F(\tilde u)\|_Y.$$
Suppose
$x^\dagger,x\in V$, $F(x^\dagger)=y$, $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$ with
$\delta\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|x-x^\dagger\|_X\le e$. If
$R:=\|F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y>\tau\delta$, then

$$\|F'(x)(x^\dagger-x)+F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{1+ce(1+\tau)}{\tau}R.$$

In particular, if $\sigma\in(0,1)$, $e\le e_0$, and
$$\gamma:=\frac{\sigma\tau}{1+ce_0(1+\tau)}>1,$$
then
$$\|F'(x)(x^\dagger-x)+F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}R.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $H$ and $K$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces and let $T\in\mathcal B(H,K)$ be a bounded linear operator ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]). For fixed $y\in K$ the map

$$x\longmapsto\langle Tx,y\rangle_K$$

is a bounded linear functional on $H$: it is linear in $x$ because $T$ is linear and the pairing is linear in its first argument, and $|\langle Tx,y\rangle_K|\le\|Tx\|\,\|y\|\le\|T\|\,\|x\|\,\|y\|$ by Cauchy–Schwarz and the operator-norm inequality ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]], [[def-operator-norm]]). By Riesz representation ([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]) there is therefore a unique vector $T^*y\in H$ with

$$\langle Tx,y\rangle_K=\langle x,T^*y\rangle_H\qquad\text{for every }x\in H .$$

The **Hilbert adjoint** of $T$ is the map

$$T^*:K\longrightarrow H,\qquad y\longmapsto T^*y .$$

It is the unique map $K\to H$ satisfying the displayed identity, since two such maps have $\langle x,(T^*_1-T^*_2)y\rangle=0$ for all $x$ and hence $(T^*_1-T^*_2)y=0$ by positive definiteness.

**The dictionary with the Banach transpose.** Write $R_H:H\to H^*$ and $R_K:K\to K^*$ for the Riesz maps $R_H(x)=\langle\,\cdot\,,x\rangle_H$ and $R_K(y)=\langle\,\cdot\,,y\rangle_K$, and let $T'\in\mathcal B(K^*,H^*)$ be the transpose of $T$, $(T'g)(x)=g(Tx)$ ([[def-transpose-of-a-bounded-operator]]). Then for all $y\in K$ and $x\in H$,

$$\bigl(R_H(T^*y)\bigr)(x)=\langle x,T^*y\rangle_H=\langle Tx,y\rangle_K=(R_Ky)(Tx)=\bigl(T'(R_Ky)\bigr)(x),$$

so $R_H\,T^*=T'\,R_K$. The Hilbert adjoint is thus the Banach transpose conjugated by the Riesz identifications of $H$ and $K$ with their duals; it is a different operator from $T'$ whenever the Riesz maps are conjugate-linear.

Let $F$ be an ordered field (Ordered field) and let $x, y \in F$, with
$|x|$ the absolute value (Absolute value in an ordered field). Then

$$|x| \ge 0; \quad |x| = 0 \iff x = 0; \quad -|x| \le x \le |x|; \quad |-x| = |x|; \quad |xy| = |x|\,|y|;$$

and, for every $c > 0$, one has $|x| < c \iff -c < x < c$.

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field, and let
$T:X\to Y$ be bounded in the sense of [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]. The
**operator norm** of $T$ is

$$\|T\| := \sup\{\|Tx\| : x \in X,\ \|x\| \le 1\}.$$

The set on the right contains $0$ and every bound $C$ for $T$ bounds it
above. Thus its finite real supremum exists by the proved least-upper-bound
property of the library's real field ([[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]).
In particular every number strictly below the supremum is exceeded by a
member of this set; otherwise it would be a smaller upper bound. No choice
principle is used for this assertion.

The same number is the least bound of $T$:

$$\|T\| = \inf\{C \ge 0 : \|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \text{ for all } x \in X\}.$$

If $X \ne \{0\}$, positive homogeneity also gives

$$\|T\| = \sup\{\|Tx\| : \|x\| = 1\}.$$

When $X = \{0\}$, the unit sphere is empty and the unit-ball supremum is $0$,
so $\|T\| = 0$.

Let $V$ be a real or complex inner-product space with induced length $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$. Then $\|v\|\ge0$ with $\|v\|=0$ exactly for $v=0$, $\|\lambda v\|=|\lambda|\,\|v\|$ for every scalar $\lambda$, and $\|u+v\|\le\|u\|+\|v\|$; hence $\|\cdot\|$ is a norm on $V$, read over $\mathbb R$ by [[def-norm-and-normed-space]] and over $\mathbb C$ by [[def-complex-norm-and-complex-normed-space]].

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, with **conjugation** $z\mapsto\overline z$
the identity on $\mathbb R$ and complex conjugation on $\mathbb C$
(Real and imaginary parts, complex conjugation, and modulus). A **real** or
**complex inner-product space** is an $\mathbb F$-vector space $V$ together with
an inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:V\times V\to\mathbb F$ in the sense
of Real and complex inner product spaces, with the inner product linear in the first argument: for all $u,v,w\in V$ and $a,b\in\mathbb F$,

$$\langle au+bv,w\rangle=a\langle u,w\rangle+b\langle v,w\rangle,\qquad \langle u,v\rangle=\overline{\langle v,u\rangle},\qquad \langle v,v\rangle\ge0,\quad \langle v,v\rangle=0\iff v=0 .$$

**Conjugate-linearity in the second argument.** Conjugate symmetry together with
linearity in the first argument gives, for all $w\in V$,

$$\langle w,au+bv\rangle=\overline{\langle au+bv,w\rangle}=\overline{a\langle u,w\rangle+b\langle v,w\rangle}=\overline a\,\langle w,u\rangle+\overline b\,\langle w,v\rangle .$$

**Induced length.** The **induced length**, or inner-product norm, of $v$ is

makes $\langle v,v\rangle$ a nonnegative real with a unique nonnegative square

**The convention on this page.** Every inner-product space below is real or

In the real case conjugation is the identity and $|z|$ is the absolute value of

derivations.claim:
For any $z\in X$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, expansion using [F6] gives
$$\Phi_\alpha(h+tz)-\Phi_\alpha(h)=t\bigl(\langle Th-r,Tz\rangle_Y+\alpha\langle h,z\rangle_X\bigr)+\frac{t^2}{2}\bigl(\|Tz\|_Y^2+\alpha\|z\|_X^2\bigr).$$
Since $h$ is a global minimizer, this is nonnegative for every $t$. Its linear coefficient must therefore vanish: if it were nonzero, a sufficiently small $t$ of the opposite sign would make the displayed difference negative. By [F3], $\langle T^*(Th-r)+\alpha h,z\rangle_X=0$ for every $z$; taking $z=T^*(Th-r)+\alpha h$ and using positive definiteness gives $T^*(Th-r)+\alpha h=0$. Set $q:=r-Th$, so $\alpha h=T^*q$. Therefore [F3] gives $\alpha\langle h,e\rangle_X=\langle q,Te\rangle_Y$, and taking the inner product of $\alpha h=T^*q$ with $h$ gives $\alpha\|h\|_X^2=\langle q,Th\rangle_Y=\langle q,r\rangle_Y-\|q\|_Y^2$.

Put $w:=Te+r$. By [F6] and step 1.1, $\|e+h\|_X^2-\|e\|_X^2=\frac2\alpha\langle q,w\rangle_Y-\|h\|_X^2-\frac2\alpha\|q\|_Y^2.$ Indeed, $Te=w-r$; substitute this into $2\langle e,h\rangle+\|h\|^2$ and use $\langle q,r\rangle=\alpha\|h\|^2+\|q\|^2$.

By [F2], $\|q\|_Y=\sigma\|r\|_Y$ and $\|w\|_Y\le(\sigma/\gamma)\|r\|_Y$. Thus [F4] gives $2\langle q,w\rangle_Y\le2|\langle q,w\rangle_Y|\le2\|q\|_Y\|w\|_Y\le2\sigma^2\|r\|_Y^2/\gamma$. Substituting this and $\|q\|_Y^2=\sigma^2\|r\|_Y^2$ into step 2.1 yields $\|e\|_X^2-\|e+h\|_X^2\ge\|h\|_X^2+\frac{2(\gamma-1)\sigma^2}{\gamma\alpha}\|r\|_Y^2,$ which is the first claim.

Applying $T$ to $\alpha h=T^*q$ and using $q=r-Th$ gives $(TT^*+\alpha I_Y)q=\alpha r$. By [F8], $\alpha\|r\|_Y=\|(TT^*+\alpha I_Y)q\|_Y\le\|TT^*q\|_Y+\alpha\|q\|_Y$. The unit-ball definition [F7] gives $\|T^*q\|_X\le\|T^*\|\|q\|_Y$ and $\|T(T^*q)\|_Y\le\|T\|\|T^*q\|_X$: if an input vector is nonzero, divide it by its norm to place it in the unit ball; if it is zero, the bound is immediate. Then [F5] gives $\|TT^*q\|_Y\le\|T\|\|T^*\|\|q\|_Y=\|T\|^2\|q\|_Y$. Thus, using $\|T\|\le M$ and the forcing equality, $\alpha\|r\|_Y\le(M^2+\alpha)\sigma\|r\|_Y.$ Since $r\ne0$, divide by $\|r\|_Y$ and rearrange using $1-\sigma>0$ to obtain $\alpha\le\sigma M^2/(1-\sigma)$.

First variation in every real direction gives T*(Th-r)+alpha*h=0 (positive alpha); q=r-Th gives alpha*h=T*q with correct signs. With w=Te+r, expansion yields difference=2<q,w>/alpha-||h||^2-2||q||^2/alpha. CS and exact forcing give the stated positive decrement coefficient 2(gamma-1)sigma^2/(gamma*alpha). For parameter bound, applying T yields (TT*+alpha I)q=alpha*r; triangle and ||T*||=||T|| give alpha<=sigma*M^2/(1-sigma) after dividing only by nonzero ||r||. Unit-ball operator norm handles zero arguments explicitly. h=0 would contradict forcing with r!=0 and sigma<1; e=0 likewise incompatible with the range margin. No alpha=0 or sigma endpoint is allowed. No inexact solve conclusion, full AC, DC, diagram, or unstated convergence step. Reader blank-line formatting retained; no mathematical or interface repair required.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let
$F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable, meaning that $F$ is
Fréchet differentiable at each point of $U$ and $x\mapsto F'(x)$ is continuous
in operator norm. For a subset $V\subseteq U$ and a constant $c>0$, the
**product-type tangential cone condition on $V$ with constant $c$** is the
requirement that, for every $x,\tilde x\in V$,

$$\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)-F'(x)(x-\tilde x)\|_Y\le c\|x-\tilde x\|_X\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)\|_Y.$$

Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let
$F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at every point of $U$ with
$x\mapsto F'(x)$ continuous in operator norm. Let $V\subseteq U$ and let
$c>0$ be such that, for every $u,\tilde u\in V$,
$$\|F(u)-F(\tilde u)-F'(u)(u-\tilde u)\|_Y\le c\|u-\tilde u\|_X\|F(u)-F(\tilde u)\|_Y.$$
Suppose
$x^\dagger,x\in V$, $F(x^\dagger)=y$, $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$ with
$\delta\ge0$, $\tau>0$, and $\|x-x^\dagger\|_X\le e$. If
$R:=\|F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y>\tau\delta$, then

$$\|F'(x)(x^\dagger-x)+F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{1+ce(1+\tau)}{\tau}R.$$

In particular, if $\sigma\in(0,1)$, $e\le e_0$, and
$$\gamma:=\frac{\sigma\tau}{1+ce_0(1+\tau)}>1,$$
then
$$\|F'(x)(x^\dagger-x)+F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}R.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$
be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable, meaning
that $F$ is Fréchet differentiable at each point of $U$ and
$x\mapsto F'(x)$ is continuous in operator norm. The input consists of an
initial point $x_0\in U$, a datum $y^\delta\in Y$, a positive noise bound
$\delta>0$, a discrepancy factor $\tau>1$, a forcing fraction $\sigma\in(0,1)$,
a range-approximation margin $\gamma>1$, and a finite update budget
$N_{\max}\in\mathbb N_0:=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. Assume an exact solution $x^\dagger\in U$ exists
with $F(x^\dagger)=y$ and $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$. At every state
$x_n^\delta$ before the discrepancy stop, the admissible local range condition
is
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)(x^\dagger-x_n^\delta)+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y.$$

For $x_n^\delta\in U$ and $\alpha>0$, define $h_{n,\alpha}$ to be the unique
global minimizer over $h\in X$ of the regularized linearized least-squares
objective
$$J_{n,\alpha}(h):=\frac12\|F'(x_n^\delta)h+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y^2+\frac\alpha2\|h\|_X^2.$$
Equivalently, it is the unique solution of
$$\bigl(F'(x_n^\delta)^*F'(x_n^\delta)+\alpha I_X\bigr)h_{n,\alpha}=F'(x_n^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)).$$
Here $I_X$ is the identity operator on $X$.
The forcing rule selects any $\alpha_n>0$ for which
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)h_{n,\alpha_n}+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y=\sigma\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y,$$
and sets $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_{n,\alpha_n}$. The displayed range
condition is a sufficient condition for the forcing rule to have such a
parameter; it is not an input to either linearized minimization problem.

For a finite run, inspect $n=0,1,\ldots,N_{\max}$ in order. If
$x_n^\delta\notin U$, return $(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{domain-failure})$. If
$\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\tau\delta$, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{discrepancy})$. If $n=N_{\max}$, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{budget-exhausted})$. Otherwise request the exact
regularized minimizer and a positive parameter satisfying the forcing rule.
If the exact minimizer cannot be certified, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{solve-unverified})$; if the parameter selector cannot
return a positive parameter satisfying the displayed equality, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{forcing-unavailable})$. After both exact calls succeed,
set $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_{n,\alpha_n}$ and continue. Each return is a
triple of state, index, and status. No convergence claim is attached to the
failure statuses or to a budget-exhausted state.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $T:X\to Y$ be
bounded linear with Hilbert adjoint $T^*$, and let $e\in X$ and
$r\in Y\setminus\{0\}$. Suppose $0<\sigma<1$, $\gamma>1$, $\alpha>0$,
and $h$ is the unique minimizer of
$$h\longmapsto\frac12\|Th-r\|_Y^2+\frac\alpha2\|h\|_X^2.$$
Assume its residual forcing and the range-approximation condition are
$$\|Th-r\|_Y=\sigma\|r\|_Y,$$
$$\|Te+r\|_Y\le\frac\sigma\gamma\|r\|_Y.$$
Then
$$\|e\|_X^2-\|e+h\|_X^2\ge\|h\|_X^2+\frac{2(\gamma-1)\sigma^2}{\gamma\alpha}\|r\|_Y^2.$$
If also $\|T\|\le M$ for some $M>0$, then
$$\alpha\le\frac{\sigma M^2}{1-\sigma}.$$

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because The exponential is a continuous bijection from $\mathbb{R}$ onto $(0,\infty)$ states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

The Cauchy-sequence reals $\mathbb{R}_C$ ([[thm-reals-ordered-field]]) are
**Archimedean** ([[def-archimedean-field]]): for every $x \in \mathbb{R}_C$
there is a natural number $n$ with $x < n \cdot 1$, where the canonical natural
$n \cdot 1$ is the class $\hat n$ of the constant rational sequence $n$.
Equivalently, the canonical naturals $(\hat n)_{n \ge 1}$ are cofinal.

Let $V$ be a real or complex inner-product space with induced length $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$. Then $\|v\|\ge0$ with $\|v\|=0$ exactly for $v=0$, $\|\lambda v\|=|\lambda|\,\|v\|$ for every scalar $\lambda$, and $\|u+v\|\le\|u\|+\|v\|$; hence $\|\cdot\|$ is a norm on $V$, read over $\mathbb R$ by [[def-norm-and-normed-space]] and over $\mathbb C$ by [[def-complex-norm-and-complex-normed-space]].

On this page the scalar field is the field $\mathbb R$ of real numbers: $X$, $Y$
and $Z$ always denote real Banach spaces ([[def-banach-space]]) and $U
\subseteq X$ always denotes an open subset of $X$, in the metric topology of the
norm ([[def-metric-topology]]).

Let $f : U \to Y$ be a map and let $x \in U$. For a bounded linear operator
$T \in \mathcal B(X,Y)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]) write

$$r(h) := f(x+h) - f(x) - Th \qquad (h \in X,\ x+h \in U).$$

Then $f$ is **Fréchet differentiable at $x$** when there is
$T \in \mathcal B(X,Y)$ with

$$\lim_{\substack{h \to 0 \\ h \ne 0}} \frac{\|f(x+h)-f(x)-Th\|}{\|h\|} = 0 ,$$

the limit being taken over those $h$ with $x + h \in U$. Such an operator $T$ is
a **Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$**, written $T = Df(x)$, and $\|T\|$ is its
operator norm ([[def-operator-norm]]). When $f$ is Fréchet differentiable at
every point of $U$, $f$ is **differentiable on $U$** and the **derivative** is
the map $Df : U \to \mathcal B(X,Y)$, $x \mapsto Df(x)$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field, and let
$T:X\to Y$ be bounded in the sense of [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]. The
**operator norm** of $T$ is

$$\|T\| := \sup\{\|Tx\| : x \in X,\ \|x\| \le 1\}.$$

The set on the right contains $0$ and every bound $C$ for $T$ bounds it
above. Thus its finite real supremum exists by the proved least-upper-bound
property of the library's real field ([[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]).
In particular every number strictly below the supremum is exceeded by a
member of this set; otherwise it would be a smaller upper bound. No choice
principle is used for this assertion.

The same number is the least bound of $T$:

$$\|T\| = \inf\{C \ge 0 : \|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \text{ for all } x \in X\}.$$

If $X \ne \{0\}$, positive homogeneity also gives

$$\|T\| = \sup\{\|Tx\| : \|x\| = 1\}.$$

When $X = \{0\}$, the unit sphere is empty and the unit-ball supremum is $0$,
so $\|T\| = 0$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $T:X\to Y$ be
a bounded linear operator, let $r\in Y$ be nonzero, and let
$\sigma\in(0,1)$ and $\gamma>1$. Suppose that a fixed $v\in X$ satisfies
$$\|Tv-r\|_Y\le\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}\|r\|_Y.$$
For each $\alpha>0$, the functional
$$\Phi_\alpha(h):=\frac12\|Th-r\|_Y^2+\frac\alpha2\|h\|_X^2\qquad(h\in X)$$
has the unique global minimizer
$$h_\alpha=(T^*T+\alpha I_X)^{-1}T^*r,$$
where $T^*$ is the Hilbert adjoint and $I_X$ is the identity on $X$. Moreover,
there exists at least one $\alpha>0$ for which
$$\|Th_\alpha-r\|_Y=\sigma\|r\|_Y.$$

derivations.claim: Define $\gamma:=\sigma\tau/[1+ce_0(1+\tau)]$. The bound $e_0<(\sigma\tau-1)/(c(1+\tau))$ gives $1+ce_0(1+\tau)<\sigma\tau$, so $\gamma>1$. Since $e_0=\|x_0-x^\dagger\|_X\ge0$ and $c>0$, the other smallness bound gives $0\le ce_0<(1-\sigma)/2$. Hence $1-ce_0>0$; also $\sigma+ce_0>0$ because $\sigma>0$, and $2ce_0<1-\sigma$ gives $\sigma+ce_0<1-ce_0$. Thus $q=(\sigma+ce_0)/(1-ce_0)$ lies in $(0,1)$.

For each pre-stop index, the given derivative bound and [F8] give $\|F'(x_n^\delta)\|\le M$. Thus [F4] and $\alpha_n\le\sigma M^2/(1-\sigma)$ give $e_n^2-e_{n+1}^2\ge D\,R_n^2,\qquad D:=\frac{2(\gamma-1)\sigma(1-\sigma)}{\gamma M^2}>0,$ where $R_n:=\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y$.

We construct the exact path up to its first crossing by finite induction. Initially $x_0^\delta=x_0\in B_{2r}(x_0)$ and $e_0=\|x_0-x^\dagger\|$. Suppose $x_n^\delta\in B_{2r}(x_0)$ and $e_n:=\|x_n^\delta-x^\dagger\|\le e_0$. If its residual is at most $\tau\delta$, the path stops. Otherwise [F2] with $e=e_0$ gives the range-approximation hypothesis with the $\gamma$ of step 1.1. Since $R_n>\tau\delta>0$, [F9] supplies the positive forcing parameter and unique minimizer. Applying [F4] shows $e_{n+1}\le e_n$ and $\|h_n\|\le e_n$. Hence $e_{n+1}\le e_0$ and $\|x_{n+1}^\delta-x_0\|_X\le\|x_{n+1}^\delta-x^\dagger\|_X+e_0\le2e_0<2r,$ so the next state remains in the local ball and the induction continues.

For $m\ge1$, if no crossing has occurred in the first $m$ updates, then $R_n>\tau\delta$ for $0\le n<m$. Summing step 1.2 telescopes and yields $D m\tau^2\delta^2< D\sum_{n=0}^{m-1}R_n^2\le e_0^2.$ By [F6], choose a natural $m>e_0^2/(D\tau^2\delta^2)$. The displayed inequality is impossible for that $m$, so a crossing occurs at a finite index $N_\delta$. Summing step 1.2 through $N_\delta-1$ also gives $N_\delta\le e_0^2/(D\tau^2\delta^2)$.

Fix $n<N_\delta$ and set $T_n:=F'(x_n^\delta)$, $h_n:=x_{n+1}^\delta-x_n^\delta$, $q_n:=y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)-T_nh_n$, and $\Delta_n:=F(x_{n+1}^\delta)-F(x_n^\delta)-T_nh_n.$ Both iterates lie in $B_{2r}(x_0)$ by step 2.1. Applying [F1] to the ordered pair $(x_n^\delta,x_{n+1}^\delta)$ gives $\|\Delta_n\|_Y\le c\|h_n\|_X\|F(x_{n+1}^\delta)-F(x_n^\delta)\|_Y$. The forcing rule gives $\|q_n\|_Y=\sigma R_n$, while $F(x_{n+1}^\delta)-y^\delta=-q_n+\Delta_n.$ Therefore, with $R_{n+1}:=\|F(x_{n+1}^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y$, $R_{n+1}\le\sigma R_n+c\|h_n\|_X(R_{n+1}+R_n).$ Using $\|h_n\|\le e_n\le e_0$ from [F4] and $1-ce_0>0$ from step 1.1 yields $R_{n+1}\le\frac{\sigma+ce_0}{1-ce_0}R_n=qR_n.$

Let $K:=1+\|F(x_0)-y\|_Y$ and $\delta_0:=\min\{1,K/\tau\}$. By [F7] and the data-noise bound, $R_0\le K$ for $0<\delta\le\delta_0$. If $N_\delta\ge2$, the first-crossing definition gives $\tau\delta<R_{N_\delta-1}$, while repeated application of step 3.2 gives $R_{N_\delta-1}\le q^{N_\delta-1}R_0\le q^{N_\delta-1}K$. Since $\log$ is strictly increasing, $\log(\tau\delta/K)<(N_\delta-1)\log q$; by [F5], $\log q<0$, so division reverses the inequality and gives $N_\delta\le1+\frac{\log(K/(\tau\delta))}{-\log q}.$ The same bound holds for $N_\delta=0$ or $1$, since $\delta\le K/\tau$ makes its right side at least $1$. Finally, for $\delta\le\delta_0\le1$, [F5] gives $\log\frac{K}{\tau\delta}\le\left|\log\frac K\tau\right|+|\log\delta|,$ so, with $C:=1+[1+|\log(K/\tau)|]/(-\log q)$, the displayed bound is at most $C(1+|\log\delta|)$, with $C$ independent of $y^\delta$ and $\delta$. By [F3], a finite run with cap at least $N_\delta$ and successful exact calls returns this crossing. The proof asserts no convergence rate for the stopped iterate.

risk_review.notes: Read all six proof steps and all actual supplier statements, including logarithm monotonicity/quotient law and Archimedean naturals. Smallness gives gamma>1, ce0<(1-sigma)/2, q in (0,1), D>0. Finite induction gives forcing parameters at nonzero pre-stop residuals, e_next<=e<=e0 and ||h||<=e0; distance to x0<=2e0<2r establishes local-ball validity before any next evaluation. Only finite paths are needed: arbitrarily choosing a positive root at each finite stage consumes finite choice, not DC. Fixed finite bound follows by telescoping; corrected missing D on the left-hand side and explicitly m>=1. The old m*tau^2*delta^2 < D sum R_n^2 does not follow when D<1; correct is D*m*tau^2*delta^2 < D sum R_n^2 <= e0^2. Statement and resulting bound unchanged. Product condition at ordered pair (x_n,x_next) bounds the negative of Delta_n with derivative at x_n, giving R_next<=q*R_n. First crossing uses R_(N-1)>tau*delta, handles N=0,1 separately, and division by log(q)<0 reverses direction correctly. K and delta0 bound R0 uniformly; positive delta is essential; e0=0 stops at zero. Read Clason Assumption11.10 and complete Theorem11.11 proof, PDF pp.111–113. No stopped-solution rate or arbitrary inexact-solve promise. No diagram. Nonfatal coefficient typo repaired with confidence1; no Statement, Definition, prerequisites or consumer interface changed.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$
be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable, meaning
that $F$ is Fréchet differentiable at each point of $U$ and

with $F(x^\dagger)=y$ and $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$. At every state

is
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)(x^\dagger-x_n^\delta)+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y.$$

For $x_n^\delta\in U$ and $\alpha>0$, define $h_{n,\alpha}$ to be the unique

$$J_{n,\alpha}(h):=\frac12\|F'(x_n^\delta)h+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y^2+\frac\alpha2\|h\|_X^2.$$
Equivalently, it is the unique solution of
$$\bigl(F'(x_n^\delta)^*F'(x_n^\delta)+\alpha I_X\bigr)h_{n,\alpha}=F'(x_n^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)).$$
Here $I_X$ is the identity operator on $X$.
The forcing rule selects any $\alpha_n>0$ for which

and sets $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_{n,\alpha_n}$. The displayed range
condition is a sufficient condition for the forcing rule to have such a

For a finite run, inspect $n=0,1,\ldots,N_{\max}$ in order. If
$x_n^\delta\notin U$, return $(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{domain-failure})$. If
$\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\tau\delta$, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{discrepancy})$. If $n=N_{\max}$, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{budget-exhausted})$. Otherwise request the exact
regularized minimizer and a positive parameter satisfying the forcing rule.
If the exact minimizer cannot be certified, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{solve-unverified})$; if the parameter selector cannot
return a positive parameter satisfying the displayed equality, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{forcing-unavailable})$. After both exact calls succeed,
set $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_{n,\alpha_n}$ and continue. Each return is a
triple of state, index, and status. No convergence claim is attached to the

This algorithm performs one finite-budget LM trial update. Inputs are $x\in U$, a $C^1$ residual function $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ on open $U$ with $m,n\ge1$ and $J=Dr$, the exact values $r(x)$ and $J(x)$, a fixed nonsingular $D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, an arithmetic mode (exact or computed), a floor $\lambda_{\min}>0$, current damping $\lambda\ge\lambda_{\min}$, factors $\gamma>1$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, a trust radius $\Delta>0$, and an attempt cap $N\ge1$. In computed mode the input values are finite stored numbers treated as the exact data for this update; only arithmetic performed below is rounded. A computed run may include a certificate that the exact scalar product $J(x)^Tr(x)$ is zero. Put $\phi(x)=\|r(x)\|_2^2/2$ and $m_0(p)=\|r(x)+J(x)p\|_2^2/2$. In exact mode the step is the unique minimizer of
$$\tfrac12\|r(x)+J(x)p\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|Dp\|_2^2,$$
which is equivalent to solving
$$(J(x)^TJ(x)+\lambda D^TD)p=-J(x)^Tr(x).$$
In computed mode the returned vector is only a candidate for this same subproblem; no exact minimizer claim is made.


In computed mode use [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Evaluate every dot product by initializing $s=0$ and, for indices in increasing order, computing $u=\operatorname{fl}(a_i b_i)$ followed by $s=\operatorname{fl}(s+u)$. Matrix-vector products and squared norms use this schedule row by row and coordinate by coordinate. Each other scalar arithmetic operation uses $\operatorname{fl}$, with copies and sign changes exact; the first failed operation returns the status assigned to its stage. Function evaluation returns either a finite stored residual vector or failure.

For attempts $j=1,\ldots,N$, do the following with the current damping. After a damping change, construct a new augmented matrix and obtain a report for that actual matrix; do not reuse an earlier damping value's factorization or report.

1. In exact arithmetic, if $J(x)^Tr(x)=0$, return stationary before calling the linear solver. In a computed run, evaluate $J(x)^Tr(x)$ by the stated dot schedule and return stationary before the solve only with the supplied certificate that this exact gradient is zero; if evaluating the product fails, return gradient-evaluation-failure; if the computed product is a rounded zero without that certificate, return gradient-unverified and do not form a ratio. Otherwise perform the augmented construction and linear solve afresh inside this attempt at its current damping: Form $A_\lambda=[J(x);\sqrt\lambda D]$ and $b_\lambda=[r(x);0]$, then call [[alg-gauss-newton-qr-svd-step-with-rank-safeguard]] in QR mode on $(A_\lambda,b_\lambda)$. Exact mode uses the exact positive square root and requires a supplied exact reduced factorization of $A_\lambda$ for each call; absence of that factorization returns linear-solve-failure. This matrix has full column rank because $D$ is nonsingular and $\lambda>0$. In computed mode, copy the stored $J(x)$ and $r(x)$ into the top blocks, compute $t=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt\lambda)$, then fill the bottom block entries $\operatorname{fl}(tD_{ij})$ in increasing row and column order and fill the appended residual entries with exact zeros. Any first arithmetic or range failure in this construction returns linear-solve-failure with its stage and indices. The call receives a computed QR report for this actual stored $A_\lambda$. A computed-candidate is usable only when that report includes the low-level procedure's independently verified full-rank certificate $s_\lambda>0$ for the actual stored matrix, namely $\|A_\lambda v\|_2\ge s_\lambda\|v\|_2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^n$. Pass this bound as the computed report's certificate field; it is not inferred from a nonzero computed diagonal or from positive definiteness of the ideal exact system alone. A rank-unverified report and every other status besides exact-step in exact mode or computed-candidate in computed mode are unusable and return linear-solve-failure with the report. A computed-candidate remains a candidate and carries no convergence guarantee. If the solver status is not exact-step in exact mode or computed-candidate in computed mode, return linear-solve-failure with its report; in particular, rank-unverified is a failure, not a usable trial.
2. If exact mode returns $p=0$ after the nonzero-gradient check, return linear-solve-failure with the inconsistent exact solve report. If computed mode returns $p=0$, return zero-step-unverified and do not compute a ratio. For every remaining candidate $p$ (the zero candidates have already returned a status), compute $\operatorname{pred}=m_0(0)-m_0(p)$. This algorithm performs one finite-budget LM trial update. Inputs are $x\in U$, a $C^1$ residual function $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ on open $U$ with $m,n\ge1$ and $J=Dr$, the exact values $r(x)$ and $J(x)$, a fixed nonsingular $D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, an arithmetic mode (exact or computed), a floor $\lambda_{\min}>0$, current damping $\lambda\ge\lambda_{\min}$, factors $\gamma>1$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, a trust radius $\Delta>0$, and an attempt cap $N\ge1$. In computed mode the input values are finite stored numbers treated as the exact data for this update; only arithmetic performed below is rounded. A computed run may include a certificate that the exact scalar product $J(x)^Tr(x)$ is zero. Put $\phi(x)=\|r(x)\|_2^2/2$ and $m_0(p)=\|r(x)+J(x)p\|_2^2/2$. In exact mode the step is the unique minimizer of
$$\tfrac12\|r(x)+J(x)p\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|Dp\|_2^2,$$
which is equivalent to solving
$$(J(x)^TJ(x)+\lambda D^TD)p=-J(x)^Tr(x).$$
In computed mode the returned vector is only a candidate for this same subproblem; no exact minimizer claim is made.


In computed mode use [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Evaluate every dot product by initializing $s=0$ and, for indices in increasing order, computing $u=\operatorname{fl}(a_i b_i)$ followed by $s=\operatorname{fl}(s+u)$. Matrix-vector products and squared norms use this schedule row by row and coordinate by coordinate. Each other scalar arithmetic operation uses $\operatorname{fl}$, with copies and sign changes exact; the first failed operation returns the status assigned to its stage. Function evaluation returns either a finite stored residual vector or failure.

For attempts $j=1,\ldots,N$, do the following with the current damping. After a damping change, construct a new augmented matrix and obtain a report for that actual matrix; do not reuse an earlier damping value's factorization or report.

1. In exact arithmetic, if $J(x)^Tr(x)=0$, return stationary before calling the linear solver. In a computed run, evaluate $J(x)^Tr(x)$ by the stated dot schedule and return stationary before the solve only with the supplied certificate that this exact gradient is zero; if evaluating the product fails, return gradient-evaluation-failure; if the computed product is a rounded zero without that certificate, return gradient-unverified and do not form a ratio. Exact mode uses the exact positive square root and requires a supplied exact reduced factorization of $A_\lambda$ for each call; absence of that factorization returns linear-solve-failure. This matrix has full column rank because $D$ is nonsingular and $\lambda>0$. In computed mode, copy the stored $J(x)$ and $r(x)$ into the top blocks, compute $t=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt\lambda)$, then fill the bottom block entries $\operatorname{fl}(tD_{ij})$ in increasing row and column order and fill the appended residual entries with exact zeros. A computed-candidate is usable only when that report includes the low-level procedure's independently verified full-rank certificate $s_\lambda>0$ for the actual stored matrix, namely $\|A_\lambda v\|_2\ge s_\lambda\|v\|_2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^n$. Pass this bound as the computed report's certificate field; it is not inferred from a nonzero computed diagonal or from positive definiteness of the ideal exact system alone. A rank-unverified report and every other status besides exact-step in exact mode or computed-candidate in computed mode are unusable and return linear-solve-failure with the report. A computed-candidate remains a candidate and carries no convergence guarantee. If the solver status is not exact-step in exact mode or computed-candidate in computed mode, return linear-solve-failure with its report; in particular, rank-unverified is a failure, not a usable trial.
2. If exact mode returns $p=0$ after the nonzero-gradient check, return linear-solve-failure with the inconsistent exact solve report. If computed mode returns $p=0$, return zero-step-unverified and do not compute a ratio. For every remaining candidate $p$ (the zero candidates have already returned a status), compute $\operatorname{pred}=m_0(0)-m_0(p)$. If that update fails, is nonfinite, or is outside the representable range, return damping-range-failure with the current $x,\lambda$ and the trial report. Otherwise set $\lambda\leftarrow\lambda^+$ and continue.
4. Otherwise evaluate $r(x+p)$ and compute $\operatorname{ared}=\phi(x)-\phi(x+p)$ and $\rho=\operatorname{ared}/\operatorname{pred}$. A failed trial evaluation or nonfinite computed result returns trial-evaluation-failure. If $\rho<\eta_1$, reject and compute $\lambda^+=\gamma\lambda$ in the selected arithmetic. If that damping update fails, is nonfinite, or is outside the representable range, return damping-range-failure with the current $x,\lambda$ and the trial report. Otherwise set $\lambda\leftarrow\lambda^+$. If this was attempt $N$, return rejection-budget-exhausted; otherwise continue.
5. If $\rho\ge\eta_1$, first determine the next damping. If also $\rho\ge\eta_2$ and $\|Dp\|_2=\Delta$, compute $q=\lambda/\gamma$ in exact mode and $q=\operatorname{fl}(\lambda/\gamma)$ in computed mode. Otherwise set $\lambda_{\rm next}=\max\{\lambda_{\min},q\}$. In every other accepted case set $\lambda_{\rm next}=\lambda$. Only after the next damping is available, accept and return $x+p$, $p$, $\rho$, and $\lambda_{\rm next}$.

Let $F$ be a complete ordered field (Complete ordered field (least-upper-bound property)). Then every
$a \in F$ with $a \ge 0$ has a **unique** $s \in F$ with $s \ge 0$ and $s^2 = a$;
we write $s = \sqrt{a}$. Consequently the positive elements of $F$ are exactly the
nonzero squares: $x > 0$ if and only if $x = y^2$ for some $y \neq 0$.

derivations.claim: Completing the square gives $\frac12|\varepsilon h-r|^2+\frac\alpha2|h|^2=\frac{\varepsilon^2+\alpha}{2}\left(h-\frac{\varepsilon r}{\varepsilon^2+\alpha}\right)^2+\frac{r^2}{2}-\frac{\varepsilon^2r^2}{2(\varepsilon^2+\alpha)}.$ Since $\varepsilon^2+\alpha>0$, the unique minimizer is $h_\alpha=\varepsilon r/(\varepsilon^2+\alpha)$.

By [F4], $2\varepsilon\sqrt\alpha\le\varepsilon^2+\alpha$, so $|h_\alpha|=\varepsilon r/(\varepsilon^2+\alpha)\le r/(2\sqrt\alpha)\le\delta/(2\sqrt\alpha)$, with a bound independent of $\varepsilon$. The unregularized linearized equation $\varepsilon h_0=r$ instead gives $|h_0|=r/\varepsilon\le\delta/\varepsilon$, which is unbounded as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ for fixed $r>0$.

The linearized residual after the regularized step is $\varepsilon h_\alpha-r=-\alpha r/(\varepsilon^2+\alpha)$. Since $r>0$, the residual-forcing equality is equivalent to $\alpha/(\varepsilon^2+\alpha)=\sigma$, hence $\alpha=\sigma\varepsilon^2/(1-\sigma)$ and $h_\alpha=(1-\sigma)r/\varepsilon$. This forcing-selected step grows like $1/\varepsilon$ when $r$ is held fixed; the fixed-$\alpha$ bound above does not give a uniform bound for this varying-parameter family.

For the finite safeguarded procedure, the augmented matrix is the column $A=(\varepsilon,\sqrt\alpha)^T$. Put $s:=\sqrt{\varepsilon^2+\alpha}$, $Q:=A/s$, and $R:=(s)$. Then $s>0$, $Q^TQ=1$, and $QR=A$, so $A=QR$ is an exact reduced QR factorization. Its augmented residual vector is $b=(-r,0)^T$, and the exact damped least-squares minimizer is the same $p=h_\alpha$ from step 1.1.

Take residual map $g(t)=\varepsilon t-y^\delta$, Jacobian $J=\varepsilon$, $D=1$, current damping $\lambda=\alpha$, a floor $0<\lambda_{\min}\le\alpha$, factors $\gamma=2$, $\eta_1=1/4$, $\eta_2=3/4$, trust radius $\Delta>|h_\alpha|$, and one allowed attempt. The exact gradient is nonzero since $J^Tg(x)=-\varepsilon r\ne0$. The model residual equals the actual residual because $g$ is affine. The predicted reduction is positive because $|\varepsilon h_\alpha-r|=\alpha r/(\varepsilon^2+\alpha)<r$, so the actual-to-predicted ratio is $1$. The trial lies inside the trust radius, hence it is accepted and does not meet the boundary condition for lowering damping; it returns the same damping $\lambda=\alpha$.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$
be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable, meaning
that $F$ is Fréchet differentiable at each point of $U$ and
$x\mapsto F'(x)$ is continuous in operator norm. The input consists of an
initial point $x_0\in U$, a datum $y^\delta\in Y$, a positive noise bound
$\delta>0$, a discrepancy factor $\tau>1$, a forcing fraction $\sigma\in(0,1)$,
a range-approximation margin $\gamma>1$, and a finite update budget
$N_{\max}\in\mathbb N_0:=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. Assume an exact solution $x^\dagger\in U$ exists
with $F(x^\dagger)=y$ and $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$. At every state
$x_n^\delta$ before the discrepancy stop, the admissible local range condition
is
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)(x^\dagger-x_n^\delta)+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y.$$

For $x_n^\delta\in U$ and $\alpha>0$, define $h_{n,\alpha}$ to be the unique
global minimizer over $h\in X$ of the regularized linearized least-squares
objective
$$J_{n,\alpha}(h):=\frac12\|F'(x_n^\delta)h+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y^2+\frac\alpha2\|h\|_X^2.$$
Equivalently, it is the unique solution of
$$\bigl(F'(x_n^\delta)^*F'(x_n^\delta)+\alpha I_X\bigr)h_{n,\alpha}=F'(x_n^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)).$$
Here $I_X$ is the identity operator on $X$.
The forcing rule selects any $\alpha_n>0$ for which
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)h_{n,\alpha_n}+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y=\sigma\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y,$$
and sets $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_{n,\alpha_n}$. The displayed range
condition is a sufficient condition for the forcing rule to have such a
parameter; it is not an input to either linearized minimization problem.

For a finite run, inspect $n=0,1,\ldots,N_{\max}$ in order. If
$x_n^\delta\notin U$, return $(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{domain-failure})$. If
$\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\tau\delta$, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{discrepancy})$. If $n=N_{\max}$, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{budget-exhausted})$. Otherwise request the exact
regularized minimizer and a positive parameter satisfying the forcing rule.
If the exact minimizer cannot be certified, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{solve-unverified})$; if the parameter selector cannot
return a positive parameter satisfying the displayed equality, return
$(x_n^\delta,n,\texttt{forcing-unavailable})$. After both exact calls succeed,
set $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_{n,\alpha_n}$ and continue. Each return is a
triple of state, index, and status. No convergence claim is attached to the
failure statuses or to a budget-exhausted state.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$
be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable everywhere with
$x\mapsto F'(x)$ continuous in operator norm. For $s>0$, write
$$B_s(x_0):=\{x\in X:\|x-x_0\|_X<s\}.$$
Suppose $B_{2r}(x_0)\subseteq U$ for some $r>0$, $x^\dagger\in B_r(x_0)$,
and $F(x^\dagger)=y$. Assume there are constants $M,c>0$ such that, for every
$x,\tilde x\in B_{2r}(x_0)$,
$$\|F'(x)\|\le M,$$
$$\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)-F'(x)(x-\tilde x)\|_Y\le c\|x-\tilde x\|_X\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)\|_Y.$$
Fix $\sigma\in(0,1)$ and $\tau>1/\sigma$. Put
$$e_0:=\|x_0-x^\dagger\|_X$$
and assume
$$e_0<\min\left\{r,\frac{\sigma\tau-1}{c(1+\tau)},\frac{1-\sigma}{2c}\right\}.$$
Set
$$\gamma:=\frac{\sigma\tau}{1+ce_0(1+\tau)};$$
the hypotheses give $\gamma>1$. For each exact iteration, use this $\gamma$ in
the range-approximation margin of the regularized LM procedure and select any
positive parameter satisfying its residual-forcing equality.
For every $\delta>0$ and $y^\delta\in Y$ satisfying
$\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, start at $x_0^\delta=x_0$ and, at each state
before stopping, let $h_n$ minimize
$$h\longmapsto\frac12\|F'(x_n^\delta)h+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y^2+\frac{\alpha_n}{2}\|h\|_X^2$$
for a selected $\alpha_n>0$ satisfying
$$\|F'(x_n^\delta)h_n+F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y=\sigma\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y,$$
and set $x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+h_n$. Let $N_\delta$ be the first
$n\in\mathbb N_0:=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ such that
$$\|F(x_n^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y\le\tau\delta.$$
Then this exact iteration is well-defined up to a finite first discrepancy
index $N_\delta$. Set
$$q:=\frac{\sigma+ce_0}{1-ce_0},\qquad K:=1+\|F(x_0)-y\|_Y,\qquad \delta_0:=\min\left\{1,\frac K\tau\right\}.$$
Here $q\in(0,1)$ and $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm. For
$0<\delta\le\delta_0$,
$$N_\delta\le1+\frac{\log(K/(\tau\delta))}{-\log q}.$$
Consequently $N_\delta=O(1+|\log\delta|)$ as $\delta\downarrow0$, with
constants depending only on the fixed problem and displayed parameters. A
finite run with update budget at least $N_\delta$ and successful exact calls
returns this first crossing; a shorter budget may return
`budget-exhausted`. No convergence rate for $x_{N_\delta}^\delta$ is asserted.

Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let
$F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable, meaning that $F$ is
Fréchet differentiable at each point of $U$ and $x\mapsto F'(x)$ is continuous
in operator norm. For a subset $V\subseteq U$ and a constant $c>0$, the
**product-type tangential cone condition on $V$ with constant $c$** is the
requirement that, for every $x,\tilde x\in V$,

$$\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)-F'(x)(x-\tilde x)\|_Y\le c\|x-\tilde x\|_X\|F(x)-F(\tilde x)\|_Y.$$

derivations.claim: The derivative of $F(t)=t$ is $F'(t)=1$, so $F(u)-F(\tilde u)-F'(u)(u-\tilde u)=0$ for every $u,\tilde u\in\mathbb R$. Thus the product condition holds on $B_2(x_0)\subset\mathbb R$ with $c=1$, and $|F'(t)|=1=M$. The exact solution lies in $B_1(x_0)$ and $B_2(x_0)\subset U$. Also $e_0=|x_0-x^\dagger|=1/16<1$, while $\frac{\sigma\tau-1}{c(1+\tau)}=\frac18,\qquad\frac{1-\sigma}{2c}=\frac14,$ so the theorem's local smallness clauses hold. Its positive-noise clause does not hold because $\delta=0$.

Let $r_n:=1-x_n$. If $r_n>0$, the objective is $\frac12(h-r_n)^2+\frac{\alpha_n}{2}h^2$. Completing the square gives the unique minimizer $h_n=r_n/(1+\alpha_n)$ and $r_n-h_n=\alpha_n r_n/(1+\alpha_n)$. The forcing equation with $\sigma=1/2$ therefore requires $\alpha_n=1$ and gives $h_n=r_n/2$.

Since $x_0=1-1/16$, $r_0=1/16>0$. Whenever $r_n>0$, step 1.2 gives $r_{n+1}=1-x_{n+1}=r_n-h_n=r_n/2$. By induction, $r_n=2^{-n}/16>0$ for every finite $n$. Therefore $|F(x_n)-y^\delta|=r_n>0=\tau\delta$ at every finite index, so no discrepancy crossing occurs. This refutes the stated finite-stopping extension to zero noise.

Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be nonempty, let $x_0\in U$, and let $F:U\to Y$ be a map. A **differential range-invariance factorization at $x_0$ on $U$** consists of a bounded linear map $K:Z\to Y$ and a map $r:U\to Z$ such that

$$F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)\qquad(x\in U).$$

Thus every data increment lies in the range of the fixed operator $K$. The factorization alone does not assert that $K$ is injective, that $r$ is unique, or that a tangential-cone inequality holds. If $U$ is open and $F$ and $r$ are Fréchet differentiable, differentiating this identity gives $F'(x)=Kr'(x)$ at every $x\in U$; no converse is asserted without further hypotheses.

Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at $x\in U$. For $\delta>0$ such that the closed ball

$$\overline B_\delta(x):=\{x+h:h\in X,\ \|h\|_X\le\delta\}$$

is contained in $U$, the **local tangential cone condition at $x$ on radius $\delta$ with constant $\eta$** holds if $0\le\eta<1$ and

$$\|F(x+h)-F(x)-F'(x)h\|_Y\le\eta\,\|F(x+h)-F(x)\|_Y\qquad(\|h\|_X\le\delta).$$

$$F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)\qquad(x\in U).$$

If $U$ is open and $F$ and $r$ are Fréchet differentiable, differentiating this identity gives $F'(x)=Kr'(x)$ at every $x\in U$; no converse is asserted without further hypotheses.

Let $X,Y,Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $X_0$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$, and let $D\subseteq X$ contain $X_0$ and a nonempty set $U$. Fix $x_0\in X_0\cap U$, a map $F:D\to Y$, a bounded linear map $K:Z\to Y$, and a map $r:D\to Z$ such that $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ for every $x\in D$. Assume that $r|_U$ is a bijection from $U$ onto a set $\widetilde U\subseteq Z$, and that $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)\in X_0\cap D$ for every $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$ admitted below. Here $I$ is the identity on $X$ and $P:X\to X$ is a bounded linear projection with $P^2=P$, $P|_{X_0}=0$, and $(I-P)(X)\subseteq X_0$. Let $\check R:X_0\to[0,+\infty]$ be a proper convex regularizer, let $R_P:P(X)\to[0,+\infty]$ be a nonnegative penalty, and let $Q:Z\times Z\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfy $Q(a,b)=Q(b,a)$ and $Q(a,b)=0$ exactly when $a=b$. For $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$, set

$$\mathcal R(\widehat r):=\check R\big((I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)\big)+R_P\big(Pr^{-1}(\widehat r)\big).$$

For $p\in[1,\infty)$, data $y^\delta\in Y$, and parameters $\alpha,\beta>0$, the **joint relaxed objective** is

$$\mathcal J_{\alpha,\beta}^\delta(\widehat r,x):=\|K\widehat r+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y^p+\alpha\mathcal R(\widehat r)+\beta Q(r(x),\widehat r)^p+\|Px\|_X^p,\qquad (\widehat r,x)\in\widetilde U\times U.$$

The joint source-condition objective takes $R_P=0$. The term $\beta Q(r(x),\widehat r)^p$ ties the relaxed range variable to the physical variable, while $\|Px\|_X^p$ penalizes the component outside $X_0$.

If $r$ is Gâteaux differentiable at a current iterate $x_n\in U$, the **frozen-Newton objective** with parameters $\alpha_n,\beta_n>0$ is

$$\mathcal J_n^\delta(\widehat r,x):=\|K\widehat r+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y^p+\alpha_n\mathcal R(\widehat r)+\beta_n Q\big(r(x_n)+r'(x_n)(x-x_n),\widehat r\big)^p+\|Px\|_X^p.$$

Here $r'(x_n)$ is the bounded linear Gâteaux derivative used to form the affine range proxy; no minimizer existence or uniqueness is part of either definition.

Let $X$ be a real Banach space and let $X^*$ be its continuous real dual. The dual pairing is evaluation, written $\langle \xi,x\rangle_{X^*,X}:=\xi(x)$ for $\xi\in X^*$ and $x\in X$. Let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be a proper convex functional: $R$ never takes the value $-\infty$, its effective domain $\operatorname{dom}R:=\{x\in X:R(x)<+\infty\}$ is nonempty, and $R((1-t)x+tz)\le (1-t)R(x)+tR(z)$ for $x,z\in X$ and $t\in[0,1]$, with $0\cdot(+\infty):=0$ for this convex-combination formula. For $x\in\operatorname{dom}R$, its subdifferential is

$$\partial R(x):=\{\xi\in X^*:R(z)\ge R(x)+\langle\xi,z-x\rangle_{X^*,X}\text{ for every }z\in X\}.$$

An element of $\partial R(x)$ is a subgradient of $R$ at $x$. Set $\partial R(x):=\varnothing$ when $x\notin\operatorname{dom}R$. The subdifferential may be empty at a point of $\operatorname{dom}R$; no nonemptiness assertion is part of this definition.

Let $X$ be a real Banach space, let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, choose $x^\dagger\in\operatorname{dom}R$, and choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$. For $x\in\operatorname{dom}R$, the **Bregman distance** generated by $\xi^\dagger$ from the reference point $x^\dagger$ to $x$ is

$$D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger):=R(x)-R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}.$$

The subgradient inequality makes this quantity nonnegative, and $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x^\dagger,x^\dagger)=0$. The definition fixes the orientation: the first argument is the comparison point and the second is the reference point carrying the chosen subgradient.

Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, let $F:D(F)\subseteq X\to Y$, let $x^\dagger\in D(F)$ with exact datum $y=F(x^\dagger)$, and let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex with $x^\dagger\in\operatorname{dom}R$. Fix $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$, an exponent $1\le p<\infty$, a continuous nondecreasing concave function $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $\psi(0)=0$ and $\psi(t)>0$ for $t>0$, a coefficient $0\le\beta<1$, and a level $R_0\ge R(x^\dagger)$. The **variational source condition** with these data holds on the named regularizer sublevel $L_{R_0}:=\{x\in D(F):R(x)\le R_0\}$ when

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}\le\beta D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)+\psi\!\left(\|F(x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\right)\qquad(x\in L_{R_0}).$$

The condition is an assumption on the selected subgradient and the stated sublevel; it makes no assertion that a subgradient exists at every point or that a regularized minimizer exists.

derivations.claim: Compare the approximate-minimum inequality with $(\widehat r,x)=(r(x^\dagger),x^\dagger)$. By [F1], $Kr(x^\dagger)+F(x_0)=F(x^\dagger)=y$, while $Q(r(x^\dagger),r(x^\dagger))=0$ and $Px^\dagger=0$. Since $r^{-1}(r(x^\dagger))=x^\dagger$ and $P(x^\dagger)=0$, the comparison regularizer is $\check R(x^\dagger)$, so its objective is at most $\delta^p+\alpha\check R(x^\dagger)$. Writing the estimated data residual as $K(\widehat r_\delta-r(x^\dagger))+(y-y^\delta)$, the triangle inequality gives $\|K(\widehat r_\delta-r(x^\dagger))\|\le\|K\widehat r_\delta+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|+\delta$. For $p=1$ the power inequality is equality; for $p>1$, $f(t)=t^p$ has $f\prime\prime(t)=p(p-1)t^{p-2}\ge0$ for $t>0$ and is continuous at zero, so it is convex on $[0,\infty)$; midpoint convexity gives $(a+b)^p\le2^{p-1}(a^p+b^p)$ for $a,b\ge0$. Rearranging yields $2^{1-p}\|K(\widehat r_\delta-r(x^\dagger))\|^p\le\|K\widehat r_\delta+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|^p+\delta^p$. Combining this with the comparison and $\eta_\delta\le C_\eta\delta^p$ gives $s_\delta+\alpha(\check R(\check x_\delta)-\check R(x^\dagger))\le d_\delta$.

By [F3], $\xi^\dagger$ is a subgradient at $x^\dagger$, and [F4] gives $\check R(\check x_\delta)-\check R(x^\dagger)=e_\delta+\langle\xi^\dagger,\check x_\delta-x^\dagger\rangle$. The VSC [F5] therefore implies $\check R(\check x_\delta)-\check R(x^\dagger)\ge(1-b)e_\delta-\psi(\|F(\check x_\delta)-F(x^\dagger)\|^p)$. Substituting this lower bound in step 1.1 yields $s_\delta+(1-b)\alpha e_\delta\le d_\delta+\alpha\psi(\|F(\check x_\delta)-F(x^\dagger)\|^p)$.

Put $u_\delta=r^{-1}(\widehat r_\delta)$, so $\check x_\delta=(I-P)u_\delta$. Since $r^{-1}(r(x_\delta))=x_\delta$, assumption [A3] and the triangle inequality give $\|Pu_\delta\|\le\|Px_\delta\|+C_QQ(r(x_\delta),\widehat r_\delta)$. Lipschitz continuity of $r$ gives $\|r(\check x_\delta)-\widehat r_\delta\|=\|r((I-P)u_\delta)-r(u_\delta)\|\le L_r\|Pu_\delta\|$. Applying [F1] at $\check x_\delta$ and $x^\dagger$, then applying $(a+b)^p\le2^{p-1}(a^p+b^p)$ twice, yields $\|F(\check x_\delta)-F(x^\dagger)\|^p\le2^{p-1}\|K(\widehat r_\delta-r(x^\dagger))\|^p+2^{2p-2}\|K\|^pL_r^p(\|Px_\delta\|^p+C_Q^pQ(r(x_\delta),\widehat r_\delta)^p)\le C_*s_\delta$. Monotonicity of $\psi$ gives $\psi(\|F(\check x_\delta)-F(x^\dagger)\|^p)\le\psi(C_*s_\delta)$.
Substitute the last bound from step 2.2 into the inequality from step 2.1. This gives $s_\delta+(1-b)\alpha e_\delta\le d_\delta+\alpha\psi(C_*s_\delta)$, as claimed.

Applying the same power inequality to $\|r(x_{n+1})-r^\dagger\|\le A+\|\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger\|$ gives $A^p\ge2^{1-p}\|r(x_{n+1})-r^\dagger\|^p-\|\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger\|^p$. Therefore $\|\ell_n(x_{n+1})-\widehat r_{n+1}\|^p\ge t\|r(x_{n+1})-r^\dagger\|^p-\lambda\|\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger\|^p-2^{p-1}c_{\rm tcr}^p\|r(x_n)-r^\dagger\|^p$, with $t=2^{2-2p}-2^{p-1}c_{\rm tcr}^p$ and $\lambda=2^{1-p}$.

Set $z:=Pu$. Since $\|r(\check x)-r(u)\|\le L_r\|z\|$, the factorization and power inequality give $\|F(\check x)-F(x^\dagger)\|^p\le2^{p-1}\|K(\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger)\|^p+2^{p-1}\|K\|^pL_r^p\|z\|^p$. By the VSC [F5], the Bregman identity [F4], the penalty lower bound, and $\psi(a+b)\le C_\psi(\psi(a)+\psi(b))$, we obtain $\mathcal R(\widehat r_{n+1})-\check R(x^\dagger)\ge m(D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x,x^\dagger)+\psi(C_P\|z\|^p))-C_\psi\psi(2^{p-1}\|K(\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger)\|^p)$. Indeed, the VSC yields coefficient $1-b$ on the Bregman term, and the penalty leaves coefficient $\gamma-C_\psi$ on the penalty-index term; their minimum is $m$.

Substituting steps 1.1–1.3 into the objective comparison and applying the compatibility inequality gives $C_\psi S_{n+1}+\alpha_nmT+\beta_nt\|r(x_{n+1})-r^\dagger\|^p\le\beta_nv\|r(x_n)-r^\dagger\|^p+\beta_n\lambda\|\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger\|^p+\alpha_nC_\psi\psi(2^{p-1}\|K(\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger)\|^p)+2\delta^p+\eta_n$, where $T:=D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x,x^\dagger)+\psi(C_P\|Pu\|^p)$. By [F3], $D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x,x^\dagger)\ge0$, so $T\ge0$. Since $\|\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger\|^p\le\widetilde C_QT$ and $\beta_n\lambda\widetilde C_Q\le\alpha_nm/4$, the left regularizer term absorbs the displayed compatibility term and a second copy of it, leaving $\alpha_nmT/2$; in particular it bounds another $\beta_n\lambda\|\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger\|^p$. The resulting inequality is $C_\psi S_{n+1}+\beta_n\lambda\|\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger\|^p+\beta_nt\|r(x_{n+1})-r^\dagger\|^p\le\beta_nv\|r(x_n)-r^\dagger\|^p+\alpha_nC_\psi\psi(2^{p-1}\|K(\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger)\|^p)+2\delta^p+\eta_n$.

Divide step 2.1 by $C_\psi$ and use $\beta_n=c_{\beta\alpha}\alpha_n$. Since $C_\psi S_{n+1}\ge2^{1-p}\|K(\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger)\|^p$, we have $2^{p-1}\|K(\widehat r_{n+1}-r^\dagger)\|^p\le C_\psi2^{2p-2}S_{n+1}=\overline C S_{n+1}$. Monotonicity of $\psi$ gives $S_{n+1}+\alpha_nE_{n+1}\le d_n+\alpha_n\psi(\overline C S_{n+1})$. Applying [F6] with $c_1=c_2=1$, $C_3=\overline C$, $r=S_{n+1}$, and $e=E_{n+1}$ proves both conjugate bounds.

Let $1\le p<\infty$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be real Banach spaces, $X_0\subseteq X$ a closed linear subspace, $D\subseteq X$ a domain containing $X_0$ and $U$, and $x_0\in U\cap X_0$. Let $F:D\to Y$, $K\in\mathcal L(Z,Y)$, and $r:D\to Z$ satisfy $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ on $D$, with $r|_U:U\to\widetilde U$ bijective and $r$ Lipschitz with constant $L_r$ on $D$. Let $P:X\to X$ be a bounded linear projection such that $P|_{X_0}=0$, $(I-P)(X)\subseteq X_0$, and $P(x_0)=P(x^\dagger)=0$ for an exact solution $x^\dagger\in U\cap X_0$; put $y:=F(x^\dagger)$. Assume the projected points $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)$ belong to $D\cap X_0$ for all admitted $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$.

Let $\check R:X_0\to[0,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial\check R(x^\dagger)\subseteq X_0^*$, and suppose that for some $R_0\ge\check R(x^\dagger)$, $b\in[0,1)$, and continuous nondecreasing concave $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $\psi(0)=0$, the variational source inequality

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,\check x-x^\dagger\rangle\le bD_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x,x^\dagger)+\psi\big(\|F(\check x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\big)$$

holds whenever $\check x\in D\cap X_0$ and $\check R(\check x)\le R_0$, where $D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x,x^\dagger):=\check R(\check x)-\check R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,\check x-x^\dagger\rangle$. Set $R_P=0$ in the joint objective. Let $Q:\widetilde U\times\widetilde U\to[0,\infty]$ satisfy $Q(a,b)=Q(b,a)$ and $Q(a,b)=0$ exactly when $a=b$, and assume there is a constant $C_Q\ge0$ such that

$$\|P(r^{-1}(a))-P(r^{-1}(b))\|_X\le C_Q Q(a,b)\qquad(a,b\in\widetilde U).$$

For $\delta>0$, let $y^\delta\in Y$ satisfy $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$. Let $\alpha,\beta>0$, $C_\eta\ge0$, and let $(\widehat r_\delta,x_\delta)\in\widetilde U\times U$ be an $\eta_\delta$-minimizer of the joint objective, meaning

$$\mathcal J_{\alpha,\beta}^\delta(\widehat r_\delta,x_\delta)\le\mathcal J_{\alpha,\beta}^\delta(\widehat r,x)+\eta_\delta\qquad((\widehat r,x)\in\widetilde U\times U),\qquad 0\le\eta_\delta\le C_\eta\delta^p.$$

Assume $\check x_\delta:=(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r_\delta)$ lies in the stated VSC sublevel. Define

$$s_\delta:=2^{1-p}\|K(\widehat r_\delta-r(x^\dagger))\|_Y^p+\beta Q(r(x_\delta),\widehat r_\delta)^p+\|Px_\delta\|_X^p,\qquad e_\delta:=D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x_\delta,x^\dagger),$$

and

$$C_*:=2^{2p-2}\max\left\{1,\|K\|^pL_r^p,\frac{\|K\|^pL_r^pC_Q^p}{\beta}\right\},\qquad d_\delta:=(2+C_\eta)\delta^p.$$

Then

$$s_\delta+(1-b)\alpha e_\delta\le d_\delta+\alpha\psi(C_*s_\delta).$$

Let $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous, nondecreasing, concave, and satisfy $\psi(0)=0$. Extend $g=-\psi$ to $\mathbb R$ by $g(s)=+\infty$ for $s<0$, and define $H(q):=g^*(-q)=\sup_{s\ge0}(\psi(s)-qs)$ for $q>0$, assuming the displayed suprema below are finite. For $c_1,c_2,C_3,\alpha>0$ and $d,r,e\ge0$, if

$$c_1r+c_2\alpha e\le d+\alpha\psi(C_3r),$$

then

$$e\le\frac1{c_2}\left(\frac d\alpha+H\!\left(\frac{c_1}{C_3\alpha}\right)\right),\qquad r\le\frac2{c_1}\left(d+\alpha H\!\left(\frac{c_1}{2C_3\alpha}\right)\right).$$

Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be nonempty, let $x_0\in U$, and let $F:U\to Y$ be a map. A **differential range-invariance factorization at $x_0$ on $U$** consists of a bounded linear map $K:Z\to Y$ and a map $r:U\to Z$ such that

$$F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)\qquad(x\in U).$$

Thus every data increment lies in the range of the fixed operator $K$. The factorization alone does not assert that $K$ is injective, that $r$ is unique, or that a tangential-cone inequality holds. If $U$ is open and $F$ and $r$ are Fréchet differentiable, differentiating this identity gives $F'(x)=Kr'(x)$ at every $x\in U$; no converse is asserted without further hypotheses.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1\subset\mathbb R^3$, $0<\rho<1$, $0<m<1<M$, and $5/2<s_1<7/2$. Use the exact intrinsic $H^{s_1}(\Omega)$ Hilbert norm from the collared source-functional lemma, and put
$$V=\{a\in H^{s_1}(\Omega;\mathbb R):a=0\text{ a.e. on }\Omega\setminus B_\rho\},\qquad \mathcal C=\{\sigma\in1+V:m\le\sigma\le M\}.$$
Let $\sigma_0,\sigma^\dagger\in\mathcal C$, and assume $\sigma^\dagger\in B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ for $s_1<s_2<2s_1-1$. Set $a^\dagger=\sigma^\dagger-\sigma_0$, and choose $R>\|a^\dagger\|_V$. Write $Y=\ell^2(L^2(S^2;\mathbb C))$ for the centered mean-zero Neumann voltage sequence space, regarded as a real Hilbert space, and give $X=Z=V\times Y$ the sum norm. Let $X_0=V\times\{0\}$, $D=X$, $x_0=(0,0)$ and $P(a,z)=(0,z)$.

There is a globally Lipschitz, continuously Fréchet differentiable map $\Gamma:V\to Y$ with globally Lipschitz derivative, agreeing for $\sigma_0+a\in\mathcal C$ with the centered physical observation $((\mathscr N_{\sigma_0+a}-\mathscr N_1)Y_{\ell k})_{\ell,k}$. Define
$$T(a)=\Gamma(a)-\Gamma(0)-\Gamma'(0)a,\quad r(a,z)=(a,z+T(a)),\quad K(a,b)=\Gamma'(0)a+b,\quad F(a,z)=\Gamma(a)+z.$$
Then $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ on $D$, $r$ and its inverse $r^{-1}(a,b)=(a,b-T(a))$ are globally Lipschitz, and these facts hold on the admitted set
$$U=\{(a,z):\sigma_0+a\in\mathcal C,\ \|a\|_V<R,\ \|z\|_Y<R\}.$$
The projected points $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)$ belong to $U\cap X_0$ for $\widehat r\in r(U)$.

On the ambient linear space $V$ define the proper convex regularizer
$$\check R(a)=\tfrac12\|\sigma_0+a\|_{s_1,\Omega}^2+I_{\mathcal C}(\sigma_0+a),$$
where the indicator is zero on $\mathcal C$ and $+\infty$ elsewhere. On every admitted physical coefficient this is exactly the original quadratic Sobolev penalty. The functional $\xi^\dagger(v)=(\sigma^\dagger,v)_{s_1,\Omega}$ is a subgradient at $a^\dagger$, and its Bregman distance on $\mathcal C-\sigma_0$ is exactly $\frac12\|a-a^\dagger\|_V^2$. On every fixed sublevel containing the truth, the VSC holds with $b=3/4$ and a continuous nondecreasing concave truncated logarithmic index
$$\psi(u)=C[\log(1/u)]^{-\nu}\quad(0<u\le u_0),\qquad \psi(0)=0,\qquad \nu=\frac{(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)}{s_2-1},$$
continued constantly above a sufficiently small $u_0>0$. Its subadditivity constant may be taken as $C_\psi=1$.

Put $L_T=\operatorname{Lip}(T)$ and let $L=\operatorname{Lip}(\Gamma')$. For $Q(\widehat r,\widehat r')=\|\widehat r-\widehat r'\|_Z$, the projection-coupling constant may be taken as $1+L_T$, and
$$\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)-r'(x_2)(x_1-x_2)\|_Z\le LR\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)\|_Z\qquad(x_1,x_2\in U).$$
For the frozen method choose $C_P\ge2\|K\|^2\operatorname{Lip}(r)^2$, $\gamma>1$ and $R_P(z)=\gamma\psi(C_P\|z\|_Y^2)$. Then the required compatibility bound holds with
$$\widetilde C_Q=\max\left\{4(1+L_T)^2,\frac{2R^2}{\psi(C_PR^2)}\right\}.$$
In particular, the structural hypotheses of the joint and frozen one-step estimates hold with $p=2$, the displayed exact regularizer, $R_P=0$ for the joint method, and the displayed $R_P$ for the frozen method. For frozen rates additionally require $LR<c_{\rm tcr}<1/\sqrt{20}$, choose $c_{\beta\alpha}\le\min\{1/4,\gamma-1\}/(4\widetilde C_Q)$, and use the remaining parameter, tolerance and stopping conditions of the frozen rate theorem. This small-neighborhood hypothesis is local around the chosen initial conductivity; it restricts neither the stated Besov truth class nor its logarithmic exponent.

Let $1\le p<\infty$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $X_0$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$, and let $D,U\subseteq X$. Let $x_0,x^\dagger\in D\cap U\cap X_0$, let $F:D\to Y$, $K\in\mathcal L(Z,Y)$, and $r:D\to Z$ satisfy $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ for all $x\in D$. Assume $r|_U:U\to\widetilde U$ is a bijection, $r$ is Lipschitz on $D$ with constant $L_r$, and $r$ has bounded linear Gâteaux derivatives on $U$. Let $P:X\to X$ be a bounded linear projection with $P^2=P$, $P|_{X_0}=0$, and $(I-P)(X)\subseteq X_0$. Assume $P(x^\dagger)=0$ and $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)\in D\cap X_0$ for each admitted $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$.

Let $\check R:X_0\to[0,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial\check R(x^\dagger)$, and write

$$D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(z,x^\dagger):=\check R(z)-\check R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,z-x^\dagger\rangle_{X_0^*,X_0}.$$

Suppose that, on the stated sublevel $\check R(z)\le R_0$, the variational source inequality

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,z-x^\dagger\rangle_{X_0^*,X_0}\le bD_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(z,x^\dagger)+\psi\!\left(\|F(z)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\right)$$

holds for some $R_0\ge\check R(x^\dagger)$ and $0\le b<1$. Assume that $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous, nondecreasing and concave, with $\psi(0)=0$, and that for a constant $C_\psi>0$,

$$\psi(a+b)\le C_\psi\bigl(\psi(a)+\psi(b)\bigr)\qquad(a,b\ge0).$$

Let $H(q):=\sup_{s\ge0}(\psi(s)-qs)$, and assume the values of $H$ used below are finite. Let $\gamma>C_\psi$, $C_P\ge2^{p-1}\|K\|^pL_r^p$, and $\widetilde C_Q>0$. Let $R_P:P(X)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfy $R_P(0)=0$ and

$$R_P(z)\ge\gamma\psi(C_P\|z\|_X^p)\qquad(z\in P(X)).$$

For each admitted $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$, put $u(\widehat r):=r^{-1}(\widehat r)$ and $\check x(\widehat r):=(I-P)u(\widehat r)$. Assume the compatibility bound

$$\|\widehat r-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p\le\widetilde C_Q\left(D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x(\widehat r),x^\dagger)+\psi(C_P\|Pu(\widehat r)\|_X^p)\right).$$

Choose $c_{\beta\alpha}>0$ with $c_{\beta\alpha}\le\min\{1-b,\gamma-C_\psi\}/(4\widetilde C_Q)$, and set

$$m:=\min\{1-b,\gamma-C_\psi\},\quad a:=2^{1-p},\quad \lambda:=2^{1-p},\quad t:=2^{2-2p}-2^{p-1}c_{\rm tcr}^p,\quad v:=(1+2^{p-1})c_{\rm tcr}^p,\quad \overline C:=C_\psi 2^{2p-2}.$$

Assume $0<c_{\rm tcr}<1$ and $t>0$, and for all $x_1,x_2\in U$ assume

$$\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)-r'(x_2)(x_1-x_2)\|_Z\le c_{\rm tcr}\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)\|_Z.$$

Assume the candidate projected point satisfies $\check R(\check x(\widehat r_{n+1}))\le R_0$.

Let $Q(a,b):=\|a-b\|_Z$. Fix $\delta>0$, $y^\delta\in Y$ with $\|y^\delta-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y\le\delta$, and $\alpha_n>0$, with $\beta_n:=c_{\beta\alpha}\alpha_n$. Suppose $(\widehat r_{n+1},x_{n+1})\in\widetilde U\times U$ satisfies, for some $\eta_n\ge0$,

Let $X$ be a real Banach space, let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, choose $x^\dagger\in\operatorname{dom}R$, and choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$. For $x\in\operatorname{dom}R$, the **Bregman distance** generated by $\xi^\dagger$ from the reference point $x^\dagger$ to $x$ is

$$D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger):=R(x)-R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}.$$

The subgradient inequality makes this quantity nonnegative, and $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x^\dagger,x^\dagger)=0$. The definition fixes the orientation: the first argument is the comparison point and the second is the reference point carrying the chosen subgradient.

Assume the hypotheses of the joint range-invariance VSC estimate lemma, with the same notation, with fixed $\beta>0$, and with $R_P=0$ in the joint objective. Define

$$H(q):=\sup_{s\ge0}\bigl(\psi(s)-qs\bigr)\qquad(q>0),\quad \rho_\delta:=H\!\left(\frac{1}{C_*\alpha(\delta)}\right).$$

$$c_-\delta^p\le\alpha(\delta)\rho_\delta\le c_+\delta^p,\qquad H\!\left(\frac{1}{2C_*\alpha(\delta)}\right)\le C_H\rho_\delta.$$

Then the approximate joint reconstructions satisfy, as $\delta\downarrow0$,

$$D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x_\delta,x^\dagger)=O(\rho_\delta),\qquad S_\delta=O(\delta^p),$$

where $S_\delta$ is the scalar residual, coupling, and projection error defined in the joint range-invariance VSC estimate lemma. In particular,

$$\|K(\widehat r_\delta-r(x^\dagger))\|_Y=O(\delta),\quad \|Px_\delta\|_X=O(\delta),\quad Q(r(x_\delta),\widehat r_\delta)=O(\delta),$$

and the data residual $\|K\widehat r_\delta+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y$ is $O(\delta)$.

For the following three-dimensional EIT specialization, assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1\subset\mathbb R^3$, let the known background be $1$ outside $B_\rho\Subset B_1$, and impose fixed bounds $0<m<1<M$ and $m\le\sigma\le M$. Let $s_1\in(5/2,7/2)$, use the intrinsic quadratic penalty $\frac12\|\sigma\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}^2$ on this admissible class, and let $\sigma^\dagger\in B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ with $s_2\in(s_1,2s_1-1)$. The Sobolev norm is the exact intrinsic Hilbert norm in the EIT compatibility lemma. Use centered mean-zero Neumann voltage data $(\mathscr N_\sigma-\mathscr N_1)Y_{\ell k}$ in $Y=\ell^2(L^2(S^2))$, its observation-augmentation range coordinates, and admitted approximate joint minimizers in the set $U$ specified by that lemma. The artificial voltage is $z\in Y$ and the projection is $P(\sigma-\sigma_0,z)=(0,z)$. Put

$$\nu=\frac{(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)}{s_2-1},\qquad L_\delta=\log(1/\delta).$$

For fixed $\beta>0$, noise bounded by $\delta$, and $\eta_\delta=O(\delta^2)$, the balanced choice $\alpha\asymp\delta^2L_\delta^\nu$ gives

$$\|\sigma_\delta-\sigma^\dagger\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}=O(L_\delta^{-\nu/2}),\qquad \|z_\delta\|_Y=O(\delta),\qquad S_\delta=O(\delta^2).$$

At the nominal endpoint $\alpha\asymp\delta^2$, the same conductivity norm rate holds under the explicit actual-noise and tolerance condition

$$2\|y^\delta-y\|_Y^2+\eta_\delta=O(\delta^2L_\delta^{-\nu});$$

then $S_\delta=O(\delta^2L_\delta^{-\nu})$ and $\|z_\delta\|_Y=O(\delta L_\delta^{-\nu/2})$. In each case the coupling distance and relaxed data residual have order $O(\sqrt{S_\delta}+\|y^\delta-y\|_Y)$. In particular the sum of the conductivity norm error and the artificial-voltage norm is $O(L_\delta^{-\nu/2})$ in all three stated regimes.

Fix $p,
u,a,C_*,C>0$ and let $\psi$ be a continuous nondecreasing concave source index with $\psi(0)=0$. Suppose its conjugate $H(q)=\sup_{t\ge0}(\psi(t)-qt)$ satisfies $H(q)\le C(\log q)^{-
u}$ for all sufficiently large $q$. Let $\delta\downarrow0$ be a nominal parameter, and put $L_\delta=\log(1/\delta)$. Suppose nonnegative errors satisfy
$$S_\delta+a\alpha_\delta e_\delta\le d_\delta+\alpha_\delta\psi(C_*S_\delta),\qquad \alpha_\delta\asymp\delta^p,\qquad d_\delta=O(\delta^pL_\delta^{-

Then
$$e_\delta=O(L_\delta^{-

For the joint objective estimate with $p\ge1$ and actual data noise $\varepsilon_\delta=\|y^\delta-y\|$, the hypothesis on $d_\delta$ is supplied by $2\varepsilon_\delta^p+\eta_\delta=O(\delta^pL_\delta^{-

u/2})$.

The universal assertion that $\alpha\asymp\delta^2$ yields a vanishing norm error for every deterministic noise family bounded by $\delta$ is false, even for an exact quadratic Tikhonov minimizer and a truth satisfying every nonnegative variational source inequality: on real $\ell^2$, take $Ke_j=j^{-1}e_j$, $x^\dagger=0$, $y^{\delta_j}=\delta_j e_j$, $\delta_j=1/j$, $\alpha_j=\delta_j^2$, and objective $\|Kx-y^{\delta_j}\|^2+ rac{\alpha_j}{2}\|x\|^2$. Its unique minimizer is $2e_j/3$. This counterexample refutes the universal abstract endpoint assertion; it makes no assertion that these data arise from an EIT conductivity map.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1(0)\subset\mathbb R^3$, fix $0<\rho<1$ and $0<m<1<M$, and let $E$ be the closed real subspace of $L^\infty(\Omega)$ consisting of functions vanishing almost everywhere outside $B_\rho(0)$. Set $\mathcal A=\{a\in E:\operatorname*{ess\,inf}(1+a)>m,\ \operatorname*{ess\,sup}(1+a)<M\}$ and $\sigma=1+a$. Choose an orthonormal spherical-harmonic basis $Y_{\ell k}$ of mean-zero $L^2(S^2)$, with $\ell\ge1$ and $1\le k\le2\ell+1$. For each basis current there is a unique weak solution $u_{\sigma,\ell k}\in H^1(\Omega)$ with boundary mean zero such that
$$\int_\Omega\sigma\nabla u_{\sigma,\ell k}\cdot\overline{\nabla v}=\int_{S^2}Y_{\ell k}\overline{\operatorname{Tr}v}\qquad(v\in H^1(\Omega)).$$
The centered sequence
$$G(a):=\big(\operatorname{Tr}(u_{\sigma,\ell k}-u_{1,\ell k})\big)_{\ell,k}$$
belongs to $Y=\ell^2(L^2(S^2))$. The map $G:\mathcal A\to Y$ is Fréchet differentiable, and both $G$ and $G'$ are Lipschitz on $\mathcal A$, with constants depending only on $m,M,\rho$ and the ball. Its derivative in direction $h\in E$ is the trace sequence of the unique boundary-mean-zero solutions
$$\int_\Omega\sigma\nabla v_{h,\ell k}\cdot\overline{\nabla w}=-\int_\Omega h\nabla u_{\sigma,\ell k}\cdot\overline{\nabla w}.$$
The uncentered sequence $(\operatorname{Tr}u_{1,\ell k})_{\ell,k}$ does not belong to $Y$.
