An **effective field** is a field whose elements have finite encodings and whose exact addition, subtraction, multiplication, equality test, and inversion of nonzero elements are terminating procedures. Input a finite-dimensional strict matrix realization of a $k$-linear ribbon category with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$, finite-dimensional color objects with fixed bases, exact matrices for every braiding and inverse braiding used, the evaluation and coevaluation maps for the closure, the twist matrices, and the matrix $J_W$ of the ribbon-induced pivotal comparison $j_W=u_W\circ\theta_W:W\to W^{\vee\vee}$ for $W=V_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes V_{a_n}$, where $u_W$ is the Drinfeld morphism. Also input a finite braid word $\beta$ on $n\ge1$ strands and the top color tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. The matrices are assumed to satisfy the stated ribbon-category axioms; an implementation does not infer those axioms from arbitrary matrices.

Use the strand-position permutation homomorphism $\pi:B_n\to\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$ given by $\pi(\sigma_i)=(i\ i+1)$. Read the braid letters in composition order, updating the current color tuple at each crossing by swapping its adjacent colors. For a positive letter $\sigma_i$, use the matrix of
$$1\otimes\cdots\otimes c_{V_{a_i},V_{a_{i+1}}}\otimes\cdots\otimes1,$$
and for a negative letter use its inverse. Let the blackboard-framed closure join the bottom and top endpoint at each position by the identity pairing. Reject the input if the final color tuple differs from the initial tuple: the tuple records the colors at the paired endpoints, so equality is exactly the condition that the closure carries a consistent color on every component. Starting with the identity matrix, multiply the typed crossing matrices in word order to obtain $M_\beta:W\to W$, then return the finite matrix contraction
$$\operatorname{ev}_{W^\vee}\bigl((J_WM_\beta)\otimes1_{W^\vee}\bigr)\operatorname{coev}_W\in k.$$
In ordinary dual-basis coordinates this contraction is the matrix trace $\operatorname{Tr}(J_WM_\beta)$.
This is the exact ribbon evaluation of the blackboard-framed colored braid closure in the given matrix realization. No algorithm is asserted for arbitrary abstract ribbon categories without effective finite matrix data.

derivations.claim: After $j$ updates, induction on $j$ shows that the running matrix is the composite of the first $j$ typed crossing maps in composition order. The base case $j=0$ is the identity of $W$; the update rule in [F1] composes exactly the next generator or its inverse, proving the induction step. There are precisely $m$ letters, so there are precisely $m$ updates.

At $j=m$, [F1] identifies the matrix with $M_\beta$. Its final-color check makes it an endomorphism of $W$, and the output contraction is the categorical pivotal trace of that endomorphism, hence the defined closure evaluation. Every update is one finite matrix multiplication and the last contraction is finite; the effective-field procedures terminate, so the algorithm terminates and has the asserted value.

Let $\omega$ be an indeterminate, set $A=\omega^{-2}$, and put $k'=\mathbb Q(\omega)$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}$. Work over the scalar extension to $k'$ of the library Hopf algebra at $q_L$. The parameter and Cartan-generator conversion from Korinman's convention is $q_L=q_K^{-1}$ and $K_L=K_K^{-1}$; the root generators $E,F$ correspond unchanged. The vector basis order remains $(v_+,v_-)$. Korinman displays these same column-action matrices for the root generators; no transpose is required. Thus the module matrices are
$$E=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad F=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad K_K=\begin{pmatrix}q_K&0\\0&q_K^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Equivalently, for the library parameter use $K_L=K_K^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(q_L,q_L^{-1})$ and the library coproduct convention $\Delta(E)=E\otimes K_L^{-1}+1\otimes E$, $\Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K_L\otimes F$. The parameters $q_K$ and $q_L$ are not identified.

The object $V$ is absolutely simple in the $k'$-linear representation category.

Korinman's §2.1 matrix
$$C_K=\begin{pmatrix}0&\omega\\-\omega^5&0\end{pmatrix}$$
is labeled there as the matrix of his inverse half-ribbon operator on the underlying vector space $V$. It is not the equivariant left-duality identification used below. Here $\Omega$ denotes specifically the Snyder–Tingley operator $X$, whose inverse matrix is computed independently below; it is not identified with $C_K$.

To specify the half-ribbon action, use the Snyder–Tingley convention $q_{\mathrm{ST}}=q_K$, $K_{\mathrm{ST}}=K_K=K_L^{-1}$, $E_{\mathrm{ST}}=E$, and $F_{\mathrm{ST}}=F$ in the same ordered basis. Since $q_K=\omega^{-4}$, choose $q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{1/4}=\omega^{-1}$. Let $X=JT_{w_0}$ be their half-ribbon element and let $\Omega$ be its operator on $V$. On the fundamental highest- and lowest-weight vectors, their formula gives $Xv_+=-q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_-$ and $Xv_-=q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_+$. The half-ribbon action therefore gives the actual inverse matrix and its square:
$$\operatorname{Mat}_{(v_+,v_-)}(\Omega^{-1})=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\omega^3\\\omega^3&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Omega^2=-\omega^{-6}\operatorname{id}_V=-A^3\operatorname{id}_V.$$
Snyder–Tingley’s associated Hopf-algebra ribbon element is $X^{-2}$; the positive categorical twist in this Kauffman-bracket convention is its inverse $X^2=\Omega^2$. In the ordered basis $(v_+\otimes v_+,v_+\otimes v_-,v_-\otimes v_+,v_-\otimes v_-)$, the positive braiding is
$$c_{V,V}=\begin{pmatrix}A&0&0&0\\0&0&A^{-1}&0\\0&A^{-1}&A-A^{-3}&0\\0&0&0&A\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its ribbon quantum dimension is $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. The half-ribbon and universal $R$-matrix are those of the topological half-ribbon representation category; the selected ribbon element is the Kauffman-bracket one, not the usual $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ ribbon element.

Let $v_+^*,v_-^*$ be the ordinary dual basis. The left-dual action on $V^*$ is the contragredient action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ for the antipode $S$ of the stated library Hopf convention. Identify the displayed copy of $V$ with this left dual $V^\vee$ by $v_+\mapsto v_-^*$ and $v_-\mapsto -A^{-2}v_+^*$. In this identification the evaluation and coevaluation maps are
$$B(v_+\otimes v_-)=1,\quad B(v_-\otimes v_+)=-A^{-2},\quad B(v_+\otimes v_+)=B(v_-\otimes v_-)=0,$$
$$U(1)=-A^2v_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+.$$
These are the explicit duality maps used in the closure trace.

The positive Artin generator is drawn with braid height increasing upward; the left input strand ends on the right, and the right input strand passes over it:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.center),scale=.8]
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (.46,-.08);
  \draw[->] (.54,.08) -- (1,1);
  \draw[->] (1,-1) .. controls (.72,-.5) and (.28,.5) .. (0,1);
  \node at (-.2,-1) {$i$};
  \node at (1.2,-1) {$i+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

The uninterrupted strand in the drawing is the overpassing strand. This is the crossing convention for the displayed matrix; the proof below uses its matrix entries and the half-ribbon source formulas, not the drawing.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals, twist $\theta$
([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) and Drinfeld morphism
$u_X\colon X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ of
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Put

$$j_X:=u_X\,\theta_X\ \colon\ X\longrightarrow X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Then $j$ is a natural isomorphism: it is the composite of the natural
isomorphism $u$ with the natural automorphism $\theta$ of the identity. It is
**monoidal** up to the monoidal comparison $d_{X,Y}\colon
X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\to(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$ of the double-dual
functor,

$$j_{X\otimes Y}=d_{X,Y}\circ(j_X\otimes j_Y),$$

which is precisely the statement that $u\theta$ is the pivotal comparison
induced by the ribbon structure; the identity follows from the tensor relation
$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ for
the Drinfeld morphism together with the twist axiom
$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and
the naturality of $\theta$. Iterating the comparison identifies
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}$ with the corresponding composite of the $j_X$ and the
coherence isomorphisms of the tensor power.

Let $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), and let
$\rho_n\colon B_n\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(X^{\otimes n})$ be the
canonical braid action
([[cor-an-object-of-a-braided-category-carries-canonical-braid-actions]]). The
**ribbon evaluation** of the $X$-colored closed braid is the value

$$t_n(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_L\!\left(j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)\right)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

in the sense of
[[def-the-categorical-trace-of-a-morphism-into-the-double-dual]]: the composite
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)$ is a morphism
$X^{\otimes n}\to(X^{\otimes n})^{\vee\vee}$, which is exactly the input type of
the left categorical trace. When $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$
the value $t_n(\beta)$ is a scalar. For $n=1$ the group $B_1$ is trivial and
$t_1(e)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_X)$, the left dimension of $X$.

For $n=0$ put $t_0(e)=1_{\mathbf 1}$, the evaluation of the empty
closed tangle. This is a separate convention; no generator or dual pairing
is needed for the empty diagram.

The identification of $t_n(\beta)$ with the evaluation
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ of the blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$
under the functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]] is
the content of the closure-comparison lemma of this page; it must be proved
before the trace is used as a link evaluation, and it is not assumed here. The
functor $F_X$ is constructed under countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), while the definition of $t_n$ above is choice-free
and uses neither that functor nor that principle; only the comparison, not the
trace, carries the choice cost.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

Let $A$ be an indeterminate, $R_A=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1},(A^{-4}+1)^{-1}]$,
$q=A^{-2}$, $t=q^2=A^{-4}$, $\delta=-(q+q^{-1})=-A^2-A^{-2}$, and
$z_0=-1/(t+1)$. For a nonempty regular diagram $D$, define
$\langle D\rangle$ by summing its crossing smoothings with weights $A$ and
$A^{-1}$ and the factor $\delta^{k-1}$ for a state with $k$ circles. Let
$B_n$ be the $n$-strand Artin braid group with positive geometric generators
$\sigma_i$ (label $i$ passes below the midpoint and label $i+1$ passes above),
drawn with braid parameter increasing from bottom to top; let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be the homomorphism $e(\sigma_i)=1$. Let $H(n)$ be
the type-A Hecke algebra with generators $T_i$, quadratic relation
$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v$, braid relations, and distant commutation; let $\pi_n$
send $\sigma_i$ to $T_i$. Its normalized Markov trace $\operatorname{tr}_n$
satisfies $\operatorname{tr}_n(1)=1$, cyclicity, tower restriction, and
$\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_n)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$. Let
$\mathrm{TL}_n$ be the noncrossing pairing algebra with loop value $\delta$,
and let $\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)}$ be the unnormalized trace,
where $c(D)$ is the number of circles after joining corresponding top and
bottom endpoints outside the rectangle; set
$\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. For $\beta\in B_n$,
$n\ge1$, orient its closure in the braid direction. Under the specialization
$v\mapsto t$, $z\mapsto z_0$ of the Hecke tower, one has
$$\langle\widehat\beta\rangle =\delta^{n-1}(-A)^{e(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\big|_{v=t,\,z=z_0}.$$
The identity gives bracket value $1$ on the one-strand identity closure. Its
positive and negative Markov stabilizations multiply the raw bracket by
$-A^3$ and $-A^{-3}$, respectively.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $B_n=\langle\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid\text{Artin
relators}\rangle$ be the braid group of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]); recall that $B_0$ and $B_1$
are trivial. The **exponent sum** is the unique homomorphism

$$e_n:B_n\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad e_n(\sigma_i)=1\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

where $\mathbb Z$ is the additive group of integers. It is well defined because
every defining relator of the Artin presentation has exponent sum $0$: the
braid relator $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$
has both sides of exponent sum $3$, and each far-commutation relator has both
sides of exponent sum $2$, so the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto1$ kills all
relators, and [[thm-von-dyck]] applies. It is surjective for $n\ge2$ and it is
the trivial map on the trivial group $B_1$. For every Artin word
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$ one has
$e_n(\beta)=\sum_{r=1}^k\varepsilon_r$ independently of the word, and
$e_n(\beta^{-1})=-e_n(\beta)$. **Caveat:** $e_n$ is the composite of the
abelianisation $B_n\to B_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with a surjection onto the free cyclic
group $\mathbb Z$ (for $n\ge2$): since the target is abelian, every commutator is sent to $0$, so $e_n$ factors through $B_n/[B_n,B_n]$ ([[def-abelianisation-of-a-group]]). No normal form, Garside structure or
faithfulness statement is used anywhere.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) with
chosen left duals ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]), braiding $c$
([[def-braiding]]) and twist $\theta$, and let $X\in\mathcal C$. Write
$X_{+1}:=X$ and $X_{-1}:=X^{\vee}$. In a strict model of $\mathcal C$
([[thm-every-braided-monoidal-category-is-monoidally-equivalent-to-a-strict-braided-one]])
there is a unique strict monoidal functor

$$F_X\colon\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal C$$

from the framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ with

$$F_X(+)=X,\qquad F_X(-)=X^{\vee},$$

$$F_X\bigl(X^{+}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=c_{X_\varepsilon,X_{\varepsilon'}},\qquad F_X\bigl(X^{-}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=(c_{X_{\varepsilon'},X_\varepsilon})^{-1},\qquad F_X(\cup_{+1})=\operatorname{coev}_X,\qquad F_X(\cap_{+1})=\operatorname{ev}_X,\qquad F_X(\varphi^{\pm1}_{+1})=\theta_X^{\pm1},$$

where the cup and cap are the coevaluation and evaluation maps attached to the
chosen left duals and the signs are the blackboard conventions of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]]. The remaining elementary tangles
of $\mathcal T$, those carrying a negative sign at a cup, cap or twist, receive
the values forced by these data through the relations. Explicitly put
$j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, with $u$ as in
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Then

$$F_X(\cup_-)=(1_{X^\vee}\otimes j_X^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee},\qquad F_X(\cap_-)=\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}(j_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}),\qquad F_X(\varphi_-^{\pm1})=\theta_{X^\vee}^{\pm1}.$$

structure; they need no identification $X^{\vee\vee}=X$ on objects. For a general ribbon
category the same assignment determines a strong monoidal functor, unique up to
the canonical coherence isomorphisms of the strictification. Isotopic framed
tangles are equal morphisms of $\mathcal T$, so $F_X$ is an invariant of framed
tangles. Uniqueness needs no choice.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category with chosen left duals and twist
$\theta$ ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]), let $X\in\mathcal C$, let
$n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, and let $\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the
blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$: the closed framed tangle diagram obtained
from the $(n,n)$-tangle diagram of $\beta$ by joining its top boundary points
to its bottom boundary points by the identity pairing in the blackboard
framing, with every band colored by $X$. Denote by
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ the value of the tangle evaluation functor
on a word in the elementary generators representing this closed diagram. Then

$$t_n(\beta)=F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

where $t_n$ is the ribbon trace of
[[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]] and $F_X$ is the tangle
evaluation functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]].
Consequently $t_n(\beta)$ depends only on the framed isotopy class of

stabilization $\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n$ is the framed closure of $\beta$ with
one positive curl added on a band, while the closure of the negative
stabilization adds one negative curl; with Turaev's convention the positive
curl is the generator $\varphi_X$ with $F_X(\varphi_X)=\theta_X$.

derivations.claim: In the ordered basis of [F1], direct subtraction gives $e:=A(c_{V,V}-AI)=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0&0\\0&-A^2&1&0\\0&1&-A^{-2}&0\\0&0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$. Writing $U(1)=-A^2v_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+$ and $B(v_+\otimes v_-)=1$, $B(v_-\otimes v_+)=-A^{-2}$ shows entrywise that $e=UB$. Hence $B(U(1))=-A^2-A^{-2}=\delta$ and $e^2=\delta e$. The explicit snake equalities in [F2] give the adjacent tensor relations: $e_{12}e_{23}e_{12}=UB\otimes1$ because the middle composites $(1\otimes B)(U\otimes1)$ and then $(B\otimes1)(1\otimes U)$ are identities; the reversed calculation gives $e_{23}e_{12}e_{23}=e_{23}$. Distant placements commute because they act on disjoint tensor factors.

Use source coordinates $(u,v)$ with their standard positive orientation and positive projection coordinates $(t,x)$ on the braid box. For $h>0$, the map $(t,x)=(v,-2hu)$ has determinant $2h>0$. It sends the source over direction $(1,1)$ to $(1,-2h)$ and the source under direction $(-1,1)$ to $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is $4h>0$. The source left/right pairs have constant $u$, hence constant braid position $x$ and give the through pairing $I$; the source top/bottom pairs have constant $v$, hence constant braid time $t$ and give the cup-cap $e_i$. The displayed page coordinates $(x,t)$ reverse the positive projection orientation; their visual quarter-turn is not the orientation comparison. Thus the A/B crossing expansion is $C_i=AI+A^{-1}e_i$. Its inverse is $C_i^{-1}=A^{-1}I+Ae_i$, since their product is $I+(A^2+A^{-2}+\delta)e_i=I$. By [A1] and [F8]–[F9], the categorical ribbon trace is the framed tangle evaluation of this braid closure, and that evaluator is monoidal with the stated crossing and duality maps. Expanding a braid word into the two smoothing choices therefore gives the bracket weights in [F4]. Because the closure has $n\ge1$ strands, each complete smoothing is a nonempty closed 1-manifold, hence a union of at least one circle. Its categorical value is $\delta^{|S|}$ by monoidality in [F8] and the loop value [F2], whereas the bracket state sum uses $\delta^{|S|-1}$; the extra single factor is independent of the state. Thus $t_n(\beta)=\delta\langle\widehat\beta\rangle$.

The matrix trace $t_n$ in [F3] closes the tensor-word braid with the duality maps $B,U$ of [F2]. Substituting each crossing into the trace expansion from step 2.1 therefore gives the first identity in the Statement. The Hecke formula [F6] then yields $t_n(\beta)=\delta^n(-A)^{e(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\big|_{v=t,z=z_0}$. By [F7], $e(\beta)=w(\beta)$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals, twist $\theta$
([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) and Drinfeld morphism
$u_X\colon X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ of
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Put

$$j_X:=u_X\,\theta_X\ \colon\ X\longrightarrow X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Then $j$ is a natural isomorphism: it is the composite of the natural
isomorphism $u$ with the natural automorphism $\theta$ of the identity. It is
**monoidal** up to the monoidal comparison $d_{X,Y}\colon
X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\to(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$ of the double-dual
functor,

$$j_{X\otimes Y}=d_{X,Y}\circ(j_X\otimes j_Y),$$

which is precisely the statement that $u\theta$ is the pivotal comparison
induced by the ribbon structure; the identity follows from the tensor relation
$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ for
the Drinfeld morphism together with the twist axiom
$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and
the naturality of $\theta$. Iterating the comparison identifies
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}$ with the corresponding composite of the $j_X$ and the
coherence isomorphisms of the tensor power.

Let $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), and let
$\rho_n\colon B_n\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(X^{\otimes n})$ be the
canonical braid action
([[cor-an-object-of-a-braided-category-carries-canonical-braid-actions]]). The
**ribbon evaluation** of the $X$-colored closed braid is the value

$$t_n(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_L\!\left(j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)\right)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

in the sense of
[[def-the-categorical-trace-of-a-morphism-into-the-double-dual]]: the composite
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)$ is a morphism
$X^{\otimes n}\to(X^{\otimes n})^{\vee\vee}$, which is exactly the input type of
the left categorical trace. When $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$
the value $t_n(\beta)$ is a scalar. For $n=1$ the group $B_1$ is trivial and
$t_1(e)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_X)$, the left dimension of $X$.

For $n=0$ put $t_0(e)=1_{\mathbf 1}$, the evaluation of the empty
closed tangle. This is a separate convention; no generator or dual pairing
is needed for the empty diagram.

The identification of $t_n(\beta)$ with the evaluation
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ of the blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$
under the functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]] is
the content of the closure-comparison lemma of this page; it must be proved
before the trace is used as a link evaluation, and it is not assumed here. The
functor $F_X$ is constructed under countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), while the definition of $t_n$ above is choice-free
and uses neither that functor nor that principle; only the comparison, not the
trace, carries the choice cost.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear ribbon category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)=k$. Let $X$ be absolutely simple, so its twist is $\theta_X=\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ for a unique $\lambda\in k^\times$. For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the value of the blackboard-framed $X$-colored closure and let $w(\beta)$ be the exponent sum, with positive Artin generator and positive stabilization conventions fixed as in the supplied ribbon-trace formulas. Then
$$J_X(\widehat\beta):=\lambda^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)$$
depends only on the oriented unframed link type of $\widehat\beta$ when every component has color $X$. This statement makes no normalization by the categorical dimension.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\beta,\beta'$ be braids. Then
$\widehat\beta$ and $\widehat{\beta'}$ are equivalent oriented links if and
only if $\beta$ and $\beta'$ are Markov equivalent, that is, related by a finite
sequence of conjugations in a fixed braid group, stabilizations
$\beta\mapsto\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ into the next braid group, and their
inverses.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided rigid monoidal category with braiding $c$, and
fix left duals $X^\vee$ for all objects together with the dual-morphism
operation of [[def-the-dual-of-a-morphism]].

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category and let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal C$.

A **left dual** of $X$ is an object $X^\vee$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}_X:X^\vee\otimes X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}_X:\mathbf 1\to X\otimes X^\vee$$

such that the composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_X\otimes1_X}(X\otimes X^\vee)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{X,X^\vee,X}}X\otimes(X^\vee\otimes X)\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{ev}_X}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_X}X$$

and

$$X^\vee\xrightarrow{\rho_{X^\vee}^{-1}}X^\vee\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_{X^\vee}\otimes\operatorname{coev}_X}X^\vee\otimes(X\otimes X^\vee)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X^\vee,X,X^\vee}}(X^\vee\otimes X)\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}}\mathbf 1\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\lambda_{X^\vee}}X^\vee$$

are identity morphisms.

A **right dual** of $X$ is an object ${}^\vee X$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}'_X:X\otimes{}^\vee X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}'_X:\mathbf 1\to{}^\vee X\otimes X$$

such that the mirror composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\rho_X^{-1}}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}'_X}X\otimes({}^\vee X\otimes X)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X,{}^\vee X,X}}(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}'_X\otimes1_X}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X}X$$

and

$${}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\lambda_{{}^\vee X}^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}'_X\otimes1_{{}^\vee X}}({}^\vee X\otimes X)\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{{}^\vee X,X,{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X\otimes(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\xrightarrow{1_{{}^\vee X}\otimes\operatorname{ev}'_X}{}^\vee X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_{{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X$$

are identity morphisms.

This page uses EGNO's convention: the word "left" refers to the side on which
the dual object sits in the evaluation map.

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Write

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) and Drinfeld morphism
$u_X\colon X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ of

functor,

which is precisely the statement that $u\theta$ is the pivotal comparison
induced by the ribbon structure; the identity follows from the tensor relation

the Drinfeld morphism together with the twist axiom
$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and
the naturality of $\theta$. Iterating the comparison identifies
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}$ with the corresponding composite of the $j_X$ and the
coherence isomorphisms of the tensor power.

Let $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), and let
$\rho_n\colon B_n\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(X^{\otimes n})$ be the
canonical braid action
([[cor-an-object-of-a-braided-category-carries-canonical-braid-actions]]). The
**ribbon evaluation** of the $X$-colored closed braid is the value

$$t_n(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_L\!\left(j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)\right)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

in the sense of

the value $t_n(\beta)$ is a scalar. For $n=1$ the group $B_1$ is trivial and

For $n=0$ put $t_0(e)=1_{\mathbf 1}$, the evaluation of the empty
closed tangle. This is a separate convention; no generator or dual pairing
is needed for the empty diagram.

The identification of $t_n(\beta)$ with the evaluation
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ of the blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$
under the functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]] is
the content of the closure-comparison lemma of this page; it must be proved
before the trace is used as a link evaluation, and it is not assumed here. The
functor $F_X$ is constructed under countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), while the definition of $t_n$ above is choice-free
and uses neither that functor nor that principle; only the comparison, not the

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Let $\mathcal C$ have objects finite-dimensional rational vector spaces $U$ equipped with a linear involution $S_U$ ($S_U^2=1$), and morphisms commuting with the involutions. Use $S_{U\otimes W}=S_U\otimes S_W$, the ordinary flip braiding, standard vector-space duality, and define $\theta_U=S_U$. This is a ribbon category: the twist is natural because every morphism commutes with $S$; its tensor rule is $S_{U\otimes W}=S_U\otimes S_W$ and the double flip is the identity; and on the dual, $S_{U^*}=(S_U^{-1})^T=S_U^T=(\theta_U)^*$, giving ribbon dual compatibility. The unit is $\mathbb Q$ with trivial involution, so $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=\mathbb Q$. By [F7], the Drinfeld morphism in this symmetric vector-space category is the canonical double-dual identification: on $v\in U$ and $f\in U^*$ its evaluation is $u_U(v)(f)=f(v)$. Thus the ribbon-induced pivotal map $j_U=u_U\theta_U$ is the canonical double-dual identification composed with $S_U$.

Take $X=\mathbb Q e_+\oplus\mathbb Q e_-$ with $S_X=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. It is decomposable and its twist is invertible but nonscalar. For the identity $e\in B_1$, [F1] gives $t_1(e)=\operatorname{Tr}(S_X)=1+(-1)=0$. For $\sigma_1\in B_2$, the braid action is the flip $P$. By [F8], under the canonical vector-space double-dual comparison, $j_{X\otimes X}$ has matrix $S_X\otimes S_X$, so the trace of $(S_X\otimes S_X)P$ is $2$: the basis tensors $e_+\otimes e_+$ and $e_-\otimes e_-$ contribute diagonal entries $1$, while the two mixed basis tensors are exchanged and contribute no diagonal entries.

The braid $\sigma_1$ is the positive Markov stabilization of the identity braid in $B_1$, so [F3] says their oriented unframed closures are equivalent. Their exponent sums are $w(e)=0$ and $w(\sigma_1)=1$. For any proposed $\lambda\in\mathbb Q^\times$, the corrected values are $0$ and $2\lambda^{-1}$, which are unequal because $2\ne0$ and $\lambda$ is invertible. This contradicts the false claim. The counterexample has precisely the missing hypothesis identified by [F2]: its invertible twist is not scalar on the decomposable color.

citations.quote:
Fix a rigid monoidal category with chosen left duals. For a morphism
$a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, the **left categorical trace** of $a$ is the endomorphism
of the unit

$$\operatorname{Tr}_L(a):\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_X}X\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{a\otimes1_{X^\vee}}X^{\vee\vee}\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}}\mathbf 1.$$

For a morphism $b:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$, the **right categorical trace** of $b$ is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(b):\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{1_{X^\vee}\otimes b}X^\vee\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X}\mathbf 1.$$

So a bare endomorphism $X\to X$ is not yet an input to categorical trace; one
first needs a comparison between $X$ and a double dual.

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Write

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

Every permutation of a finite set is a product of pairwise disjoint cycles,
uniquely up to reordering the factors and cyclically rotating the entries within
each cycle. The identity permutation has the empty disjoint-cycle decomposition.

Let $X$ be a finite set and let $\sigma\in\operatorname{Sym}(X)$, with cycle
notation and composition as in [[def-symmetric-group]].

The **support** and **fixed-point set** of $\sigma$ are

$$\operatorname{supp}(\sigma):=\{x\in X:\sigma(x)\ne x\},\qquad \operatorname{Fix}(\sigma):=\{x\in X:\sigma(x)=x\}.$$

A cycle $(a_0\,a_1\,\ldots\,a_{k-1})$ has **length** $k$ and support
$\{a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}\}$. Two cycles are **disjoint** when their supports are
disjoint. A **disjoint-cycle decomposition** of $\sigma$ is an expression for
$\sigma$ as a product of pairwise disjoint cycles of length at least $2$.
One-cycles are omitted, and the empty product is the identity permutation.

When $|X|=n$, the **cycle type** of $\sigma$ is the list of natural numbers
$c_1(\sigma),\ldots,c_n(\sigma)$, where $c_k(\sigma)$ is the number of
$k$-element orbits of the action generated by $\sigma$. Thus $c_1(\sigma)$ is
the number of fixed points. Equivalently, the cycle type records the lengths of
all cycles after each fixed point is inserted as a one-cycle.

For $n\ge2$, the **braid group** $B_n$ is the group with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and relations

$$\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\qquad(1\le i\le n-2),$$

$$\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\qquad(1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1).$$

Equivalently,

$$B_n=\langle \sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\ (1\le i\le n-2),\ \sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\ (1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

interpreted in the sense of [[def-group-presentation]] and
[[def-relators-relations-and-finite-presentations]].

For $n=0$ and $n=1$, there are no generators, and $B_n$ is the trivial group
given by the empty presentation.

Let $\langle X\mid R\rangle$ be a presentation, let $H$ be a group, and let
$u:X\to H$ be a function. If the evaluation of every $r\in R$ under $u$ is
$e_H$, then there is a unique homomorphism

$$\overline u:\langle X\mid R\rangle\longrightarrow H$$

with $\overline u([x])=u(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Moreover, $\overline u$ is
surjective if and only if $u(X)$ generates $H$.

derivations.claim: If $n=1$, the braid group is trivial and $\pi$ is its unique homomorphism. If $n\ge2$, put $s_i=(i\ i+1)$. For $|i-j|>1$, $s_i$ and $s_j$ commute because they have disjoint supports; for adjacent indices, both $s_i s_{i+1}s_i$ and $s_{i+1}s_i s_{i+1}$ equal $(i\ i+2)$. These are the Artin relators, so [F5] gives the homomorphism $\pi$. By [F4], each positive or negative braid generator swaps its two adjacent tensor factors, so the action on $W=V^{\otimes n}$ is the factor permutation given by $\pi(\beta)$. The twist is identity. Let $w_1,\ldots,w_{d^n}$ be the tensor basis of $W$ and $w_1^*,\ldots,w_{d^n}^*$ its ordinary dual basis. Substitution in [F2]'s formula gives $u_W(w_r)(w_s^*)=1$ when $r=s$ and $0$ otherwise, so the pivotal comparison is the canonical double-dual identification. The categorical trace formula [F1] is therefore the ordinary matrix trace of that permutation operator.

Fix a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $V$. A basis tensor $e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_n}$ is fixed by the factor permutation exactly when its indices are constant on each orbit of $\pi(\beta)$; by [F3], these orbits are exactly the cycles counted by $c(\pi(\beta))$, including fixed points. There are $d$ independent choices for each cycle, hence exactly $d^{c(\pi(\beta))}$ fixed basis tensors. A permutation matrix has trace equal to its number of fixed basis vectors, proving the formula.

The identity in $B_1$ has one permutation cycle, the identity in $B_2$ has two, and $\sigma_1$ has the transposition permutation with one cycle. Substitution into the formula gives $d$, $d^2$, and $d$, respectively; the latter closure is a single component because its endpoint permutation has one cycle. These calculations include $d=0$ because every listed cycle count is positive.

derivations.claim: A degree-$n$ chord diagram is a pairing of $2n$ cyclically ordered endpoints, so only finitely many such diagrams exist. A 4T relation is determined by a background diagram and finitely many endpoint positions, and a 1T relation by one diagram; hence there are finitely many relation vectors. By [F1], each has integer coefficients, so they form the rows of a finite integer matrix $A$. Write $A_n(F):=F^{C_n}/\operatorname{rowspan}_F(A)$ and $W_n(F):=\operatorname{Hom}_F(A_n(F),F)$. Since $k$ has characteristic zero, $\mathbb Q$ embeds in $k$. The rank of $A$ is unchanged by this field extension: a nonzero maximal minor over $\mathbb Q$ remains nonzero in $k$, while every larger minor that vanishes over $\mathbb Q$ still vanishes in $k$. Thus the row space over $k$ is the scalar extension of the rational row space, and $A_n(k)\cong A_n(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}k$.

The quotient is finite-dimensional, so extending a rational basis and its dual basis gives $W_n(k)\cong W_n(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}k$. If $n=0$, the sole diagram is the empty diagram and any weight system is its value $c\in k$; the constant invariant $V(K)=c$ has top symbol $c$. For $n>0$, choose a finite $\mathbb Q$-basis $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_d$ of $W_n(\mathbb Q)$; finite-dimensional row reduction chooses this basis without a choice axiom. By [F2], for each $i$ there is a rational-valued finite-type invariant $V_i$ with top symbol $\phi_i$. Write the given weight system as $W=\sum_{i=1}^d a_i\phi_i$ with $a_i\in k$, and define $V=\sum_{i=1}^d a_iV_i$, viewing each rational value in $k$. Linearity of the finite-difference operator gives top symbol $W$. If $W_n(\mathbb Q)=0$, the sum is empty and the zero invariant supplies the zero weight system.

citations.quote:
Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. A **framed $m$-singular knot** has finitely many transverse double points and finitely many simple zeroes of a smooth section of $\nu_K$, all disjoint; its number $m$ of singularities is the number of double points plus the number of zeroes. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. These are the $+$ and $-$ resolutions of that zero and determine the framing classes on the resolved knots.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of unframed oriented knots and an $m$-singular knot $K$, its **finite difference** is
$$
D_mV(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^m}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\epsilon_i\right)V(K_\epsilon),
$$
where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. The same formula defines $D_mV$ for an invariant of framed knots on framed singular knots, counting both double points and framing zeroes among the $m$ singularities. For one double point it reads $V(K_+)-V(K_-)$; the zero resolutions use the local normal-section model just specified. An invariant has **type at most $n$** if $D_{n+1}V$ vanishes on every $(n+1)$-singular object in its category. It has **exact type $n$** if it has type at most $n$ but not type at most $n-1$. Type at most $-1$ means the zero invariant, so a nonzero type-at-most-zero invariant has exact type zero. For an unframed link, replace $S^1$ by a finite disjoint union of oriented circles, allow marked self- or mixed double points, and use the same resolution sum. For a framed link, take a normal section on each component and count its simple zeroes together with all double points.

Let $D,D'$ be regular oriented diagrams of links $L,L'$. If the diagrams
differ by one oriented Reidemeister move or a planar isotopy, the links are
equivalent. The local Reidemeister replacement has a realization supported
in a ball over its move disk, after choosing lifts that agree outside that
ball. Comparing arbitrary realizing links may additionally require changing
their heights away from the move disk.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: To realize a degree-$n$ diagram, take its finite cyclic list of chord endpoints, identify each paired pair as a four-valent vertex, and join consecutive endpoints by arcs in $S^3$. Choose disjoint small vertex balls first. Place the finitely many intervening arcs successively in general position relative to those already placed; two one-dimensional arcs in a three-manifold can be separated by a small endpoint-fixed perturbation, so there are no unintended intersections. Smoothing the joins gives exactly the prescribed double points. In the framed case choose a nonzero normal section along the regular arcs and the two branches at every vertex. To close the section around the parameter circle, cut at one regular parameter; the two endpoint unit normals lie in an oriented two-plane and can be joined because its unit circle is connected. Smooth the finitely many joins. This constructs a zero-free framed representative. The framed branch uses [A1] for the normal-bundle structures.

Let $K,K'$ be representatives of the same diagram. Identify their finite marked graphs and fix matching local models in disjoint vertex balls. Join corresponding edge arcs by a homotopy relative to those balls, and homotope the normal sections over the edge strips, allowing zeroes during the homotopy. A finite relative perturbation makes the coincidence equations for two distinct curve parameters transverse: they are three scalar equations in the two curve parameters and time, so their solutions are isolated. It also makes the normal-section zero equation transverse: it is two scalar equations in the curve parameter and time, so its solutions are isolated. The parameter domains can be made compact after deleting a neighborhood of the diagonal, where each curve is locally embedded; the fixed vertex neighborhoods contain no new events. The higher-codimension loci for tangencies, triple points, degenerate section zeroes, or simultaneous events are avoided by the same finite perturbation. Hence only finitely many isolated double-point or framing-zero events occur. Passing any one event changes $D_nV$ by, up to sign, $D_{n+1}V$ on the object with that extra singularity, which vanishes by type at most $n$ in [F1]. Therefore $D_nV(K)=D_nV(K')$. For a 4T generator choose the four local singular representatives with the same outside $(n-2)$ marked double points and, in the framed case, the same zero-free framing outside the move ball. Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. A **framed $m$-singular knot** has finitely many transverse double points and finitely many simple zeroes of a smooth section of $\nu_K$, all disjoint; its number $m$ of singularities is the number of double points plus the number of zeroes. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. These are the $+$ and $-$ resolutions of that zero and determine the framing classes on the resolved knots.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of unframed oriented knots and an $m$-singular knot $K$, its **finite difference** is
$$
D_mV(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^m}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\epsilon_i\right)V(K_\epsilon),
$$
where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. The same formula defines $D_mV$ for an invariant of framed knots on framed singular knots, counting both double points and framing zeroes among the $m$ singularities. For one double point it reads $V(K_+)-V(K_-)$; the zero resolutions use the local normal-section model just specified. An invariant has **type at most $n$** if $D_{n+1}V$ vanishes on every $(n+1)$-singular object in its category. It has **exact type $n$** if it has type at most $n$ but not type at most $n-1$. Type at most $-1$ means the zero invariant, so a nonzero type-at-most-zero invariant has exact type zero. For an unframed link, replace $S^1$ by a finite disjoint union of oriented circles, allow marked self- or mixed double points, and use the same resolution sum. For a framed link, take a normal section on each component and count its simple zeroes together with all double points.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented smooth knot
$K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$, its normal bundle is
$\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, oriented so that a positive tangent to $K$ followed by a
positive basis of a normal fibre gives the ambient orientation. A **framing**
of $K$ is a homotopy class through smooth nowhere-zero sections of $\nu K$.
The normal bundle is made a smooth vector bundle under this axiom; a framed
knot includes the section class as data, not a choice made afterwards. For the
relative integer use the round metric transferred from the unit sphere in
$\mathbb R^4$ by the explicit diffeomorphism
$$x\longmapsto\left(\frac{2x}{1+\lVert x\rVert^2},\frac{\lVert x\rVert^2-1}{1+\lVert x\rVert^2}\right),\qquad\infty\longmapsto(0,0,0,1).$$
It induces a smooth bundle metric on $\nu K$. The resulting winding number is
independent of the metric: any two smooth fibre metrics interpolate through
positive metrics and the corresponding angle maps are homotopic.

Given a reference framing $[s_0]$ and another framing $[s_1]$, use a bundle
metric and the positive quarter-turn $J$ on each oriented normal plane. Choose
representatives $s_0,s_1$ and normalize both to unit sections
$\widehat s_i(x):=s_i(x)/\lVert s_i(x)\rVert$. Write
$$\widehat s_1(x)=\cos\theta(x)\widehat s_0(x)+\sin\theta(x)J\widehat s_0(x).$$
The resulting map $S^1\to S^1$ has a continuous angle lift along a parameter
interval $[0,1]$: subdivide into finitely many intervals whose images lie in
open semicircles and choose consecutive local arguments agreeing at endpoints.
Since the map is closed, the lift satisfies $\theta(1)-\theta(0)=2\pi m$ for
some $m\in\mathbb Z$; different lifts differ by a constant multiple of
$2\pi$, and homotopies keep $m$ fixed. Conversely, the difference between
$\theta(t)$ and $\theta(0)+2\pi mt$ is periodic, so linear interpolation of
these angles gives a homotopy to the degree-$m$ rotation of $\widehat s_0$.
Every integer occurs by such a rotation. Thus $m$ classifies the framing class
relative to $[s_0]$ and gives the **relative framing integer**. Once a reference
framing is supplied, the framing classes are an integer torsor; no absolute
integer is assigned before choosing a reference.

The **self-linking number** of a framed knot $(K,[s])$ is the linking number
of $K$ with a sufficiently small push-off along $s$, oriented parallel to $K$.
The push-off and its integer are independent of the representative section,
small radius, and normalized tubular chart by the preceding well-definedness
result.

If a compact oriented surface $\Sigma$ is supplied with boundary $K$, its
**Seifert framing relative to $\Sigma$** is the homotopy class of the inward
unit conormal to $K$ in $\Sigma$, viewed as a nonzero normal section to $K$ in
$S^3$. This definition is relative to the supplied surface; it neither asserts
that every knot bounds such a surface nor asserts the self-linking-zero result.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be an
oriented smooth embedded circle and let $s$ be a smooth nowhere-zero section of
its normal bundle. For any tubular neighbourhood chart that is the inclusion
on the zero section and identifies each vertical normal fibre with the ambient
normal quotient by the identity, the curve $K_{\varepsilon s}$ obtained by
mapping the graph of $\varepsilon s$ into $S^3$ is an embedded oriented circle
disjoint from $K$ for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. The integer
linking number of $K$ with $K_{\varepsilon s}$ is independent of the sufficiently
small radius, of the representative section in its homotopy class, and of the
normalized tubular chart. It therefore defines a self-linking integer of the
framing class $[s]$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a regular oriented diagram
of a knot $K$ with blackboard framing $b_D$. The self-linking number of the
framed knot $(K,b_D)$ equals the diagram writhe:
$$\operatorname{sl}(K,b_D)=\operatorname{wr}(D).$$
More generally, let $D$ be a regular oriented diagram of an oriented link
$L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$, and let $b_{D,i}$ be the blackboard framing
of $K_i$ induced by its component subdiagram. Then
$\operatorname{sl}(K_i,b_{D,i})=\operatorname{wr}_i(D)\qquad(1\le i\le r).$ Total writhe of a link still includes
the signs of mixed crossings, while the sum of component self-linking numbers
uses only self-crossings.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

The input is a finite regular oriented link diagram together with its declared
components. If it does not have exactly two components, return
`invalid-input`. For a two-component diagram $D$, initialize $s:=0$ and make
one pass over its finite crossing list. At each crossing whose branches lie on
different components, add
$$\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$$
to $s$, where the determinant is taken in the oriented projection plane; ignore
self-crossings. Return $s/2$. The even-sum lemma establishes that this output is
an integer and is the diagram's linking number.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. On every finite regular oriented diagram
with exactly two components, the crossing-scan algorithm halts after one
iteration per crossing and returns the integer half-sum of the mixed crossing
signs. On an input with any other number of components it returns
`invalid-input` after the finite component-count check.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Let $K$ be an $n$-singular knot with an isolated chord corresponding to the double point $p$. Its two preimages split the parameter circle into arcs $A$ and $B$. Isolation means no other marked double point has one preimage on each of $A$ and $B$. Choose a regular projection. There are finitely many ordinary crossings between the arcs. Switch them one at a time until every crossing has the $A$-branch over the $B$-branch. Each switch changes $D_nV$ by, up to sign, the $(n+1)$-fold difference on the knot with that ordinary crossing newly marked; this is zero by [F1]. Thus these switches preserve $D_nV(K)$.

For the framed branch, let $V$ be integer-valued self-linking. On a regular framed diagram compare a unit representative of its framing section $f$ with the unit blackboard normal section $b$. Their oriented fibrewise angle defines a map $S^1\to S^1$; let $\tau(f,b)\in\mathbb Z$ be its degree. In the tubular coordinates determined by $(b,Jb)$, the push-off along $f$ winds $\tau(f,b)$ times meridionally relative to the blackboard push-off. A positive meridian links the core once, since its oriented normal disk meets the core once with the sign fixed by the positive frame $(T,b,Jb)$. Thus $\operatorname{sl}(K,f)=\operatorname{sl}(K,b)+\tau(f,b)$; [F9] supplies the unit-twist normalization, and this local orientation calculation fixes its sign. Equivalently, each positive turn creates a local clasp with two positive mixed crossings, and [F7]–[F8] give the same linking increment. By [F6], $\operatorname{sl}(K,b)=\operatorname{wr}(D)$. For a framed singular knot with two disjoint singularities, all changes outside their local balls are fixed. Inside each ball, resolving a double point changes only that crossing's writhe contribution and local angle path; resolving a framing zero changes only the local angle path. Winding degrees add under concatenation, so the four self-linking values have the form $C+c_1\epsilon_1+c_2\epsilon_2$ for constants independent of $(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$. Their alternating second difference is $(C+c_1+c_2)-(C+c_1-c_2)-(C-c_1+c_2)+(C-c_1-c_2)=0$. This covers any pair of double-point or framing-zero singularities, so self-linking has type at most $1$. On a one-chord diagram with blackboard framing, the two crossing resolutions have writhes $+1$ and $-1$ and zero relative twist; their derivative is $1-(-1)=2$ by [F3] and [F6]. This is nonzero over $\mathbb Z$, so no universal framed 1T vanishing law is valid. The $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption enters only through [F4]–[F9] and [A1].

The consistent over-under assignment lets the lifts of the interiors of $A$ and $B$ lie in opposite open half-spaces bounded by a plane through $p$. Cap each arc on its own side by a short boundary-parallel arc to obtain oriented singular knots $A^\circ$ and $B^\circ$ carrying the remaining marked double points. The two resolutions at $p$ are the connected sums $A^\circ\#B^\circ$ and $B^\circ\#A^\circ$. An orientation-preserving half-turn of the round $S^3$ that exchanges the two balls of the connected-sum decomposition carries the first knot, with its orientation, to the second; the path of rotations through angles from $0$ to $\pi$ is an ambient isotopy. Hence the two resolutions are ambient-isotopic, so their $V$-values agree and $D_nV(K)=0$.

derivations.claim: Let $C$ be half the signed sum of all mixed crossings except the marked one. Under [A1], [F4] identifies the diagram half-sum with the integer linking number and [F5] makes it an ambient-isotopy invariant. By [F2] and [F3], the positive and negative resolutions contribute respectively $+\tfrac12$ and $-\tfrac12$ to this linking number, so $\operatorname{lk}(L_1,L_2)_+-\operatorname{lk}(L_1,L_2)_-=(C+\tfrac12)-(C-\tfrac12)=1$. This is the stated positive-minus-negative derivative under [F1]; reversing that subtraction changes its sign.
A knot has one component and therefore no unordered pair of distinct components; the total pairwise linking sum contains no terms and equals $0$.

If both marked crossings are mixed, write their resolution signs as $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\in\{+1,-1\}$ and absorb every other mixed crossing into $C$. By [F2]–[F4], $\operatorname{lk}(L_{\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2})=C+\tfrac12(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)$. The alternating second difference is zero: the constant has coefficient $1-1-1+1=0$, and each term linear in one $\epsilon_i$ cancels when the other sign is summed. If either marked crossing is a self-crossing, the link formula [F3] is independent of that resolution, so the alternating sum over its two choices cancels term by term. Thus $D_2=0$ for every pair of marked crossings by [F1].

derivations.claim: Form the coefficientwise formal expression $C_D(z)=\sum_{j\ge0}c_j(D)z^j$ from [F1]. It is a diagram invariant, has value $1$ on an unknot, and satisfies $C_{D_+}-C_{D_-}=zC_{D_0}$ coefficientwise. A local positive and negative curl on any component of the $r$-component unlink are both that unlink; the oriented smoothing is the $(r+1)$-component unlink. Thus $c_j(U_r)-c_j(U_r)=c_{j-1}(U_{r+1})$ for every $j\ge1$. All coefficients of $U_{r+1}$ vanish. Therefore the unlink values of the formal expression are $1$ for one component and $0$ for more than one. This is also the forced unlink value for ANY polynomial-valued invariant satisfying the Definition.

Here is the finite argument that the expression is actually in $\mathbb Z[z]$. In a diagram choose finitely many component basepoints and an order. Call a crossing bad when its first encounter in this traversal is the underpass. If none is bad, the first component passes over every later component and has a descending self-diagram. Pull its successive arcs above everything they first encounter to isolate a round circle; repeat for the remaining components. Thus a descending diagram is an unlink. At a bad crossing the skein relation writes its value as the value of the switched diagram, plus or minus $z$ times its oriented smoothing. The switched diagram has one fewer bad crossing and the same number $N$ of crossings; the smoothing has $N-1$ crossings. Reset the finite component data on a smoothing if necessary. The nonnegative integer $N(N+1)/2+b$, with $b$ the number of bad crossings, decreases in each branch. Hence this is a FINITE resolution tree. Its leaves have values $0$ or $1$ by step1.1. Working back through the tree uses only integer addition/subtraction and multiplication by $z$, so $C_D\in\mathbb Z[z]$. In fact every branch has at most $N$ smoothing operations, giving degree at most $N$. This proves finiteness and integrality without assuming an integer-valued formal sequence theorem or making an infinite selection.

Apply the SAME finite tree to any two polynomial-valued invariants satisfying the stated normalization and skein relation. Their unlink leaves agree by step1.1, and each internal skein relation then forces agreement. Their values agree on every diagram. Existence follows from [F1], step 2.1 and the ambient-link interpretation [F2], and this argument proves uniqueness. The separately fixed empty-link extension is unique as well, since its prescribed value is zero. Consequently the separate existence/uniqueness obligation mentioned in the Definition is now discharged: the resulting actual link invariant is exactly $\nabla$, and its coefficient $[z^k]\nabla_L$ is well-defined for every $k$. Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.
