Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Let $F:M^m\to N^n$ be smooth and let $Z\subseteq N$ be an embedded submanifold
of codimension $c$, and suppose $F\pitchfork Z$. If $c\le m$, then
$F^{-1}(Z)$ is an embedded submanifold of $M$ of codimension $c$ (possibly empty). If $c>m$,
then $F^{-1}(Z)=\varnothing$. In the first case, for each $p\in F^{-1}(Z)$,

$$ T_pF^{-1}(Z)=\{v\in T_pM:dF_p(v)\in T_{F(p)}Z\}. $$

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:C\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be a smooth
isotopy of a finite disjoint union of circles, constant near both ends, and
suppose both end projections under the fixed $\pi$ are regular. Arbitrarily
close to $F$ in the strong smooth topology there is such an isotopy $F'$, equal
to $F$ near the ends, whose projected slices have only these exceptional events:

(i) finitely many ordinary cusps, at distinct times; in a source coordinate
$x$, writing $g(x,t)=\pi F'(x,t)$, each satisfies
$g_x=0$, $\det(g_{xx},g_{xt})\ne0$ and
$\det(g_{xx},g_{xxx})\ne0$;

(ii) the **off-diagonal unordered** double-point locus is a smooth
one-dimensional manifold with boundary in the local-extension sense of
[[def-smooth-chart-atlas-and-structure-on-a-manifold-with-boundary]]; its boundary
consists exactly of the double points at $t=0,1$. Its interior is a manifold
without boundary, and its time projection has only finitely many
nondegenerate critical points, each an ordinary quadratic tangency of two
immersed branches;

(iii) finitely many transverse triple events, with all three pairs of
projected tangents independent, and no quadruple points.

No two exceptional events have the same time. All other slices are regular,
and between exceptional times their decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy.

Let $F'$ satisfy the general-position conditions of
[[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-links-can-be-put-in-general-position]], with
exceptional times $t_1<\cdots<t_N$. Immediately before and after each event,
its regular diagrams differ, up to planar isotopy, by one oriented
Reidemeister move: R1 at an ordinary cusp, R2 at a quadratic double tangency,
and R3 at a transverse triple event. The regular intervals contribute planar
isotopies, and the moves preserve the over/under and orientation data of $F'$.
Consequently the end diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of these moves.

An **oriented Reidemeister move** is one of the following local replacements of
a regular oriented link diagram ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]),
performed inside a small closed disk while the diagram outside the disk is left
unchanged, and understood up to planar isotopy outside the disk
([[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]]). All sign and orientation variants of
each local picture are included.

**(R1) Kink creation and deletion.** A single strand is replaced by a small
kink: two arcs crossing once and otherwise disjoint from the strand, with the
over/under datum of the new crossing as in the picture. The move is allowed in
both directions (create or delete the kink) and with both signs of the kink,
the sign being the sign of the crossing created. The orientations of the two
strands of the kink are the two possible consistent orientations through the
crossing, and all of them occur in the move list.

**(R2) Slide of two strands.** Two local arcs belonging to two strands are
replaced so that the number of crossings between those strands changes by two
of opposite signs: the standard picture slides one strand over or under the
other, creating or deleting the pair of crossings, with the two crossings being
the two possible signs in either order. All four orientation patterns of the
two strands at the two crossings are included.

**(R3) Sliding a strand past a crossing.** One strand is moved across an
existing crossing of two other strands, so that the crossing of the two other
strands passes from one side of the moving strand to the other; the three
crossings of the local picture keep their signs and the over/under data are
preserved. The three strands must have a consistent strict height order:
one is above both others, one below both, and the remaining strand is between
them. The cyclic over/under pattern is excluded. Every orientation pattern
and all six height orders of this standard local picture are included.

A local R2 or R3 picture is **braid-like** when, after a local coordinate
change and deformation, all participating strands run in the same positive
longitudinal direction. This is a local condition and does not require a
globally chosen braid axis. R1 is kept as a separate kink move.

The strands keep their orientations throughout every move. The union of the
three move types, together with planar isotopy, generates the equivalence
relation on diagrams used in the Reidemeister equivalence theorem below; the
moves are sometimes called R1, R2, R3 as above. Since every move changes the
diagram only inside a disk, it has a type and a finite list of local
orientation/sign variants, and each variant is realized by an ambient isotopy
as the next items show. The complete list of variants is required because the
Markov and Alexander constructions below act on oriented diagrams and count
signed crossings.

derivations.claim: **The endpoint realizations and the common cap.** Regard a planar diagram as a diagram on the projection sphere, and choose a small closed disk $U$ about its mark meeting the diagram in one crossing-free arc only. The complementary disk contains a proper interval diagram; its two endpoints can be put at any prescribed two boundary points by an orientation-preserving disk coordinate change, preserving the interval orientation. Realize its crossings at small distinct positive or negative heights in a thickening of that disk, and straighten short end collars. Round the thickening to a standard three-ball $B$. Closing the interval by a fixed unknotted arc in the complementary ball $B_*$ gives exactly the original diagram on the sphere: the two projected disks glue along their boundary and the cap is the single deleted arc. This operation changes no crossing, sign, or resolution; it replaces the marked circle in every resolution by one interval. Make these choices for both diagrams with the same $B,B_*$, endpoints and cap $J$. The cap and slightly longer knot collars may be chosen identical as parametrized embeddings at both ends. Indeed an orientation-preserving change of circle parametrization can prescribe its parametrization on an interval; it extends over the remaining interval by a strictly increasing smooth map. Such circle reparametrizations are isotopic to the identity, as seen by interpolating their increasing lifts $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $f(x+1)=f(x)+1$, with the identity lift. Thus there is a smooth isotopy $F_t$ of the closed parametrized knots with these endpoint embeddings and this common source interval $J$. Reparametrize time to make it stationary near $0,1$. Here the existence of $F_t$ is exactly the hypothesis that the two closed diagrams represent the same oriented knot.

**Trivialize a moving ball, including its endpoint charts.** Along the track of the slightly enlarged source interval $J$, choose a smooth pair of normal vectors to the nonzero knot tangent, equal to the same standard pair near $t=0,1$. Such a pair exists on the rectangle $J\times I$: start with local transverse frames, extend them along the interval and then in time, and correct their terminal angle by a smooth rotation, equal to zero initially and to that angle terminally. The terminal angle has a smooth real lift on an interval. Regarding $S^3$ as the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^4$, use the explicit tube $(F_t(s)+u n_1(s,t)+v n_2(s,t))/\sqrt{1+u^2+v^2}$, with the two normals tangent to $S^3$. Its derivative is injective along the zero section. For uniformly small transverse coordinates it is an embedded tube; compactness gives a common width and excludes intersections with the rest of the knot outside the enlarged interval. Rounded end caps give a smooth family of embedded three-balls $b_t:B_*\to S^3$ about the cap, intersecting the knot in the chosen cap and its standard end collars. At the two stationary ends this family is the same specified ball chart: $b_0=b_1$. Apply [F1] to $b_t$ and, if necessary, a slightly larger ball chart, to get $H_t$ with $H_t b_0=b_t$. Then $G_t=H_t^{-1}F_t$ fixes the cap and its collar throughout. Its restriction to the complementary source interval is a proper-arc isotopy in the fixed $B=S^3\setminus\operatorname{Int}B_*$. At $t=0$ it is the first tangle; at $t=1$ it is $h$ applied to the second, where $h=H_1^{-1}|_B$ is a diffeomorphism equal to the identity on a boundary collar, because $b_1=b_0$ on the slightly larger ball. No identification of the terminal ball chart with an arbitrary initial chart has been assumed.

**Correct the terminal diffeomorphism on the arc.** Identify $B$ with the unit ball and choose the coordinate origin off the second compact arc $T$. The chart can have this property by a small interior change fixing its boundary collar. Since $h$ is the identity near the boundary, for $0<r\le1$ the maps $h_r(x)=\begin{cases}r h(x/r),&|x|\le r,\\ x,&|x|\ge r\end{cases}$ are smooth diffeomorphisms, agreeing smoothly at $|x|=r$, and equal to the identity on a fixed boundary collar. Put $h_0=1$. For $r$ less than the positive distance from the origin to $T$, $h_r|_T$ is exactly the identity. Thus $(s,r)\mapsto h_r(T(s))$ is a smooth isotopy of proper arcs even at $r=0$, although the ambient Alexander formula need not be smooth at $(x,r)=(0,0)$. Each slice is embedded, its endpoints and collars are fixed, and its final slice is $h(T)$. Reverse this arc isotopy and concatenate it with step 2.1, using stationary time changes at the join. The resulting smooth arc isotopy runs from the first tangle to the second relative to the same boundary endpoints and collars. This argument uses no claim that the diffeomorphism group of a three-ball is smoothly contractible.

**Projection and relative perturbations.** Choose the standard ball model as a rounded thickening of the projection disk, with the two fixed endpoint collars radial in that disk and with constant height. The rest of the compact arc track is in the interior of the ball. Shorten the protected collars if needed. Compactness then separates their projected endpoint neighbourhoods from every other branch: off a slightly larger source collar the radial coordinate in the disk is uniformly bounded away from its boundary. On the remaining transition collars the projection is still a fixed regular embedded arc. Reparametrize the isotopy in time to be stationary near its two regular end diagrams. In the finite-dimensional family of [F2], replace the time cutoff $\lambda(t)$ by $\lambda(t)\rho(s)$, where $\rho$ vanishes on the protected source collars and is positive on their complement. Embed the compact source rectangle in Euclidean space; multiplying coordinate polynomials of degree at most $43$ by this cutoff independently prescribes jets through order three at any at most six distinct free source points. Explicitly, at points $X_i$, the polynomials $\prod_{j\ne i}|X-X_j|^8$ times suitable cubic Taylor polynomials prescribe the required jets, since multiplication by the nonzero cutoff is invertible on jets. Keep the spatial height coordinate unchanged. Small parameters preserve slice embeddings by compact local immersion and distant-point separation, fix the time-end diagrams, and fix the protected endpoint collars. The collars meet no singular stratum, and the transition region is regular with no other projected branch, so absence of perturbations on the collars loses no needed transversality.

The equations $g_s=0$ have codimension two in $(s,t)$; the extra degeneracy $\det(g_{ss},g_{sss})=0$ has total codimension three and is avoided. Distinct-point equality has codimension two in $(s_1,s_2,t)$; equality plus tangent dependence has codimension three, giving isolated quadratic double tangencies with nonzero relative normal velocity. Triple equality has codimension four in $(s_1,s_2,s_3,t)$; adding tangent dependence or a vanishing derivative increases codimension and is avoided. Quadruple equality has codimension six in dimension five and is absent. Simultaneous distinct events have combined codimension larger than the shared-time configuration dimension; independent jets at up to six points exclude them. derivations.claim: The quotient by the monic polynomial $X^2$ is the free abelian group with basis $1,X$. The displayed multiplication is the quotient-ring multiplication, so it is associative, commutative, and has unit $1$. On this basis, $\epsilon$ and $\Delta$ satisfy both counit identities; explicitly, $(\epsilon\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(1)=1$, $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\epsilon)\Delta(1)=1$, and the same composites send $X$ to $X$.

Cocommutativity follows by swapping tensor factors in the two displayed values of $\Delta$. For coassociativity, both $(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(1)$ and $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Delta(1)$ equal $1\otimes X\otimes X+X\otimes1\otimes X+X\otimes X\otimes1$, and both composites send $X$ to $X\otimes X\otimes X$. Hence $(\mathcal A,m,\eta,\Delta,\epsilon)$ is a commutative Frobenius algebra once the Frobenius compatibility is checked.

On the ordered basis $1\otimes1,1\otimes X,X\otimes1,X\otimes X$ of $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$, each of $(m\otimes\mathrm{id})(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)$, $\Delta m$, and $(\mathrm{id}\otimes m)(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})$ has respective outputs $1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, $X\otimes X$, $X\otimes X$, and $0$. Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

**Input:** a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ and a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on its crossing set. A diagram object is supplied as mathematical input; this procedure does not parse a serialized string.

**Output:** the normalized bigraded Khovanov cochain module $C^{i,j}(D)$ and its candidate differential $d:C^{i,j}(D)\to C^{i+1,j}(D)$, constructed by the following finite instructions.

1. Enumerate every state $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$ once. Form the crossingless resolution by using the A-smoothing at $v(c)=0$ and the B-smoothing at $v(c)=1$.
2. For each state, create one tensor factor of the integral Frobenius algebra for each resolution circle and place the resulting tensor product in cohomological degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum degree $|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$ for its circle labels $a$.
3. For each state and each crossing $c_j$ with $v(c_j)=0$, create the edge to $v+e_j$. Apply multiplication if that smoothing change merges two circles, comultiplication if it splits one circle, the identity on other tensor factors, and the sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. Sum the edge maps out of every state to obtain $d$.
4. Return the finite direct sum of the state modules with these degrees and maps. The square-zero property is the separate local lemma named by `justified_by`.

derivations.claim: Fix a state $v$ and two distinct coordinates $i<j$ with $v(c_i)=v(c_j)=0$. The two length-two paths from $v$ to $v+e_i+e_j$ induce equal unsigned maps: saddles on disjoint circles commute as tensor maps; when the two saddles meet one component, the three possible merge/split patterns give respectively associativity, coassociativity, or one of the two equal Frobenius composites in [F1]. These are all possibilities because each edge changes one smoothing by one saddle.

The sign on the path that changes $i$ then $j$ has exponent $\sum_{r<i}v(c_r)+\sum_{r<j}v(c_r)+1$, while the path that changes $j$ then $i$ has exponent $\sum_{r<j}v(c_r)+\sum_{r<i}v(c_r)$. Their signs are opposite, so the two equal unsigned composites from step 1.1 cancel in the sum defining the component of $d^2$ from $v$ to $v+e_i+e_j$. If there are fewer than two crossings, no length-two paths occur and $d^2$ is the empty sum; otherwise every term of $d^2$ lies in exactly one such pair. Hence $d^2=0$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

At each resolution state, let $X_p$ act by multiplication by $X$ on the tensor factor for the circle containing $p$, and by the identity on every other circle factor. The basepoint action is the direct sum of these statewise maps. Define the reduced cochain complex by
$$\widetilde C(D,p):=C(D)/\operatorname{im}(X_p),$$
with the same cohomological grading and with reduced quantum degree $\widetilde j=j-1$ for the class represented by a state whose basepoint circle is labelled $1$. Its cohomology is the reduced integral Khovanov cohomology $\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(D,p)$. The unknot is normalized so that its reduced group lies in bidegree $(0,0)$.

A resolution with $k$ closed circles and the distinguished interval is assigned $\mathcal A^{\otimes k}\otimes M$. An edge that merges a circle into the interval uses $m_M(1\otimes1)=1$ and $m_M(X\otimes1)=0$; an edge that splits the interval uses $\Delta_M(1)=X\otimes1$, where the circle factor is written first and the interval factor second. Edges not meeting the interval use $m$ or $\Delta$. This based tangle cube is the quotient complex above, with the stated quantum shift.

The image after tensoring is $\operatorname{im}(d)\otimes\mathbb Q$ by clearing denominators, so rationalized homology is $H^i(C)\otimes\mathbb Q$ and has dimension $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}H^i(C)$. Rank-nullity in this bounded rational complex gives $\dim C^i=\dim H^i+\dim\operatorname{im}d^i+\dim\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$; alternating over $i$ cancels the image dimensions. On a state $v$, summing $q^{\sum\deg(a)}$ over its $k(v)$ independent labels gives $(q+q^{-1})^{k(v)}$, so the unreduced chain Euler sum is $\sum_v(-1)^{|v|-n_-}q^{|v|+n_+-2n_-}(q+q^{-1})^{k(v)}$. These are the exact tensor interpretations of the local neck-cutting identities, including when two dot positions are on the same circle.

**An explicit cancellation rule.** Suppose a differential between consecutive degrees has block matrix $\begin{pmatrix}\phi&\beta\\ \gamma&\delta\end{pmatrix}:A_0\oplus R\to B_0\oplus S$, with $\phi$ an isomorphism. Set $L(a,r)=(a+\phi^{-1}\beta r,r)$ and $T(b,s)=(b,s-\gamma\phi^{-1}b)$. These invertible integral changes of coordinates give $T d L^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(\phi,\delta-\gamma\phi^{-1}\beta)$. Conjugate the adjacent differentials too. The equation $d^2=0$ and invertibility of $\phi$ imply that the incoming differential has zero $A_0$ coordinate and the outgoing differential vanishes on $B_0$. Thus there is a direct summand $A_0\xrightarrow{\phi}B_0$, contracted by $h|_{B_0}=\phi^{-1}$, $h=0$ elsewhere. Inclusion and projection of the remaining coordinates, conjugated by $L,T$, are chain maps $i,p$ with $pi=1$ and $1-ip=dh+hd$. Introduce four precisely located saddles: $u:E_1\to P$ inserts $E_2$ below $E_1$, $v:E_2\to P$ inserts $E_1$ above $E_2$, $w:E_1\to Q$ inserts $E_2$ above $E_1$, and $z:E_2\to Q$ inserts $E_1$ below $E_2$. Let $x$ and $y$ be the dot operators on the bottom cup and top cap of $E_1$, respectively. The degree-one differential is $d^1(a,b,c)=(-ua+vb,\ -xa+yc,\ -a+c,\ wc-zb),$ with output coordinates $(P,W_1,W_X,Q)$. Indeed the six cube edges are $100\to110$ with sign $-$, $010\to110$ with sign $+$, $100\to101$ with sign $-$, $001\to101$ with sign $+$, $010\to011$ with sign $-$, and $001\to011$ with sign $+$. The two edges to $101$ split the middle circle from the bottom cup or top cap, giving exactly the two displayed circle-coordinate pairs by step 2.1. The $101\to111$ edge has sign $-$ and merges that middle circle into the remaining through arc of $E_1E_2E_1$. Cancel it by step 2.2: its row is $-a+c$, so the residual coordinate substitution is $c=a$. The retained degree-one coordinates are $(a,b)$, the retained degree-two coordinates are $(P,Q)$, and the differentials become $I\xrightarrow{\binom{s_1}{s_2}}E_1\oplus E_2\xrightarrow{\begin{pmatrix}-u&v\\ w&-z\end{pmatrix}}P\oplus Q,$ where $s_i:I\to E_i$ is the saddle inserting $E_i$. Its retained coordinates before reordering are $(E_2,E_1)$ and $(Q,P)$, with matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-z&w\\ v&-u\end{pmatrix}$. Swapping both pairs, without a sign, gives exactly the preceding matrix and the preceding $d^0$. The four entries refer to the same saddles on the same labelled boundary matchings: for instance $E_2\to P$ inserts $E_1$ above, and $E_1\to P$ inserts $E_2$ below, on both sides. Hence these are actual equal tensor maps by step 1.1, not identifications of unlabelled spaces. Their kernels, composites and signs need no further $\tau$ identities. Composing the two explicit cancellation maps and their inverses gives the RIII equivalence; the homotopy for a composite of retractions $(i_1,p_1,h_1)$ and $(i_2,p_2,h_2)$ is $h_1+i_1h_2p_1$.

In RII, $W_1$ has the underlying grading of $E$ increased by two, $W_X$ has the grading of $E$, and $Z$ has the grading of $E$ increased by two. **Exterior differentials and the marked quotient.** Dots commute with every exterior saddle: $m(Xa,b)=Xm(a,b)=m(a,Xb)$ and $\Delta(Xa)=(X\otimes1)\Delta(a)=(1\otimes X)\Delta(a)$. A middle circle being delooped is contained in the local disk, so no exterior saddle meets it. Boundary-fixing isotopies of the matchings preserve the labelled exterior arcs. All matrix changes, inverses of $\pm1$ blocks, projections, inclusions and contractions above therefore commute with unsigned exterior saddles and with $X$ at a fixed exterior marked point. A local homotopy lowers $r$ by one, so its two exterior terms in $dh+hd$ cancel; local degree-zero maps commute with the signed total differential. These identities prove the same retractions for the total cube. The identities descend modulo $\operatorname{im}X_p$ because every map and every homotopy commutes with $X_p$; this argument does not assume that every local saddle acts trivially on the distinguished interval. It proves all assertions, integrally and choice-free.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

Let $(D,p)$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a knot with a basepoint $p$ away from the crossings, and let $C(D)$ be its normalized integral Khovanov cochain complex. At each resolution state, let $X_p$ act by multiplication by $X$ on the tensor factor for the circle containing $p$, and by the identity on every other circle factor. The basepoint action is the direct sum of these statewise maps. Define the reduced cochain complex by
$$\widetilde C(D,p):=C(D)/\operatorname{im}(X_p),$$
with the same cohomological grading and with reduced quantum degree $\widetilde j=j-1$ for the class represented by a state whose basepoint circle is labelled $1$. Its cohomology is the reduced integral Khovanov cohomology $\widetilde{Kh}^{i,\widetilde j}(D,p)$. The unknot is normalized so that its reduced group lies in bidegree $(0,0)$.

Equivalently, cut the based knot at $p$ to a one-interval tangle. Put $M=\mathbb Z$ in quantum degree $0$ with $X\cdot1=0$. A resolution with $k$ closed circles and the distinguished interval is assigned $\mathcal A^{\otimes k}\otimes M$. An edge that merges a circle into the interval uses $m_M(1\otimes1)=1$ and $m_M(X\otimes1)=0$; an edge that splits the interval uses $\Delta_M(1)=X\otimes1$, where the circle factor is written first and the interval factor second. Edges not meeting the interval use $m$ or $\Delta$. This based tangle cube is the quotient complex above, with the stated quantum shift.

The integral signed Khovanov cubes have the local graded cancellation models described below. They are chain homotopy equivalences over every fixed exterior resolution, commute with exterior saddle differentials, and commute with multiplication by $X$ at every marked point outside the local disk. Consequently they also give chain homotopy equivalences after taking the reduced quotient. For the crossing with A-smoothing the identity matching and B-smoothing the cap-cup matching, the two three-crossing braid cubes with words $121$ and $212$ retract to the same three-term complex. The two-crossing inverse-pair cube retracts to the identity matching in local cohomological degree one and quantum shift upward by one. All retractions are integral; their homotopies and the two cancellations in the three-crossing cube are specified in the proof.

Let $f:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ be a chain map in an additive category. The
**mapping cone** of $f$ is the chain complex $\operatorname{Cone}(f)_\bullet$
whose degree-$n$ term is
$$\operatorname{Cone}(f)_n:=D_n\oplus C[1]_n=D_n\oplus C_{n-1},$$
and whose differential is
$$d_n^{\operatorname{Cone}(f)}(y,x):=(d_n^D(y)+f_{n-1}(x),-d_{n-1}^C(x)).$$

Thus $\operatorname{Cone}(f)$ is the direct sum of $D$ and the shift $C[1]$ as
a graded object, with the off-diagonal term given by $f$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

derivations.claim: **Crossing order and planar isotopy.** Reordering adjacent crossing coordinates $a,b$ is corrected by the diagonal state factor $s(v)=(-1)^{v(a)v(b)}$: on an $a$-edge its ratio is $(-1)^{v(b)}$, and on a $b$-edge it is $(-1)^{v(a)}$, exactly the sign change from swapping their order. Thus local crossings can be ordered first, and can be restored to the original order afterward by explicit chain isomorphisms. A planar isotopy bijects labelled resolution circles and saddles, so its factor permutations give a grading-preserving chain isomorphism.

**The determinant sign of each curl.** A Reidemeister-I return joins one of the four adjacent endpoint pairs of [F7]. For the right-hand return choose the strand direction $SW\to NE\to SE\to NW$. At the crossing the over and under tangents are respectively $(1,1)$ and $(-1,1)$, whose determinant is $2>0$. A-smoothing closes the return $NE$--$SE$ into the small circle and leaves the left-hand continuing arc; B-smoothing has only the continuing arc. Thus this positive curl has the multiplication differential, small circle in local degree zero, used in the curl contraction. For the top return choose $SW\to NE\to NW\to SE$. The tangents are $(1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$, with determinant $-2<0$. B-smoothing closes the top return into the small circle while A-smoothing has only the continuing arc. Thus this negative curl has the comultiplication differential, small circle in local degree one. Rotation by $180$ degrees gives the left and bottom returns without changing A/B labels or determinant sign. Reversing the component direction negates both tangents and also leaves the determinant sign unchanged. These four return pairs and the two directions exhaust the oriented local R1 pictures; no orientation-reversing chart or reflection is used.

**Both curls, with natural contractions.** For a positive curl the local differential is multiplication from a small circle and a continuing arc. Put the small-circle factor first, denote the dot on the continuing arc by $x$, and use coordinates $1\otimes u+X\otimes v$. The map is $(u,v)\mapsto u+xv$. Its $1$-label component is the identity; cancel it, leaving $v\mapsto X\otimes v-1\otimes xv$ in degree zero. Equivalently this is $j=\Delta-\jmath m\Delta$, with $\jmath(v)=1\otimes v$; it sends $1$ to $X\otimes1-1\otimes X$ and $X$ to $X\otimes X$. The canceled pair has inverse identity, so its contraction is the explicit cancellation rule of [F5], agreeing with the cochain identity-cone contraction in [F6]. For a continuing generator of quantum degree $d$, both terms of this survivor have raw quantum degree $d-1$ and local cohomological degree zero, so the raw quantum shift is $\{1\}$ in the stated lowering convention. Thus its raw shifts are exactly $[-1]\{-2\}$. These descriptions commute with exterior saddles because the dot and the local saddle commute with them by the displayed Frobenius identities; they therefore contract the total complexes, including exterior differentials with their totalization signs. The additional normalizations are $\{-1\}$ for a positive curl and $[1]\{2\}$ for a negative curl, canceling the respective raw shifts.

Thus the two canceled pairs are actual contractible summands over the integral exterior cube and the surviving identity matching is in local degree one with quantum increase one. This is precisely the raw shift $[-1]\{-1\}$ in the Statement. An RII pair has one positive and one negative crossing, so its normalization changes by $[1]\{1\}$ and cancels that shift. A quadratic tangency has two branches which are both graphs over their common tangent direction; orienting these graphs temporarily in the same direction puts every underlying RII picture into this model or the opposite crossing order. Reversing either actual strand arrow only changes crossing signs, still one of each, and does not change the A/B maps. Step 2.2 shows that $Q_i=N_i[1]\{1\}$ is a two-sided inverse of $P_i$ up to local chain homotopy; the contractions are natural under adjoining other crossings. Thus the relation $aba\simeq bab$, with $a=P_1,b=P_2$, also gives the relations with exponent triples $---$, $++-$, $-++$, $+--$ and $--+$, interpreting negative exponents by these explicit inverses. The $---$ relation is the inverse relation; $aba^{-1}\simeq b^{-1}ab$ follows by multiplication on the left by $b^{-1}$ and on the right by $a^{-1}$; $a^{-1}ba\simeq bab^{-1}$ follows by multiplication on the left by $a^{-1}$ and on the right by $b^{-1}$; their inverses give $+--$ and $--+$. The crossings concern the pairs of strands $AB,AC,BC$, respectively; a strict height order has precisely the six transitive sign patterns just listed, excluding the two cyclic patterns $+-+$ and $-+-$. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $D$ and $D'$ be regular oriented link diagrams.
Then $D$ and $D'$ represent equivalent oriented links if and only if $D'$ can be
obtained from $D$ by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented
Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3.

Let $D,D'$ be finite regular oriented link diagrams related by a planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move. Let $\bar C(D)$ be the integral signed state cube before the writhe shifts, with cohomological degree $|v|$ and quantum degree $|v|+\sum\deg(a)$, and normalize it by $C(D)=\bar C(D)[n_-]\{2n_--n_+\}$ to obtain the state degrees $i=|v|-n_-$ and $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$. Before normalization, a positive type-I curl gives $\bar C(D_+)\simeq\bar C(D)\{1\}$, a negative type-I curl gives $\bar C(D_-)\simeq\bar C(D)[-1]\{-2\}$, a type-II move gives $\bar C(D_{II})\simeq\bar C(D)[-1]\{-1\}$, and a type-III move gives an unshifted equivalence. Consequently the normalized complexes are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent. If $D,D'$ are based knot diagrams and the move disk is disjoint from the basepoint, the same chain homotopy equivalence descends to their reduced quotient complexes, equivalently to the cut-tangle complexes with interval module $M=\mathbb Z$, $X\cdot1=0$.

For a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ with $n$ ordered crossings, the procedure that enumerates all $2^n$ smoothing states, assigns one copy of $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ per resolution circle, places a generator in degrees $i=|v|-n_-$ and $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$, and sums the signed merge or split edge maps terminates after finitely many operations. Its output is a finite direct sum of finite-rank free abelian groups with a differential of bidegree $(1,0)$ satisfying $d^2=0$; hence it is a bounded bigraded cochain complex.

A chain map $f:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ is a **chain homotopy equivalence** if
there exists a chain map $g:D_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ such that
$$g\circ f\simeq1_C,\qquad f\circ g\simeq1_D.$$

Such a map $g$ is called a **homotopy inverse** of $f$.

The normalization in that supplier cancels the raw shifts, so these maps have bidegree $(0,0)$.

A chain map takes cocycles to cocycles and coboundaries to coboundaries. If two chain maps differ by $dh+hd$, their values on a cocycle differ by a coboundary, so they induce the same cohomology map. Thus each equivalence in step 1.1 gives mutually inverse maps in every bidegree. Composing the finitely many induced isomorphisms identifies the cohomology of $C(D)$ and $C(D')$. It follows that the groups $Kh^{i,j}(L)$ are independent of the chosen diagram up to bigraded isomorphism. The empty sequence gives the identity, and no assertion of a canonical isomorphism for all move sequences is needed.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Assume countable choice. Let $(D,p)$ and $(D',p')$ be finite regular diagrams of the same oriented smooth knot, with marks away from crossings. Remove a small open arc about each mark and regard each complementary diagram as a one-interval tangle diagram in a disk, using the complementary disk in the projection sphere. Identify their two boundary endpoints and short oriented product collars. The resulting proper arcs can be realized in one standard smooth three-ball so that they are smoothly isotopic with those endpoints and collars fixed. Their diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves supported away from those collars. This holds when the two diagrams coincide and only the mark has moved along the knot.

Let $D,D'$ be finite regular oriented link diagrams related by a planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move. Let $\bar C(D)$ be the integral signed state cube before the writhe shifts, with cohomological degree $|v|$ and quantum degree $|v|+\sum\deg(a)$, and normalize it by $C(D)=\bar C(D)[n_-]\{2n_--n_+\}$ to obtain the state degrees $i=|v|-n_-$ and $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$. Before normalization, a positive type-I curl gives $\bar C(D_+)\simeq\bar C(D)\{1\}$, a negative type-I curl gives $\bar C(D_-)\simeq\bar C(D)[-1]\{-2\}$, a type-II move gives $\bar C(D_{II})\simeq\bar C(D)[-1]\{-1\}$, and a type-III move gives an unshifted equivalence. Consequently the normalized complexes are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent. If $D,D'$ are based knot diagrams and the move disk is disjoint from the basepoint, the same chain homotopy equivalence descends to their reduced quotient complexes, equivalently to the cut-tangle complexes with interval module $M=\mathbb Z$, $X\cdot1=0$.

Let $C_\bullet,D_\bullet$ be chain complexes in an abelian category
$\mathcal A$, and let $f,g:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ be chain maps. A **chain homotopy**
$s:f\simeq g$ is a graded morphism of degree $1$,
$$s_n:C_n\to D_{n+1},$$
such that for every $n\in\mathbb Z$,
$$f_n-g_n=d^D_{n+1}s_n+s_{n-1}d^C_n.$$

Equivalently, $f-g$ is the degree-$0$ boundary of the degree-$1$ family $s$ in
[[def-hom-complex-of-chain-complexes]].

A chain map $f:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ is a **chain homotopy equivalence** if
there exists a chain map $g:D_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ such that
$$g\circ f\simeq1_C,\qquad f\circ g\simeq1_D.$$

Such a map $g$ is called a **homotopy inverse** of $f$.

Closing the boundary collars by the same crossing-free cap recovers the two based diagrams. In each resolution this closure replaces the distinguished interval by the based circle and adds no crossing, so it preserves $n_+,n_-$, cohomological degree and reduced quantum degree. The quotient/interval identification is the one proved in the defining reduced-complex item.

Every interior R1, R2 or R3 in the movie avoids the distinguished end collars. By [F4], its chain maps and contractions descend to the reduced quotient. citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented diagram of a link with $n_+$ positive crossings, $n_-$ negative crossings, writhe $w=n_+-n_-$, and $n=n_++n_-$. For each resolution state $v$, let $k(v)$ be its number of circles and let $D_v$ use the A-smoothing at coordinates $0$ and B-smoothing at coordinates $1$. Put $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ and define the normalized bracket
$$f_D(A):=(-A^3)^{-w}\sum_{v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}} A^{n-2|v|}\delta^{k(v)-1}.$$
For the unreduced cohomology, define $\chi_q(Kh(D))=\sum_{i,j}(-1)^i\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}Kh^{i,j}(D)q^j$. Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

An **oriented Reidemeister move** is one of the following local replacements of
a regular oriented link diagram ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]),
performed inside a small closed disk while the diagram outside the disk is left
unchanged, and understood up to planar isotopy outside the disk
([[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]]). All sign and orientation variants of
each local picture are included.

**(R1) Kink creation and deletion.** A single strand is replaced by a small
kink: two arcs crossing once and otherwise disjoint from the strand, with the
over/under datum of the new crossing as in the picture. The move is allowed in
both directions (create or delete the kink) and with both signs of the kink,
the sign being the sign of the crossing created. The orientations of the two
strands of the kink are the two possible consistent orientations through the
crossing, and all of them occur in the move list.

**(R2) Slide of two strands.** Two local arcs belonging to two strands are
replaced so that the number of crossings between those strands changes by two
of opposite signs: the standard picture slides one strand over or under the
other, creating or deleting the pair of crossings, with the two crossings being
the two possible signs in either order. All four orientation patterns of the
two strands at the two crossings are included.

**(R3) Sliding a strand past a crossing.** One strand is moved across an
existing crossing of two other strands, so that the crossing of the two other
strands passes from one side of the moving strand to the other; the three
crossings of the local picture keep their signs and the over/under data are
preserved. The three strands must have a consistent strict height order:
one is above both others, one below both, and the remaining strand is between
them. The cyclic over/under pattern is excluded. Every orientation pattern
and all six height orders of this standard local picture are included.

A local R2 or R3 picture is **braid-like** when, after a local coordinate
change and deformation, all participating strands run in the same positive
longitudinal direction. This is a local condition and does not require a
globally chosen braid axis. R1 is kept as a separate kink move.

The strands keep their orientations throughout every move. The union of the
three move types, together with planar isotopy, generates the equivalence
relation on diagrams used in the Reidemeister equivalence theorem below; the
moves are sometimes called R1, R2, R3 as above. Since every move changes the
diagram only inside a disk, it has a type and a finite list of local
orientation/sign variants, and each variant is realized by an ambient isotopy
as the next items show. The complete list of variants is required because the
Markov and Alexander constructions below act on oriented diagrams and count
signed crossings.

Let $D,D'$ be regular oriented diagrams of links $L,L'$. If the diagrams
differ by one oriented Reidemeister move or a planar isotopy, the links are
equivalent. The local Reidemeister replacement has a realization supported
in a ball over its move disk, after choosing lifts that agree outside that
ball. Comparing arbitrary realizing links may additionally require changing
their heights away from the move disk.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram, order its crossings as $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and form the direct sum of state modules $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$ over all functions $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$. Here $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, each crossing is changed from its A-smoothing at $0$ to its B-smoothing at $1$, and the edge map is the multiplication $m$ for a merge or comultiplication $\Delta$ for a split, multiplied by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$ on the edge at $c_j$. Then the sum $d$ of all edge maps satisfies $d^2=0$.

For a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ with $n$ ordered crossings, the procedure that enumerates all $2^n$ smoothing states, assigns one copy of $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ per resolution circle, places a generator in degrees $i=|v|-n_-$ and $j=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$, and sums the signed merge or split edge maps terminates after finitely many operations. Its output is a finite direct sum of finite-rank free abelian groups with a differential of bidegree $(1,0)$ satisfying $d^2=0$; hence it is a bounded bigraded cochain complex.

In the positive curl, the $0$-state contributes $(q+q^{-1})^2$ and the $1$-state contributes $-q(q+q^{-1})$, because the state coordinate raises quantum degree by one and homological degree by one. Hence $\chi_q^{\mathrm{raw}}(U_+)=(q+q^{-1})^2-q(q+q^{-1})=1+q^{-2}=q^{-1}(q+q^{-1})$. In the negative curl, the $0$-state contributes $q+q^{-1}$ and the $1$-state contributes $-q(q+q^{-1})^2$. Hence $\chi_q^{\mathrm{raw}}(U_-)=(q+q^{-1})-q(q+q^{-1})^2=-q^3-q=-q^2(q+q^{-1})$. These computations use only the state modules and gradings before the writhe normalization.

For each quantum degree, tensor the bounded finite-rank free complex with $\mathbb Q$. Clearing denominators shows that kernels and images localize to the kernels and images of the rationalized maps; applying the same argument to a kernel modulo the preceding image identifies rationalized cohomology with integral cohomology tensored with $\mathbb Q$. Its dimension is therefore the integral rank of cohomology. In the bounded rational complex, rank-nullity gives $\dim C^i=\dim H^i+\dim\operatorname{im}d^i+\dim\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$; alternating over $i$ cancels the image terms. Thus the raw cohomology Euler polynomials equal the chain Euler polynomials in steps 1.1–1.2. The distinct Laurent polynomials $q+q^{-1}$, $q^{-1}(q+q^{-1})$, and $-q^2(q+q^{-1})$ come from diagrams of the same unknot by [F4]. The raw groups are consequently not invariant, and the raw unknot factor is not the claimed $q+q^{-1}$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $D,D'$ be regular oriented link diagrams
([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]), regarded as decorated immersed oriented
$4$-valent planar graphs. Then $D$ and $D'$ are **planar isotopic** when there
is an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy
$\Phi\colon\mathbb R^2\times I\to\mathbb R^2$, with $\Phi_0=\mathrm{id}$ and
each $\Phi_t$ an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]), such that
$\Phi_1$ carries the decorated graph of $D$ to that of $D'$: it maps the image
curve of $D$ bijectively onto that of $D'$, carries the over/under datum of
every double point to the over/under datum of the corresponding double point,
and preserves the strand orientations. A **planar isotopy of diagrams** is a
family $D_t=\Phi_t(D_0)$ for such a jointly smooth ambient isotopy $\Phi$,
with the decorations transported by $\Phi_t$. The source curves are immersed,
not embedded in the plane at their crossings.

Planar isotopies are admitted as moves in the Reidemeister theorem: they carry
a regular projection between the exceptional times of a general-position
isotopy of the link, and no crossing of the diagram is created or destroyed
along them. They are listed separately from the three local moves
([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]), of which R1 and R2 create or destroy crossings, while R3 rearranges three
existing crossings and preserves their number.
Composing planar isotopies and composing them with the local moves gives the
equivalence relation generated by the moves, and every single move below is
understood up to planar isotopy outside its small disk.

derivations.claim: **Straighten only a crossing-free marked germ.** Translate the mark to $z=0$ and rotate its oriented tangent to the positive real axis, by paths of positive planar similarities. Since the mark is a regular non-double point, there is a small disk meeting the diagram in just one arc. The inverse-function theorem expresses that arc as $y=f(x)$, where $f(0)=f'(0)=0$. It can be straightened by the supported shear $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y-t\chi(x,y)f(x))$, $0\le t\le1$: choose a cutoff equal to one near the smaller graph segment and supported in a rectangle of width and height comparable to a sufficiently small $r$. There $f(x)=O(r^2)$, whereas $\partial_y\chi=O(r^{-1})$. Thus $1-t(\partial_y\chi)f>0$ after shrinking $r$. Each vertical coordinate map is strictly increasing and the identity outside a compact interval, so each shear is a global orientation-preserving diffeomorphism; its inverse is smooth by its positive vertical derivative. Choose nested neighborhoods so that after this shear the diagram in $|z|<2r$ is the real diameter and no other strand meets that disk. Shrink $r<1$ if necessary. The part not in the real interval $|x|<r$ consequently satisfies $|z|\ge r$. All these isotopies merely transport the mark and crossing decorations; their local supports meet no crossing.

**An actual rotation recharting.** Choose $0<\epsilon<\min(r/4,1/4)$ and set $a=i\epsilon$. On the oriented stereographic sphere use the fractional linear coordinate $$w=-\frac{1+\overline a z}{z-a}.$$ The matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-\overline a&-1\\1&-a\end{smallmatrix}\right)/\sqrt{1+|a|^2}$ is unitary with determinant one: its columns have norm one and scalar product zero, and its unnormalized determinant is $1+|a|^2$. Hence its fractional linear action is the action of an orientation-preserving rotation of the round two-sphere. Its omitted old point is $a$, which lies off the real germ in the marked disk, hence in a face adjacent to the mark and outside all crossing disks. The old omitted point $\infty$ is sent to $-\overline a$, which is an ordinary point of the new chart. The map is smooth on the entire spherical diagram and preserves the oriented local crossing charts and all transported decorations.

**A quantitative exterior closing arc.** For every old diagram point outside the interval $|x|<r$, step 1.1 and the triangle inequality give $$|w|\le\frac{1+\epsilon|z|}{|z|-\epsilon}\le B:=\frac{1+\epsilon r}{r-\epsilon}.$$ The second inequality holds because the rational function has derivative $-(1+\epsilon^2)/(s-\epsilon)^2<0$ for $s\ge r$. The inequality $B<1/\epsilon$ is equivalent to $2\epsilon<r(1-\epsilon^2)$, which follows from $\epsilon<r/4$ and $\epsilon<1/4$. Choose a real $R$ strictly between $B$ and $1/\epsilon$. On the real germ $$|w(x)|^2=\frac{1+\epsilon^2x^2}{x^2+\epsilon^2},$$ whose derivative with respect to $x^2$ is $(\epsilon^4-1)/(x^2+\epsilon^2)^2<0$. Since the value at $x=0$ is $1/\epsilon^2>R^2$ and at $|x|=r$ is at most $B^2<R^2$, the circle $|w|=R$ meets that germ at exactly $x=\pm c$, with $$c^2=\frac{1-R^2\epsilon^2}{R^2-\epsilon^2},\qquad 0<c<r.$$ Both intersections are transverse, since $c\ne0$ and the derivative just computed is nonzero there. The only diagram points outside the closed disk $|w|\le R$ form the single open arc parametrized by $-c<x<c$; its closure contains the mark and has no crossing. The image is a round circular arc, because a fractional linear map sends a circle on the sphere to a circle and its pole $i\epsilon$ is not on the real circle. Every other strand and every crossing is strictly inside the disk. Thus this is the claimed exterior closing arc, with uniform crossing-free neighborhoods of it and of its two cut points.

**Record spatial coordinate identifications.** A planar shear in step 1.1 lifts on a spatial projection chart by $(x,y,h)\mapsto(\Phi_t(x,y),h)$. Its compact planar support can also be cut off in height on a larger box containing the link: use its compactly supported time-dependent planar velocity multiplied by a height cutoff equal to one on that box, with zero height velocity. The flow is complete, agrees with the displayed lift near the link, and extends by the identity to $S^3$. The initial translations and rotations have their usual orientation-preserving similarity lifts and smooth conformal extensions at the point at infinity. For the rechart, realize the projection sphere as the equator of $S^3\subset\mathbb R^3\oplus\mathbb R$. If $Q\in SO(3)$ is the rotation from step 2.1, then $(v,s)\mapsto(Qv,s)$ is an orthogonal determinant-one map of $\mathbb R^4$ preserving $S^3$ and preserving its orientation. On the equatorial collar it transports the projection direction, the signed height, and the over/under datum. The Euclidean projection and the equatorial product projection require an explicit chart identification. Write $q=(0,0,1,0)$ for the spatial stereographic point, $z=x+iy$, $$X(z)=\frac{(2x,2y,|z|^2-1)}{1+|z|^2},\qquad d(z)=\frac{2}{1+|z|^2}.$$ Standard inverse spatial stereographic projection is $$E(z,h)=\frac{(2x,2y,|z|^2+h^2-1,2h)}{1+|z|^2+h^2}.$$ The product-collar chart with the same first normal derivative is $$T(z,h)=\bigl(\sqrt{1-d(z)^2h^2}\,X(z),d(z)h\bigr).$$ On $h=0$ these charts agree and have identical full first derivatives: both normal derivatives are $d(z)e_4$, while their tangential derivatives are those of $X$. On a compact planar neighborhood containing the diagram, the coordinate transition $\Psi=E^{-1}T$ therefore satisfies $\Psi-\mathrm{id}=O(h^2)$ and $D\Psi-I=O(|h|)$ uniformly. Choose a slightly larger compact planar box and cut off this difference there and in a height slab $|h|<\eta$. A height cutoff has derivative $O(\eta^{-1})$, multiplying an error $O(\eta^2)$; thus the resulting global compactly supported displacement $V$ has $\|DV\|<1/2$ for small $\eta$. Every $\mathrm{id}+tV$ is injective by the Lipschitz bound, is a local orientation-preserving diffeomorphism, and is onto: it is proper, its image is closed and open, and the plane-height space is connected. Its inverse is smooth by the inverse-function theorem. This is an actual ambient coordinate isotopy, extending by the identity to $S^3$. First shrink any existing Euclidean height realization by a positive constant so it lies where both cutoffs equal one. Height scaling is an embedding isotopy: at every double point both branch heights are multiplied by the same positive factor. The new spatial representative is then exactly $T(z,h)$, with product-collar base coordinate $z$ and signed height $d(z)h$. Because $d(z)>0$, at a double point it preserves the strict over/under ordering. Hence the displayed Euclidean diagram is identified with the product-collar diagram by this explicit spatial map; they are not assumed literally equal off the equator. These are actual marked link isotopies and coordinate identifications with specified endpoints. Composing these coordinate maps and height isotopies gives the asserted spatial identification; no claim that the rotation is a planar isotopy is used.

**Compatibility with protected long ends.** The exterior arc and two slightly longer joining collars have injective projection and are disjoint in projection from the remaining compact part, except at their adjacent ends. On a narrow planar neighborhood of that arc its spatial height is a smooth function $h(x,y)$, extended from the arc in tubular coordinates. A supported vertical translation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(x,y,z-t\eta(x,y)h(x,y))$ sets its height to zero on a smaller neighborhood; this is a diffeomorphism for every $t$, since its derivative in $z$ is one. It cannot reverse an over/under ordering, and there are no double points in its smaller marked support. Choose the joining neighborhoods slightly longer before cutting, so the resulting cut collars are fixed smooth product collars. The remaining diagram is a compact tangle in the round disk, and the single planar exterior arc is its marked closure. These are precisely endpoint data that may be retained as protected long endpoints in a relative movie construction. Every operation has preserved the transported mark, and none passes it through a crossing. Finite composition proves the assertion, including its recorded spatial coordinate identification. No algebraic comparison of the two charts, no arbitrary mark-slide identity, and no purely planar comparison have been assumed.

citations.quote: Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram with at least one component, ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and a marked point $p$ on the projected link away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.
