The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented collared embedded annulus from a knot $K_0$ to a knot $K_1$. Let $\gamma\subset S$ be a smooth properly embedded arc joining their specified marked points and equal to their vertical marked intervals in smaller end collars. There exist based regular diagrams representing these endpoint knots and a finite oriented movie between them, consisting of planar isotopies, R1, R2, R3, births, saddles and deaths, with a marked point in every frame. The marked track is strictly increasing in height, never dies, never lies at a diagram crossing, and misses the closed support disks of every exceptional move. Every regular interval also keeps a neighborhood of the mark fixed in its chosen diagram coordinates.

More precisely, first an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller end collars carries the given marked surface to one with monotone marked arc. A smooth level-preserving change of spatial coordinates then puts a neighborhood of that arc into a fixed exterior closing-arc position. The movie trace, transported back by those same coordinates, is ambient isotopic to the original marked $S$ relative to the smaller end collars. Its endpoint diagrams and their marked parametrizations use the corresponding endpoint coordinate identifications. One may retain prescribed endpoint diagrams already in this compatible long-tangle presentation. The conclusion does not assert a based Reidemeister sequence between arbitrary prescribed planar endpoint diagrams or between arbitrary basepoint presentations, and asserts no movie-independence theorem for algebraic maps.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:C\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be a smooth
isotopy of a finite disjoint union of circles, constant near both ends, and
suppose both end projections under the fixed $\pi$ are regular. Arbitrarily
close to $F$ in the strong smooth topology there is such an isotopy $F'$, equal
to $F$ near the ends, whose projected slices have only these exceptional events:

(i) finitely many ordinary cusps, at distinct times; in a source coordinate
$x$, writing $g(x,t)=\pi F'(x,t)$, each satisfies
$g_x=0$, $\det(g_{xx},g_{xt})\ne0$ and
$\det(g_{xx},g_{xxx})\ne0$;

(ii) the **off-diagonal unordered** double-point locus is a smooth
one-dimensional manifold with boundary in the local-extension sense of
[[def-smooth-chart-atlas-and-structure-on-a-manifold-with-boundary]]; its boundary
consists exactly of the double points at $t=0,1$. Its interior is a manifold
without boundary, and its time projection has only finitely many
nondegenerate critical points, each an ordinary quadratic tangency of two
immersed branches;

(iii) finitely many transverse triple events, with all three pairs of
projected tangents independent, and no quadruple points.

No two exceptional events have the same time. All other slices are regular,
and between exceptional times their decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy.

Let $F'$ satisfy the general-position conditions of
[[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-links-can-be-put-in-general-position]], with
exceptional times $t_1<\cdots<t_N$. Immediately before and after each event,
its regular diagrams differ, up to planar isotopy, by one oriented
Reidemeister move: R1 at an ordinary cusp, R2 at a quadratic double tangency,
and R3 at a transverse triple event. The regular intervals contribute planar
isotopies, and the moves preserve the over/under and orientation data of $F'$.
Consequently the end diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of these moves.

derivations.claim: **Small marked arcs and their relative center–tangent data.** Parametrize a uniformly small marked interval by oriented arclength $v$ near zero, smoothly in the isotopy parameter $t$; the resulting reparametrization changes neither knot nor mark and is stationary in the end collars. Let $b(t)=F(0,t)$ and let $u(t)$ be its unit tangent. Identify $S^3$ with unit quaternions. The imaginary unit quaternion $c(t)=b(t)^{-1}u(t)$ lies in $S^2$, and $(b(t),c(t))$ is a smooth loop in $S^3\times S^2$, constant in the end collars. The two endpoint marked arcs are the same by hypothesis. In exponential coordinates at $b(t)$ the small actual arc has the form $vu(t)+O(v^2)$, with derivative $u(t)+O(v)$ uniformly in $t$. Interpolating its error to zero gives a smooth family of embedded intervals for a sufficiently small uniform width: projection onto $u(t)$ has strictly positive derivative. This interpolation is stationary in the end collars if their common model is taken to be the geodesic round arc, as stipulated. Its inverse will later restore the actual marked germ.

**An explicit contraction fixes both parameter ends.** A smooth loop in either $S^d$, $d=2,3$, misses a point. Indeed a derivative bound makes its $n$ equal parameter intervals map into $n$ balls of radius $C/n$; their total spherical $d$-volume is at most $C'n^{1-d}$, which tends to zero. They cannot cover the positive-volume sphere. Choose one omitted point for each of the two loops from step 1.1. Stereographic coordinates from those points send each loop into Euclidean space. The straight interpolation from its constant endpoint value to its value at $t$ contracts it through loops constant on the same end collars; inverse stereographic projection gives smooth loops $b_s(t),c_s(t)$, with $s=0$ constant and $s=1$ the given data. Thus $$A_{s,t}(v)=b_s(t)\bigl(\cos v+c_s(t)\sin v\bigr)$$ is a smooth family of geodesic marked interval embeddings, with $A_{0,t}$ the common standard arc and $A_{s,t}$ equal to it in both end collars. Concatenate with the inverse error interpolation in step 1.1, using stationary smooth parameter joins. This constructs a two-parameter family of embedded intervals from the constant common arc to the actual moving marked arcs; at $t$ in either end collar the entire family is the constant arc.

**Relative ambient coordinates really are identity at both ends.** Extend the velocity in the contraction parameter $s$ of step 2.1 by the actual construction in [F1], with $t$ an additional parameter. To spell out the relative point: the track in $S^3\times[0,1]_s\times[0,1]_t$ is embedded because its last two coordinates retain $s,t$ and each interval slice is embedded. In finite track charts extend the three spatial velocity components constantly in normal coordinates, patch by a smooth partition, and apply a compact cutoff equal to one on the smaller interval track. The prescribed velocity is zero on both $t$ end collars; choose all extended components zero there, using charts of the constant product arc on those collars and a cutoff in $t$ on their complement. Integrate in $s$. Uniqueness of the ODE gives a smooth family $H_t$ of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms with $H_t(A_{0,t})$ the actual marked interval and $H_t=\mathrm{id}$ on both time end collars. Consequently $H_t^{-1}F_t$ is a knot isotopy retaining exactly the given endpoints and fixing one common marked interval for every $t$. This contraction argument is necessary: simply extending the moving interval in the parameter $t$ would not by itself force the terminal ambient map to be the identity.

**Puncture without changing height or endpoints.** Apply the product-strip and puncture construction of [F2] to this fixed common interval, with spatial coordinates independent of $t$. In a smaller neighborhood the knots agree with that interval for all $t$; compactness gives uniform separation from the rest after shortening it once. Puncturing at its central point gives an isotopy of compact long tangles, fixed on their two spatial end collars, closed by one fixed exterior arc carrying the mark. The spatial coordinate changes in step 3.1 were level-preserving, so its trace is still exactly a cylinder of knot embeddings with time coordinate $t$. In particular the restriction of time to this cylinder has nonzero derivative everywhere. There is no need for a Morse perturbation, and none is made. There is an explicit planar endpoint comparison if the displayed closed diagrams initially use a pole in the adjacent face rather than the spatial puncture at the mark. Write their common round compact projection disk as $D=\{|z|\le R\}$ and their common marked point as $p$, where $|p|>R$. Choose a small marked germ and $\delta>0$ so that its closed neighborhood misses $W=\{|z|<R+\delta\}$. Set $$b_u=\frac{uR^2}{\overline p},\qquad f_u(z)=\frac{z-b_u}{1-\overline b_u z/R^2},\qquad 0\le u\le1.$$ These are disk automorphisms, starting at the identity: on $|z|=R$ one has $|z-b_u|^2=R^2|1-\overline b_u z/R^2|^2$, and their inverse fractional linear maps have the same disk property. Their complex derivative has nonzero numerator $1-|b_u|^2/R^2>0$. Their pole is $p/u$, with infinity at $u=0$, so it stays outside $D$ and ends at the marked point. Thus $f_u|_D$ is an actual smooth isotopy of compact disk embeddings onto $D$, including $u=1$. It is an orientation-preserving coordinate chart on the punctured projection sphere. Its endpoint pole is the spatial puncture point; postcomposition by a positive planar similarity identifies it with a rotation-induced stereographic chart with that pole if such a chart is used for the spatial coordinates. One may instead retain this very chart in the puncture construction. Apply [F1] to $f_u|_D$ in the plane, with extension support in $W$. Its disk velocity is tangent to the boundary; the extension theorem for a compact source with boundary applies and gives an ambient plane isotopy $\Phi_u$ equal to $f_u$ on $D$ and identity outside $W$. Consequently it fixes the specified marked germ pointwise throughout. Choose the long closing arc to be $\Phi_1$ of the original common exterior arc. It is outside $D$, since $\Phi_1$ preserves $D$, and retains exactly the same marked germ. This supplies protected planar isotopies from the displayed endpoints to the punctured-and-reclosed endpoints; prepend and append those isotopies. For two normalized endpoints use the same $D,p,b_u,\Phi_u$ and closing arc. No arbitrary ambient extension or equality of different planar charts is being assumed: both the prescribed endpoint diagrams and their fixed marked germ are retained by the recorded relative extension.

**Relative finite projection genericity.** Repeat the family of [F3] on this compact tangle isotopy with bumps zero on smaller parameter end collars and spatial tangle-end collars. At every movable source point these bumps are positive, so the same finite monomial Hermite interpolation prescribes the required independent jets; its evaluations at protected source points are not needed. The exterior closing arc and the two joining collars have fixed regular projection, separated from the compact moving portion. Thus no bad projection stratum involving the protected mark is present. On the moving portion the cusp, tangent-double and triple equations, exclusions of their coincidences and higher degeneracies, and deleted-diagonal estimates are precisely those proved in [F3]. Arbitrarily small parameter choices give finitely many separated generic events relative the stationary endpoint diagrams. The perturbations change spatial coordinates of the slice embeddings only, so their trace remains a height-submersive cylinder. Straight interpolation between the original and sufficiently close perturbed slice maps is an embedding isotopy by the uniform local immersion and distant-pair separation bounds used in [F3]. It is fixed on every protected collar.

The event identification in [F3] gives only oriented R1, R2 and R3 moves; between them the projected decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy. Each exceptional event has compact support inside the projection disk and therefore misses the fixed marked exterior arc. The finite time list yields the required sequence. No surface critical point has been introduced, so births, saddles and deaths do not occur. Undoing $H_t^{-1}$ identifies its trace with the given marked isotopy, up to the small relative perturbation in step 5.1. Since $H_t$ is identity on both end collars, the spatial endpoint identifications are retained exactly; the explicitly recorded planar endpoint isotopies in step 4.1 return the displayed prescribed diagrams. This proves the stated relative comparison and no algebraic map assertion.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

For the empty link diagram, use its single empty resolution state and empty tensor term $\mathbb Q$ in cohomological and quantum degree $0$, with zero differential. Its induced decreasing filtration is $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ for $p\leq0$ and $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $p>0$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

**Input:** a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ and a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on its crossing set. A diagram object is supplied as mathematical input; this procedure does not parse a serialized string.

**Output:** the normalized bigraded Khovanov cochain module $C^{i,j}(D)$ and its candidate differential $d:C^{i,j}(D)\to C^{i+1,j}(D)$, constructed by the following finite instructions.

1. Enumerate every state $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$ once. Form the crossingless resolution by using the A-smoothing at $v(c)=0$ and the B-smoothing at $v(c)=1$.
2. For each state, create one tensor factor of the integral Frobenius algebra for each resolution circle and place the resulting tensor product in cohomological degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum degree $|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$ for its circle labels $a$.
3. For each state and each crossing $c_j$ with $v(c_j)=0$, create the edge to $v+e_j$. Apply multiplication if that smoothing change merges two circles, comultiplication if it splits one circle, the identity on other tensor factors, and the sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. Sum the edge maps out of every state to obtain $d$.
4. Return the finite direct sum of the state modules with these degrees and maps. The square-zero property is the separate local lemma named by `justified_by`.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram, order its crossings as $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and form the direct sum of state modules $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$ over all functions $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$. Here $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, each crossing is changed from its A-smoothing at $0$ to its B-smoothing at $1$, and the edge map is the multiplication $m$ for a merge or comultiplication $\Delta$ for a split, multiplied by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$ on the edge at $c_j$. Then the sum $d$ of all edge maps satisfies $d^2=0$.

If the filtration on every $C_n$ is finite, the spectral sequence of the filtered chain complex stabilizes pointwise and naturally abuts to $H_n(C)$ with its image filtration. This homology filtration is finite, exhaustive and separated. No uniform filtration bound in n is required.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. A **cochain complex in $\mathcal A$**
is a family of objects $(C^n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ together with morphisms
$$d^n:C^n\to C^{n+1}$$
such that
$$d^{n+1}\circ d^n=0$$
for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.

This page uses the reindexing convention that a cochain complex $C^\bullet$ may
also be read as the chain complex with $(C^\sharp)_n:=C^{-n}$ and
$d^\sharp_n:=d^{-n}$, so that lower and upper indices differ only by the sign
of the grading.

Let $A$ be an object of an abelian category. An **increasing filtration** is a specified family of subobjects $F_pA\subseteq A$, $p\in\mathbb Z$, with $F_pA\subseteq F_{p+1}A$. A **decreasing filtration** satisfies $F^{p+1}A\subseteq F^pA$. The translation on the same object is $F^pA=F_{-p}A$; translating back gives $F_pA=F^{-p}A$. A filtration-preserving morphism $f:A\to B$ factors on each piece as $F_pA\to F_pB\hookrightarrow B$ (or with upper indices). The restrictions are unique because the inclusions are monic. The ambient setting is [[def-abelian-category]].

derivations.claim: Put $a=1+X$ and $b=X-1$ in $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$. The relation $X^2=1$ gives $m_L(a\otimes a)=2a,\quad m_L(b\otimes b)=-2b,\quad m_L(a\otimes b)=m_L(b\otimes a)=0, \qquad \Delta_L(a)=a\otimes a,\quad\Delta_L(b)=b\otimes b.$ The counit takes value $1$ on each of $a,b$. In the basis $1,X$, the degree-preserving part of each saddle is the integral Khovanov saddle, and the only remaining terms replace $X\otimes X$ by $1$ under multiplication or replace $X$ by $1\otimes1$ under comultiplication. Each replacement raises the quantum degree by $4$, including the state shift, so the associated-graded differential is precisely the even Khovanov differential.

The projection of $D$ is a finite four-valent plane graph (with crossingless components as disjoint Jordan curves), so checkerboard-color its regions with the unbounded region white. Define the color of a region by the parity of intersections of a path from infinity to it with the projection; this is path-independent because every closed curve in the plane has even mod-$2$ intersection with the closed diagram. For each segment between crossing disks, assign label $a$ and direct it so that the black region is on its right, or assign label $b$ and direct it so that black is on its left. At a crossing, list the four incident segment ends clockwise as $1,2,3,4$, choosing the convention that sectors $(1,2)$ and $(3,4)$ are black, as in the local drawing. The arrows point outward/inward at ends $1,3$ according as their labels are $a/b$, and inward/outward at ends $2,4$ according as their labels are $a/b$. Thus the four patterns $aabb,abba,bbaa,baab$ are exactly those for which opposite ends have opposite arrows; in each case exactly one adjacent pairing connects equal labels and an incoming to an outgoing arrow. It is the oriented smoothing. All-equal patterns have two equal-label smoothings but do not orient the original crossing, while alternating and three-to-one patterns have no compatible smoothing. Thus, among segment labelings compatible with a smoothing at every crossing, having no all-equal crossing is equivalent to determining exactly one oriented state and an orientation of the link. For an oriented state, each circle has one label. Let $\delta(C)$ be the parity of the number of other Seifert circles separating it from infinity. The outside region of $C$ is black exactly when $\delta(C)=1$; its inside has the opposite color. As the interior is left of a counterclockwise circle and right of a clockwise circle, the black-right rule labels $C$ by $a$ exactly when $\delta(C)+\kappa(C)$ is even, where $\kappa(C)=1$ for counterclockwise and $0$ for clockwise. This is the parity rule in the Statement.

The cube has finitely many states and each state module is finite-dimensional, hence only finitely many quantum filtration levels occur. Reindex the cochain degrees and filtration by [F5], then apply [F4] to obtain a convergent spectral sequence with abutment $\operatorname{gr}H(C_L(D))$; reversing the filtration index changes only the page's filtration label. Index its first page as the associated-graded chain complex and its next as its cohomology. By step 1.1 and [F2], this cohomology is rational Khovanov cohomology. This is the convention in which the homology page is denoted $E_2$; changing page names does not change the limiting filtered homology.

Restrict an enhanced state to the diagram segments between crossing disks; its circle labels determine one segment labeling. From the operations in step 1.1, an edge map is nonzero exactly when the four labels at its crossing agree. Every nonzero edge preserves all segment labels, so the complex is a direct sum over segment labelings. For a fixed labeling, each all-equal crossing is a free coordinate with both smoothings and an invertible saddle; each other crossing has at most one compatible smoothing. If any crossing has no compatible smoothing the summand is zero; otherwise its compatible states form a Boolean cube on precisely the all-equal crossings.

On any nonempty cube from step 2.2, every edge coefficient is nonzero in $\mathbb Q$. Let $u(e)$ be the coefficient of a directed edge and let $s(e)=(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v_i}$ be the standard cube sign on the edge changing coordinate $j$. The equation $d^2=0$ gives $u(e_1)u(e_2)=-u(e_3)u(e_4)$ around each square, and the standard signs satisfy the same equation. Hence $u(e)/s(e)$ has product $1$ around every square. Rescale each vertex basis by the product of these ratios along a path from a fixed vertex; square faces generate all path changes in a Boolean cube, so the rescaling is path-independent and identifies its differential with the standard tensor differential. If there is a free coordinate, its factor is $\mathbb Q\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathbb Q$; contracting that factor with the tensor-product Koszul sign contracts the whole cube. If there is no free coordinate, the cube is a single zero-differential line. When $D$ is empty, this is the unique empty-state line $\mathbb Q$, whose class is the empty-tensor unit. In all cases, step 1.2 identifies the singleton lines bijectively with the orientations of the link, so they form a basis of Lee homology.

For a knot, reversing orientation leaves the oriented resolution fixed and interchanges $a$ and $b$ on each of its $k\ge1$ Seifert circles. Write the two singleton representatives as $u=\bigotimes_{i=1}^k c_i$ and $\bar u=\bigotimes_{i=1}^k\bar c_i$, where $c_i\in\{a,b\}$ and $\bar c_i$ is the other basis vector. Their state shift is $r=|v|+n_+-2n_-$. A tensor term with exactly $j$ labels equal to $1$ has quantum degree $r-k+2j$. In the expansions of $u$ and $\bar u$, its coefficients differ by $(-1)^j$: each selected $1$ contributes opposite signs from $a=1+X$ and $b=X-1$, while every $X$ contributes coefficient $1$. Thus $u+\bar u$ contains exactly the even-$j$ terms and $u-\bar u$ exactly the odd-$j$ terms. Their least chain degrees are $r-k$ and $r-k+2$, which give lower bounds for their induced homology filtration levels; boundary changes may improve those levels. The differential changes quantum degree by $0$ or $4$, so the whole filtered complex splits into its quantum congruence summands modulo $4$. The two nonzero homology classes $[u+\bar u]$ and $[u-\bar u]$ lie in distinct such summands and span homology by step 3.1. Each summand therefore contributes one filtered homology line, with level in its own congruence class.

Choose a point $p$ away from the crossings. Let $X_p$ multiply the circle containing $p$ by $X$ in each state. It commutes with each edge: the identities $m(Xz,w)=Xm(z,w)=m(z,Xw)$ and $\Delta(Xz)=(X\otimes1)\Delta(z)=(1\otimes X)\Delta(z)$ hold for $z,w=1,X$, hence for all inputs. It is a chain map with $X_p^2=1$. Its terms have quantum degrees $-2$ (sending $1$ to $X$) and $+2$ (sending $X$ to $1$), so it has filtered degree $-2$. At the mark the labels of $u,\bar u$ are opposite, with $Xa=a$ and $Xb=-b$. Hence $X_p$ interchanges the two homology lines of step 4.1, up to an overall sign. If their filtration levels are $\ell_+,\ell_-$, its filtered degree in both directions gives $\ell_-\ge\ell_+-2$ and $\ell_+\ge\ell_--2$. They lie in congruence classes differing by two modulo four, so $|\ell_+-\ell_-|=2$. Every knot-state quantum grading is odd: at the oriented state its parity is $n+k$, and the connected Seifert disk-band surface has $k-n=1-2g$; a cube edge changes $|v|+k(v)$ by an even integer. Finally $[u]$ and $[\bar u]$ are half the sum and difference of these two lines, so both have the smaller level, by the filtered direct sum into congruence summands. Thus their common level is $s_{\min}$, the larger line has level $s_{\max}=s_{\min}+2$, and the asserted equal-level and congruence properties hold. This argument concerns induced homology filtrations and makes no assertion that a fixed canonical cycle is already a maximal-filtration representative.

citations.quote: Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram with at least one component, ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and a marked point $p$ on the projected link away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

Let a finite planar resolution cube be equipped with an arrow at each crossing, transported to its saddle edges while resolving the other disjoint crossing disks, and use the odd exterior merge and split maps. There is a function assigning a sign to every edge such that the resulting signed differential squares to zero over the integers. More precisely, one can prescribe the face products on all faces, including faces whose two composites vanish, as follows. On a face with nonzero composites let $\kappa\in\{1,-1\}$ be their relative commutation sign. On a zero-composite face the two saddle arcs have alternating endpoints on one circle, one arc inside and one outside; put them in the standard two-chord picture by an orientation-preserving planar isotopy and rotate so that the inside arrow points upwards and set $\kappa=1$ when the outside arrow points left, and $\kappa=-1$ when it points right. Then the prescribed product of the four edge signs is $-\kappa$. These prescriptions are consistent, and two edge assignments realizing the same prescriptions are related by a vertexwise sign change. All the constructions are finite and choice-free. The vertexwise comparison commutes with the marked right $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action.

For a finite planar odd resolution cube with the prescribed full face signs, a Reidemeister I or II move supported away from the marked point induces a normalized bigraded chain homotopy equivalence over the right ring $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalence, inverse and contraction are finite integer matrices in exterior quotients, exterior products, and projections to the two coefficients of a small-circle generator. Their reductions modulo two are the corresponding even Khovanov cancellation maps. The result holds for every exterior closure of the move disk and every orientation of its strands, and is choice-free.

For finite based diagrams differing by Reidemeister III in a disk missing the mark, their normalized odd complexes, with the prescribed full face signs, are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent over the right ring $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalences and homotopies are integral and reduce modulo two to the even local cancellation equivalence. They apply to every exterior closure, including closures in which several local arcs belong to the same resolution circle. Together with the marked Reidemeister I and II contractions this proves invariance under every finite based Reidemeister sequence. No choice axiom is needed for these finite constructions.

derivations.claim: **An odd saddle as one more cube direction.** Replace its two local smoothings by an auxiliary crossing, ordered after the actual crossings. By [F2] its full cube has edge signs. The auxiliary edges form maps $g_v$ between its lower and upper faces; the mixed square equations say $d_1g+gd_0=0$, where $g$ preserves the actual resolution height. Put $F_v=(-1)^{|v|}g_v$. Since an actual edge increases $|v|$ by one, this identity becomes $d_1F=Fd_0$. The side-face restrictions are admissible assignments for the actual endpoint diagrams; use [F2]'s vertex-sign maps to identify them with any chosen admissible endpoint assignments. Every $g_v$ is an odd saddle, so commutes with the right marked action. The factor $(-1)^{|v|}$ and the vertex signs do too. Modulo two the construction is exactly the ordinary even saddle map. The auxiliary crossing is used only to choose coefficients, not included in the endpoint normalization. For a merge the circle count decreases by one at unchanged exterior degree; for a split it increases by one and exterior degree increases by one. Thus both maps have quantum degree $-1$ and cohomological degree zero.

**Odd birth and death signs.** A birth appends a generator $z$ for a small disjoint circle and uses the inclusion $\Lambda W\to\Lambda(W\oplus\mathbb Zz)$, without inserting $z$. External maps preserve this subalgebra, so the inclusion is a chain map with unchanged edge assignment. For a death use $(-1)^{\sigma(v)}\iota_z$, where $\iota_z$ is exterior contraction with the coefficient functional of $z$. It commutes with external merge quotients. For a split with difference $u$ not involving $z$, $\iota_z(u\wedge w)=-u\wedge\iota_z(w)$; the increase of $\sigma$ cancels that minus sign. Thus this is also a chain map. The mark is not $z$, and $\iota_z(w\wedge Z_p)=\iota_z(w)\wedge Z_p$, so both maps are marked right-module maps. A birth adds one circle and no exterior generator, giving quantum degree $+1$. A nonzero death removes a circle and one exterior generator, giving degree $-1+2=+1$. Modulo two these are the unit and counit of the even algebra.

**The deformed circle coordinates.** Work over $\mathbb Z[h]$, retaining the marked $\mathbb R$-action. Write a small circle first as $1\otimes w_1+X\otimes w_X$. If $x$ is the dot on the arc from which it splits, the split has coordinates $u\mapsto((x-h)u,u)$, since $\Delta(u)=1\otimes(X-h)u+X\otimes u$. A merge into an arc with dot $y$ is $(w_1,w_X)\mapsto w_1+yw_X$. Opposite saddles satisfy $ts=x+y-h$. For distinct circles the equation is $\Delta m(a\otimes b)=Xa\otimes b+a\otimes Xb-h a\otimes b$: substituting $1\otimes1,1\otimes X,X\otimes1,X\otimes X$ gives respectively $1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h1\otimes1$, $X\otimes X$, $X\otimes X$, $hX\otimes X$ on both sides. For a single circle it is $m\Delta(u)=(2X-h)u$. Dot operators commute with saddles by $m(Xa,b)=Xm(a,b)$ and $\Delta(Xa)=(X\otimes1)\Delta(a)=(1\otimes X)\Delta(a)$, verified on $1,X$.

**Deformed RI and RII.** A merge curl is $(u,v)\mapsto u+Xv$. Its survivor inclusion is $w\mapsto(-Xw,w)$, its projection is $(u,v)\mapsto v$, and its contraction on the target is $w\mapsto(w,0)$. A split curl is $w\mapsto((X-h)w,w)$; its survivor inclusion is $u\mapsto(u,0)$, its projection is $(u,v)\mapsto u-(X-h)v$, and its contraction is $(u,v)\mapsto v$. Substitution gives $pi=1$ and $1-ip=dh+hd$ in both cases. For RII use states $U,I,U\sqcup\mu,U$ at $00,01,10,11$ and the signed differential $d^0(u)=(su,(x-h)u,u)$, $d^1(v,w_1,w_X)=tv-w_1-yw_X$. In local degree one, $dh+hd$ is $(v,w_1,w_X)\mapsto(sw_X,w_1-tv+(x+y-h)w_X,w_X)$, exactly $1-ip$; in local degrees zero and two it is the identity. These are actual inverse maps and homotopies. The RI and RII normalization checks are the same circle-height calculations in [F3], since $h$ has quantum degree $-2$.

**An $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$-linear localized contraction.** Put $S=\mathbb Z[h,h^{-1}]$ and $A=X$, $B=h-X$. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

For the empty link diagram, use its single empty resolution state and empty tensor term $\mathbb Q$ in cohomological and quantum degree $0$, with zero differential. Its induced decreasing filtration is $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ for $p\leq0$ and $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $p>0$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $D$ and $D'$ be regular oriented link diagrams.
Then $D$ and $D'$ represent equivalent oriented links if and only if $D'$ can be
obtained from $D$ by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented
Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3.

The integral signed Khovanov cubes have the local graded cancellation models described below. They are chain homotopy equivalences over every fixed exterior resolution, commute with exterior saddle differentials, and commute with multiplication by $X$ at every marked point outside the local disk. Consequently they also give chain homotopy equivalences after taking the reduced quotient. For the crossing with A-smoothing the identity matching and B-smoothing the cap-cup matching, the two three-crossing braid cubes with words $121$ and $212$ retract to the same three-term complex. The two-crossing inverse-pair cube retracts to the identity matching in local cohomological degree one and quantum shift upward by one. All retractions are integral; their homotopies and the two cancellations in the three-crossing cube are specified in the proof.

Consequently they also give chain homotopy equivalences after taking the reduced quotient. For the crossing with A-smoothing the identity matching and B-smoothing the cap-cup matching, the two three-crossing braid cubes with words $121$ and $212$ retract to the same three-term complex. The two-crossing inverse-pair cube retracts to the identity matching in local cohomological degree one and quantum shift upward by one. A chain map $f:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ is a **chain homotopy equivalence** if
there exists a chain map $g:D_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ such that
$$g\circ f\simeq1_C,\qquad f\circ g\simeq1_D.$$

Such a map $g$ is called a **homotopy inverse** of $f$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: In $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, multiplication by $X$ is a dot operator with $X^2=1$, and $\Delta_L(z)=1\otimes Xz+X\otimes z,\qquad \Delta_Lm_L(a\otimes b)=Xa\otimes b+a\otimes Xb.$ The first identity follows by substituting $z=1,X$; the second follows by substituting the four basis pairs $1\otimes1,1\otimes X,X\otimes1,X\otimes X$. Thus the split and merge circle coordinates in [F3] remain valid for the Lee algebra, and the neck-cutting relation required in the Reidemeister II retraction holds with $X^2=1$.

For a positive curl, the local differential is $(u,v)\mapsto u+Xv$ from the small-circle coordinates $1\otimes u+X\otimes v$ to the continuing arc. Change coordinates to $(u',v')=(u+Xv,v)$. The retraction has inclusion $i(w)=(0,w)$, projection $p(u',v')=v'$, and contraction $h(w)=(w,0)$ on the target; hence $pi=1$ and $1-ip=dh+hd$. For a negative curl, the local differential is $v\mapsto(Xv,v)$ into the small-circle coordinates. Change target coordinates to $(w'_1,w_X)=(w_1-Xw_X,w_X)$; then the map is $v\mapsto(0,v)$, and the retraction onto $w'_1$ has inclusion $i(w)=(w,0)$, projection $p(w'_1,w_X)=w'_1$, and contraction $h(0,w) = w$ from the $w_X$ target summand to the source. These formulas give $pi=1$ and $1-ip=dh+hd$. Before the writhe shifts, the positive survivor has quantum shift $-1$ and the negative survivor has quantum shift $+2$; the new $+1$ and $-2$ writhe shifts cancel them, respectively. In both cases the normalized homological degree agrees with the original. For Reidemeister II use the local maps $i(v)=(v,tv,0)$ and $p(v,w_1,w_X)=v-sw_X$ from [F3]; the identity $ts=x+y$ used in $dh+hd=1-ip$ is exactly the second identity in step 1.1. Its local homological and quantum shifts are canceled by the one positive and one negative crossing normalization changes. For Reidemeister III, the two cancellations in [F4] use only identity pivots and the same split coordinates, while writhe normalization is unchanged. All coordinate changes have pivots $\pm1$ and entries given by the Lee saddle and dot maps, so they preserve the decreasing filtration after normalization.

The Lee deformation terms raise $q$ by $4$ by [F1]. Each local coordinate change in step 2.1 is triangular with diagonal entries $\pm1$; its off-diagonal entries are saddle maps, whose degree-preserving parts are the corresponding Khovanov maps and whose other terms raise $q$ by $4$. Therefore the maps, inverses, and contraction homotopies preserve the decreasing filtration after applying the normalization shifts. On the associated graded, the R1 retractions are the degree-preserving parts of the displayed curl maps, and the RII/RIII retractions are the local Khovanov equivalences of [F4]. Their filtered maps induce isomorphisms on filtered homology; their associated-graded maps induce isomorphisms on the Khovanov page and, by page iteration, on every later spectral-sequence page.

By [A1] and [F2], choose a finite sequence of oriented Reidemeister moves and planar isotopies from $D$ to $D'$; if $D=D'$, the empty sequence gives the identity. Planar isotopies rel crossing data simply relabel state circles and preserve all degrees. Compose the filtered equivalences from step 3.1 along this finite sequence. The composite has a filtered inverse up to filtered homotopy, so [F5] gives an isomorphism of filtered Lee homology and step 3.1 gives isomorphisms of all pages from rational Khovanov onward. This proves diagram independence. The only choice used is the finite move sequence supplied by $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; the local algebraic maps themselves are explicit and choice-free.

citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $D$ and $D'$ are finite regular diagrams of the same nonempty oriented link, then their rational Lee cochain complexes are related by a cochain homotopy equivalence whose maps and homotopies preserve the decreasing quantum filtrations after normalization. Consequently their Lee homology groups with induced filtrations are isomorphic, and the spectral sequences from the rational Khovanov page onward are isomorphic. These filtered groups and pages therefore depend only on the oriented link.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Therefore the dimension and filtered vector-space type computed from $D$ agree with those computed from $D'$. The two canonical classes on each diagram form a basis by step 1.1; no identification of individual basis vectors across diagrams is needed for the claimed rank or filtration invariance.

By [F1] the vector space is nonzero, and therefore every nonzero class has a finite integer level $\ell(x)$. The set of levels is a nonempty subset of the finite set of filtration indices; hence its minimum and maximum exist. This uses no choice principle.

The diagram-independence conclusion from [F2] uses the stated axiom branch [A1]. Thus the displayed formula defines an invariant of the oriented knot under AC$_\omega$.

citations.quote: Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram with at least one component, ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and a marked point $p$ on the projected link away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

Let a finite planar resolution cube be equipped with an arrow at each crossing, transported to its saddle edges while resolving the other disjoint crossing disks, and use the odd exterior merge and split maps. There is a function assigning a sign to every edge such that the resulting signed differential squares to zero over the integers. More precisely, one can prescribe the face products on all faces, including faces whose two composites vanish, as follows. On a face with nonzero composites let $\kappa\in\{1,-1\}$ be their relative commutation sign. On a zero-composite face the two saddle arcs have alternating endpoints on one circle, one arc inside and one outside; put them in the standard two-chord picture by an orientation-preserving planar isotopy and rotate so that the inside arrow points upwards and set $\kappa=1$ when the outside arrow points left, and $\kappa=-1$ when it points right. Then the prescribed product of the four edge signs is $-\kappa$. These prescriptions are consistent, and two edge assignments realizing the same prescriptions are related by a vertexwise sign change. All the constructions are finite and choice-free. The vertexwise comparison commutes with the marked right $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action.

For a finite planar odd resolution cube with the prescribed full face signs, a Reidemeister I or II move supported away from the marked point induces a normalized bigraded chain homotopy equivalence over the right ring $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalence, inverse and contraction are finite integer matrices in exterior quotients, exterior products, and projections to the two coefficients of a small-circle generator. Their reductions modulo two are the corresponding even Khovanov cancellation maps. The result holds for every exterior closure of the move disk and every orientation of its strands, and is choice-free.

For finite based diagrams differing by Reidemeister III in a disk missing the mark, their normalized odd complexes, with the prescribed full face signs, are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent over the right ring $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalences and homotopies are integral and reduce modulo two to the even local cancellation equivalence. They apply to every exterior closure, including closures in which several local arcs belong to the same resolution circle. Together with the marked Reidemeister I and II contractions this proves invariance under every finite based Reidemeister sequence. No choice axiom is needed for these finite constructions.

Let a finite oriented link-cobordism movie carry a marked point continuously through its regular levels, with its trace disjoint from all elementary move disks, and with the marked component never dying. Use the odd cubes with the prescribed full face signs and the integral Bar–Natan cubes over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$. This movie admits an integral odd map, linear for the marked right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action, and an integral marked $\mathbb R$-linear Bar–Natan map. They have cohomological degree zero and quantum degree the Euler characteristic of the movie, and their reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ agree under the statewise comparison. For a connected oriented concordance between knots the localized Bar–Natan map is a chain homotopy equivalence over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$. A localized knot complex retracts over that ring onto one free rank-one module in cohomological degree zero and odd quantum parity. All these statements concern the supplied movie; no independence from its presentation is asserted. The finite algebraic constructions use no choice axiom.

Let two finite based knot diagrams be joined along their marked arcs in a planar pointed connected-sum diagram, without new crossings. The odd complexes admit a normalized bigraded right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain isomorphism
$$ C_o(D_1)\otimes_{\mathbb A}C_o(D_2)\{-1\}\ \cong\ C_o(D_1\#D_2), $$
and the Bar–Natan complexes admit the corresponding marked $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$-linear chain isomorphism. In the odd case the induced signs realize the full prescribed face products, so admissible sign comparison applies, including zero-composite faces. The two isomorphisms agree after reduction modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ under the statewise comparison. Their construction is finite and choice-free.

Let a finite oriented based regular link diagram, with its ordered crossing disks and crossing arrows, lie on an oriented two-sphere. Choose any two orientation-preserving planar coordinate presentations whose omitted points miss the diagram and all crossing disks. Transport the diagram, crossing arrows, over/under information and mark by these coordinates; keep the same crossing order. Circle relabelling gives grading-preserving marked-module chain isomorphisms between their integral odd complexes with transported full admissible edge signs, and between their integral Bar–Natan complexes. In particular the full odd face prescription, including zero-composite faces, is unchanged by the choice of omitted point.

For independently chosen edge assignments satisfying that full prescription, compose the odd relabelling with vertexwise signs. The resulting odd and Bar–Natan isomorphisms have inverse maps, are respectively right linear over $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, and give a strictly commuting square under the statewise reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$. Their inverses give the inverse square. Whenever the endpoint triples satisfy the LEO hypotheses, these maps therefore give local maps in both directions; this applies in particular to knot triples once their separate foundations have been established. The Bar–Natan maps are already chain isomorphisms before localization. The construction is finite and requires no choice axiom. This assertion concerns recharting the same spherical diagram, not transporting a mark through a crossing of a fixed planar diagram.

Assume countable choice. Every prescribed finite regular oriented knot diagram with a specified marked point away from its crossings admits a compatible long endpoint presentation by finitely many planar isotopies and one orientation-preserving spherical rotation recharting. All crossing labels, crossing arrows if specified, strand orientations, over/under data and the mark are transported. No crossing is created, removed, or passed through the mark. The final planar diagram has a round disk containing every crossing and all of the diagram except a single crossing-free exterior closing arc carrying the mark; the disk boundary meets the diagram transversely in exactly two points. A neighborhood of that arc can be used as the protected marked neighborhood in a long-tangle movie.

The recharting omits a point in a face adjacent to the marked germ. Its spherical rotation extends by an explicit orientation-preserving linear map of $S^3$, and the planar normalizations have actual spatial coordinate lifts. Thus the construction records an orientation-preserving spatial identification of the represented marked endpoint knot, rather than declaring its coordinate identifications to be identities. A representative can be chosen with the exterior arc at constant projection height and with product collars at its two cut points. This is a geometric existence assertion. It asserts neither a purely planar protected Reidemeister comparison nor an algebraic invariance theorem. The construction uses only finite selections and explicit maps, so in fact introduces no choice beyond the stated branch.

Assume countable choice. Let $F:S^1\times[0,1]\to S^3$ be a smooth isotopy of oriented knots, stationary in end collars, with a specified marked source point. Suppose its two endpoint diagrams are regular compatible long presentations with the same standard oriented exterior marked arc, parametrized identically on a neighborhood of that point. Use the corresponding spatial endpoint coordinates, in which this common marked arc is a standard small round arc through the stereographic point at infinity; its puncture is closed in the planar diagrams by the same standard exterior arc. Then these prescribed endpoint diagrams are related by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented R1, R2 and R3 moves, whose closed support disks miss the mark. The marked neighborhood remains fixed. There are no births, saddles or deaths. The movie represents the given marked isotopy up to a spatial coordinate family equal to the identity in both end collars and a small isotopy relative those collars.

Here compatible long endpoints include the displayed common oriented arc and its spatial coordinate identifications. This statement does not silently identify arbitrary physical endpoint coordinates. Spherical endpoint recharting may first be used to choose such common compatible presentations; no algebraic invariance of that recharting or of these movies is asserted here.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented collared embedded annulus from a knot $K_0$ to a knot $K_1$. Let $\gamma\subset S$ be a smooth properly embedded arc joining their specified marked points and equal to their vertical marked intervals in smaller end collars. There exist based regular diagrams representing these endpoint knots and a finite oriented movie between them, consisting of planar isotopies, R1, R2, R3, births, saddles and deaths, with a marked point in every frame. The marked track is strictly increasing in height, never dies, never lies at a diagram crossing, and misses the closed support disks of every exceptional move. Every regular interval also keeps a neighborhood of the mark fixed in its chosen diagram coordinates.

More precisely, first an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller end collars carries the given marked surface to one with monotone marked arc. A smooth level-preserving change of spatial coordinates then puts a neighborhood of that arc into a fixed exterior closing-arc position. The movie trace, transported back by those same coordinates, is ambient isotopic to the original marked $S$ relative to the smaller end collars. Its endpoint diagrams and their marked parametrizations use the corresponding endpoint coordinate identifications. One may retain prescribed endpoint diagrams already in this compatible long-tangle presentation. The conclusion does not assert a based Reidemeister sequence between arbitrary prescribed planar endpoint diagrams or between arbitrary basepoint presentations, and asserts no movie-independence theorem for algebraic maps.

derivations.claim: By [F2], choose the full admissible face assignment. The coefficient of every height-two state in the square of the differential is zero, since the two signed saddle composites cancel, including the faces where both composites vanish. The normalized saddle grading is that of [F1]. Each state is a finite free right $\mathbb A$-module: use the basis of exterior products of the augmentation-zero differences $Z_j-Z_p$, followed by the optional marked factor $Z_p$. Thus the actual odd complex exists, with the asserted bigrading and marked action. The construction in [F2] is finite and uses no additional choice.

Modulo two, send each exterior circle generator to the even $X$-label on that circle. The merge quotient becomes the even product, and multiplication by $C_1-C_2$ becomes the even split map, since all signs disappear. The Bar–Natan formulas of [F1] reduce modulo $(2,h)$ to the same product and split. These identifications also carry appending $Z_p$ to multiplication by the marked $X$. Therefore the comparison is a bigraded marked $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain isomorphism, and in particular a chain homotopy equivalence.

The localized proof in [F4] decomposes the enhanced-state cube into Boolean summands in the basis $A=X,B=h-X$, contracts each non-singleton summand by unit identity pivots, and does so over the marked ring because the marked label is constant on a summand. The two singleton knot states are its orientations, in degree zero and odd quantum parity. The two idempotents $X/h$ and $1-X/h$ identify their span with one regular rank-one localized coefficient module. This supplies the required chain homotopy equivalence, including the module-linearity of its homotopies.

For a planar pointed sum, [F5] gives the right-linear odd map using the reduced decomposition $\Lambda V=\Lambda\ker(\operatorname{aug})\otimes\mathbb A$. On reduced exterior degrees $r_1,r_2$ its formula is $(-1)^{r_1\sigma_2}(u_1\wedge u_2)\otimes a_1a_2$. Its sign is independent of both marked factors, so it is balanced and right-linear; its internal and mixed full face products are verified in [F5]. The BN map is marked multiplication with vertex sign $(-1)^{n_-^{(1)}|v_2|}$, accounting for normalized cochain tensor signs. Both merge two circles into one and have the displayed quantum shift $\{-1\}$. Their reductions agree with the same even marked multiplication. The admissible sign comparison in [F2] transfers this to any admissible representatives. This proves the connected-sum clauses.

**Arbitrary prescribed based endpoints.** For a finite pair of based diagrams first use [F7] with the same local coordinates at their marks: each oriented marked tangent is the positive real axis. After straightening their crossing-free germs, choose one common radius $r$, one $0<\epsilon<\min(r/4,1/4)$ and one $R$ between $B=(1+\epsilon r)/(r-\epsilon)$ and $1/\epsilon$. The same rotation rechart $w=-(1+\overline a z)/(z-a)$, $a=i\epsilon$, then acts on both. Their exterior arcs are literally the same $w(x)$, with the same cut parameters $x=\pm c$, where $c^2=(1-R^2\epsilon^2)/(R^2-\epsilon^2)$. Flatten their height to zero as in [F7]. They have the same oriented geodesic marked germ and the same compatible spatial endpoint model. If puncturing spatially at the mark changes the planar chart, use [F8]'s explicit endpoint comparison: move the pole within the exterior cap, restrict the chart transitions to the common compact tangle disk, extend this compact-disk embedding isotopy to the plane, and use the image of the common closing arc. These are actual planar isotopies to the punctured-and-reclosed diagrams, not a claimed equality of drawings under pole change. All endpoint coordinate identifications are recorded in [F7] and [F8].

**Full based diagram invariance.** Suppose the prescribed based diagrams represent isotopic oriented knots. Reparametrize a representing smooth knot isotopy so that its marked source point reaches the specified endpoint marks; an orientation-preserving circle reparametrization can be chosen through rotations in its source parameter and made stationary in end collars. Compose with the explicit endpoint coordinate isotopies from step 1.5. The resulting endpoints have the common long model. By [F8] this isotopy has a finite protected movie containing only R1, R2, R3 and planar isotopies; its relative contraction ensures identity spatial coordinate maps at both ends. No birth, saddle or death is used to infer an odd equivalence. Each R move has the integral marked chain homotopy inverses and homotopies of [F3], and their common even reductions are those of [F4]. The spherical endpoint normalizations have the explicit integral marked isomorphisms and inverse squares of [F6]. Compose these actual maps and their inverses with the planar endpoint isotopies. Thus the original arbitrary prescribed based diagrams have graded marked odd chain homotopy equivalences, with the asserted comparison; the corresponding BN maps are also graded marked chain homotopy equivalences. This handles arbitrary basepoint positions through the geometric endpoint normalization and does not assume a false protected planar comparison between an arbitrary diagram and its exterior rechart.

**Finite ordering and sign choices.** A different full admissible assignment changes the odd complex by the vertex-sign marked isomorphism of [F2]; no invariance assertion about all weak square-compatible candidates is needed. Circle reorderings are actual exterior basis changes. Crossing reorderings transport cube coordinates and the full odd edge assignment. On the BN side a transposition of adjacent crossings $i,j$ changes the ordinary cube-sign convention by the vertex factor $(-1)^{v_i v_j}$: on an $i$-edge its ratio is $(-1)^{v_j}$, on a $j$-edge it is $(-1)^{v_i}$, and on all other edges it is one, exactly the change in the number of preceding 1-coordinates. Products of such transpositions handle every finite crossing permutation. The same factors can be used on the transported odd assignment; they preserve its full face products and reduce to one modulo two. Hence ordering changes and the choices in the coherent full admissible family preserve the claimed marked chain-homotopy type and common reduction.

**Concordance consumers with arbitrary endpoints.** For a collared oriented annulus between any prescribed based knot diagrams choose a proper marked arc between its boundary marks, constant on the given end collars; a product parametrization of the annulus gives such an arc by a smooth angular path between the two marks. Normalize the finite endpoint pair by step 1.5 and carry the annulus through those recorded orientation-preserving spatial endpoint identifications, using their isotopies on end collars. It now has compatible common long endpoints. Apply [F9]'s actual relative four-dimensional arc straightening, followed by its protected strip/puncture, finite Morse and relative projection construction. Its coordinates can retain the common endpoint strips: the center–tangent contraction and parameter-dependent velocity extension in [F8] apply to the family of strip intervals along the already monotone marked arc, not just to whole level knots, and give spatial coordinates identity in both end collars. Thus the required supplied protected movie exists for these endpoints. Its odd and BN maps are those of [F4], with degree the annulus Euler characteristic zero and the exact marked mod-two square; [F4] proves that the localized BN composite is a marked-ring homotopy equivalence. Compose with [F6] and the planar endpoint isomorphisms to return to the original prescribed diagrams. Read the annulus backwards for a local map in the other direction. This uses no odd movie-independence assertion and does not require any individual birth or death map to be a localized equivalence. Together with the tensor calculation in step 1.4 and the R-only invariance in step 2.1, it proves every assertion of the Statement in its full arbitrary-based-diagram scope. Countable choice is exactly the retained geometric extension/genericity hypothesis; all new algebraic maps and finite endpoint choices require no additional choice.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

For the empty link diagram, use its single empty resolution state and empty tensor term $\mathbb Q$ in cohomological and quantum degree $0$, with zero differential. Its induced decreasing filtration is $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ for $p\leq0$ and $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $p>0$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $D$ and $D'$ are finite regular diagrams of the same nonempty oriented link, then their rational Lee cochain complexes are related by a cochain homotopy equivalence whose maps and homotopies preserve the decreasing quantum filtrations after normalization. Consequently their Lee homology groups with induced filtrations are isomorphic, and the spectral sequences from the rational Khovanov page onward are isomorphic. These filtered groups and pages therefore depend only on the oriented link.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nonempty oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Its rational Lee homology is a two-dimensional vector space. For every finite regular diagram of $K$, the two homology classes obtained from the two orientations by the oriented-resolution parity-of-nesting rule form a basis, and the induced quantum filtration is independent of the diagram.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface, with product collars and boundary the finite oriented links $-L_0$ and $L_1$ in the two ends. Components of $S$ and either boundary link may be empty. After an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller prescribed end collars, $S$ has a finite movie consisting of planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves R1, R2 and R3, births, oriented saddle band moves, and deaths. All exceptional times are distinct. The movie's actual smoothly embedded trace is ambient isotopic to the given $S$ relative to those collars, with its boundary orientations and parametrizations retained. Indeed the retractions used in [F3] consist of saddles, dots, factor relabelings, and inverses of scalar identity pivots; the displayed identities show that each constituent commutes with every exterior $X_p$, so their composites and homotopies do too. At one fixed mark on each component its sign determines the orientation of that component; consequently the $2^c$ orientation classes are distinct simultaneous eigenlines of the exterior marked actions. A Reidemeister homology isomorphism intertwining those actions must carry each eigenline to the line with the same signs, and cannot kill it. Thus it carries each orientation class to a nonzero multiple of the class with the induced orientation. This argument covers every orientation and exterior connectivity of RIII without an omitted case census.

In the basis $a,b$ the Morse maps are $\eta_L(1)=\tfrac12(a-b)$, $m_L(aa)=2a$, $m_L(bb)=-2b$, $m_L(ab)=m_L(ba)=0$, $\Delta_L(a)=aa$, $\Delta_L(b)=bb$, and $\epsilon_L(a)=\epsilon_L(b)=1$. The black-right rule of [F5] then assigns equal labels exactly when the segment arrows are opposite, and different labels exactly when they agree; inspect the two possible strip colors, which exchange both labels. An orientation extends across an oriented band exactly in the opposite-arrow case. The exterior checkerboard colors remain fixed, so the surviving equal label is the canonical label after the saddle. This includes segments on the same circle, nested circles or disjoint circles. A birth creates precisely the two possibilities with nonzero coefficients. A split or a band within one surface component extends its orientation uniquely and multiplies its coefficient by a nonzero scalar. A band joining distinct components retains precisely the compatible choices and kills the others: each orientation of the joined component restricts to a unique compatible pair, so no two retained terms cancel. For a death the disappearing boundary circle belongs to a surface component with another boundary, unless that component becomes closed. A closed component of a partial surface cannot later join another component, and would be a closed component of $S$; connectedness and its incoming boundary exclude this. Thus distinct permitted orientations remain distinct on the surviving boundary after a death, and $\epsilon_L(a)=\epsilon_L(b)=1$ preserves their nonzero coefficients. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

For the empty link diagram, use its single empty resolution state and empty tensor term $\mathbb Q$ in cohomological and quantum degree $0$, with zero differential. Its induced decreasing filtration is $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ for $p\leq0$ and $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $p>0$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nonempty oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Its rational Lee homology is a two-dimensional vector space. For every finite regular diagram of $K$, the two homology classes obtained from the two orientations by the oriented-resolution parity-of-nesting rule form a basis, and the induced quantum filtration is independent of the diagram.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented knot $K$, let $V_K$ be its two-dimensional rational Lee homology with the diagram-independent induced decreasing quantum filtration $F^pV_K$. For a nonzero class $x\in V_K$, define its filtration level by
$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

Fix the orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ chosen for the mirror convention in the oriented connected-sum definition. If $K$ is a smooth oriented knot, its mirror $r(K)$ carries the orientation induced from $K$ by $r$. The reverse mirror of $K$, denoted $K^\dagger$, is the image $r(K)$ with its knot orientation reversed. Thus $K^\dagger$ changes both the ambient orientation convention and the orientation of the knot.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: On $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$ use $\langle u,v\rangle=\epsilon_L(uv)$, whose matrix in the basis $1,X$ is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Thus $1,X$ are dual labels of opposite quantum degrees. The displayed Frobenius maps give $\langle m(a,b),c\rangle=\langle a\otimes b,\Delta(c)\rangle$ on the eight basis triples, and the analogous split identity follows by transposition. Number the crossings identically on $D$ and its mirror. For a mirror vertex $w$, its corresponding original vertex is $v=1-w$. The local smoothing chart interchanges A and B under reflection, so their resolved circles agree. On the dual complex put $(C^\vee)^i=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(C^{-i},\mathbb Q)$ and $d^\vee=(d)^*$; this convention squares to zero directly. For the mirror edge changing coordinate $j$, the original reversed edge has sign $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$, while its mirror sign is $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}w_k}=(-1)^{j-1}(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$. Multiply the tensor-pairing identification on mirror vertex $w$ by $\sigma(w)=(-1)^{\sum_j(j-1)w_j}$. Since $\sigma(w+e_j)/\sigma(w)=(-1)^{j-1}$, this makes every edge commute with the transposed original edge. It is therefore an actual cochain isomorphism, including cube signs. With $n=n_++n_-$, complementation gives $i'=-i$ and state shift $|w|+n'_{+}-2n'_{-}=-|v|-n_++2n_-$, the negative original shift. Dual tensor labels have opposite label degrees as well, giving $q'=-q$. Reversing the knot orientation leaves crossing signs and resolutions unchanged, so the same isomorphism applies to $K^\dagger$.

For a finite filtered cochain complex $C$, the just-described dual quantum filtration is $F^pC^\vee=\operatorname{Ann}(F^{1-p}C)$ in complementary cohomological degrees. Evaluation induces a perfect pairing $H(C^\vee)\times H(C)\to\mathbb Q$: cocycles are exactly the functionals vanishing on boundaries, and coboundaries are exactly those vanishing on cycles, by finite elimination. Its induced homology filtration is exactly the annihilator filtration. Indeed one direction follows by evaluating representatives. Conversely a homology functional vanishing on classes represented by cycles in $F^{1-p}C$ defines a functional on the sum of the cycle space and $F^{1-p}C$, using its given values on cycles and zero on the latter subspace. The intersection condition makes this well-defined. Extend it across a finite vector-space complement; it is a cocycle because it vanishes on boundaries and represents the required dual class in $F^p$. Thus the finite homology graded quotients occur in opposite degrees under duality. Applied to the two Lee lines, $s_{\max}(K^\dagger)=-s_{\min}(K)$ and $s_{\min}(K^\dagger)=-s_{\max}(K)$. By [A1] and [F2], $s_{\max}(K)=s(K)+1$ and $s_{\min}(K)=s(K)-1$, so $s(K^\dagger)=s_{\max}(K^\dagger)-1=-s(K)$. This finite basis argument adds no choice assumption.
