citations.quote:
Work in the smooth category inherited from the oriented-link convention. In particular, an embedded bridge witness disk means the image of a smooth rank-two embedding of a planar disk, with ordinary smooth boundary or smooth transverse corners at its two marked endpoints; smoothness at a boundary or corner means local smooth extension in its charts. Witness parametrizations can be chosen for the finite disk families. This category convention does not require the knot arcs to meet the Heegaard surface transversely: tangential smooth crossings remain permitted.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $h$, let $k\ge1$, and put $m=h+k-1$. A **handlebody** is a compact three-manifold that is a regular neighborhood of a finite connected graph. A **$2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for $S^3$** consists of a splitting $S^3=U_{\alpha}\cup_{\Sigma}U_{\beta}$ into handlebodies, two systems $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)$ and $\boldsymbol\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m)$ of pairwise disjoint simple closed curves on $\Sigma$ that bound pairwise disjoint properly embedded disks in $U_{\alpha}$ and $U_{\beta}$, respectively, cutting each handlebody into exactly $k$ three-balls, and two ordered sets of distinct points $\mathbf w=(w_1,\ldots,w_k)$ and $\mathbf z=(z_1,\ldots,z_k)$ disjoint from the curves. Curves from different systems intersect transversely in finitely many points. Each component of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$ contains exactly one $w$-point and exactly one $z$-point. The diagram also includes trivial arc systems in the two handlebodies: the $\alpha$-arcs join $w_i$ to $z_i$, and the $\beta$-arcs join $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$, with indices modulo $k$. Each system is disjoint from its compression disks and is simultaneously boundary parallel: its arcs cobound pairwise disjoint embedded disks with arcs in the corresponding components of the attaching-system complement on $\Sigma$. Thus each ball obtained by compression contains one unknotted arc. Together the arcs form an oriented knot, oriented from $w_i$ to $z_i$ in $U_{\alpha}$ and from $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$ in $U_{\beta}$. The diagram is **compatible with $K$** when this knot is orientation-preservingly ambient isotopic to $K$. For a grid diagram, compatibility uses the row and column orientation fixed in the grid definition, with $w$-points at $O$ and $z$-points at $X$. For a grid representing one knot, the basepoint pairs can be numbered cyclically in reverse order of travel along the oriented knot so that $w_i,z_i$ lie in the same component $A_i$ of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and $w_i,z_{i+1}$ lie in the same component $B_i$ of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$.

Comparisons of these embedded diagrams allow **orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms**: an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of $S^3$ carrying the two handlebodies, their oriented Heegaard surface, the two attaching systems, the ordered $w,z$ points, and the two simultaneously boundary-parallel arc systems to the corresponding data. Equivalently one may specify the surface isomorphism together with its compatible collared extensions over both handlebodies carrying those arcs. The attaching systems are carried as systems; reordering their curve factors induces the corresponding product identification. Comparisons also allow **arc normalizations in the fixed splitting**: a smooth isotopy of the represented oriented knot, supported near the ordered marks and fixing each mark, during which every open connecting arc stays in its original handlebody and the two simultaneous boundary-parallel witness systems are retained or replaced by embedded witnesses for those same arcs. The surface, attaching curves, marked points and compression disks stay fixed. Such a normalization may replace a tangential marked crossing by a transverse one; the original data are not required to have neat arcs. This is a change of knot representative relative to the fixed surface, not a diagram isomorphism carrying both objects. Analytic and assigned grading data depending on the fixed surface diagram can be kept identical; the corresponding generator and disk-count identification is then the identity. Existence of normalizations with the required witnesses is a separate geometric assertion, not part of this definition. Such a comparison transports the represented oriented knot and any specified Seifert surface as well. For analytic data, it transports $j$, the surface area form, all chosen divisor neighborhoods and $J_t$ by the induced symmetric-product diffeomorphism. The comparison maps on generators and disk classes are their pushforwards under this map; compatibility with the count differential is a mathematical property to be proved. No identity action is part of this convention, even when the ambient diffeomorphism is isotopic to the identity.

The $m$-fold symmetric product $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)=\Sigma^m/S_m$ is the space of unordered $m$-tuples of points of $\Sigma$, where $S_m$ permutes coordinates. Let $q:\Sigma^m\to\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ be the quotient map. The product tori are the images $\mathbb T_{\alpha}=q(\alpha_1\times\cdots\times\alpha_m)$ and $\mathbb T_{\beta}=q(\beta_1\times\cdots\times\beta_m)$. Their intersection points are the generators. A **Whitney disk class** $\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)$ is a relative homotopy class of maps from a disk to $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ whose two boundary arcs lie on $\mathbb T_{\alpha}$ and $\mathbb T_{\beta}$ and whose endpoints are $\mathbf x$ and $\mathbf y$. Its domain is the integral two-chain of complementary regions with coefficients equal to local multiplicities. Write $n_{w_i}(\phi)$ and $n_{z_i}(\phi)$ for its local multiplicities at the marked points. An almost complex structure $J$ on $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ is a smooth endomorphism of the tangent bundle with $J^2=-1$. Fix a complex structure $j$ and an area form on $\Sigma$. For $m>0$, choose a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ of nearly symmetric almost complex structures, constant near $t=0,1$: each $J_t$ agrees with the induced integrable structure $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(j)$ on a fixed neighborhood of the diagonal and of every divisor $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$ for a chosen interior point $p$ of every complementary region, including every marked point, and tames the form descended from the product area form off that neighborhood. The path is a sufficiently small perturbation in this class. For $m=0$ the symmetric product is a point. Local multiplicities are intersection numbers with these divisors; positivity is a mathematical property to be proved, not an additional choice of disk counts. A $\mathbb J$-holomorphic strip representative is a smooth map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ satisfying $\partial_{\tau}u+J_t(u)\partial_tu=0$, with $u(\tau,0)\in\mathbb T_{\alpha}$, $u(\tau,1)\in\mathbb T_{\beta}$, and limits $\mathbf x,\mathbf y$ as $\tau\to-\infty,+\infty$. Translation in $\tau$ defines an $\mathbb R$-action. The Maslov index $\mu(\phi)$ is the Fredholm index of the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator at a representative of $\phi$; the relative Maslov grading convention is $M(\mathbf x)-M(\mathbf y)=\mu(\phi)-2\sum_{i=1}^{k}n_{w_i}(\phi)$, up to one overall additive constant.

A **periodic domain** is an integral two-chain in the complementary regions whose boundary is an integral sum of full $\alpha$- and $\beta$-curves; its local multiplicity at a marked point is the coefficient of the containing region. The pointed diagram is **admissible** when every nonzero periodic domain with $n_{w_i}=0$ for all $i$ has at least one positive and at least one negative region coefficient. A path $\mathbb J$ is **regular for a set of disk classes** when the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator at every holomorphic-strip representative in those classes is surjective. For a path regular on the classes used, let $\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)$ be the space of strip representatives. If, for each generator $\mathbf x$, only finitely many pairs $(\mathbf y,\phi)$ with $\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)\ne\varnothing$, $\mu(\phi)=1$, and $n_{w_i}(\phi)\ge0$ for every $i$ occur, and each quotient is finite, the multipointed full filtered minus module is the free module over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$ generated by $\mathbb T_{\alpha}\cap\mathbb T_{\beta}$, with differential
$$\partial^-\mathbf x=\sum_{\mathbf y}\sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\mathbf y),\;\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)\ne\varnothing\\\mu(\phi)=1,\; n_{w_i}(\phi)\ge0\ \forall i}}\#_2\bigl(\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)/\mathbb R\bigr)\,U_1^{n_{w_1}(\phi)}\cdots U_k^{n_{w_k}(\phi)}\mathbf y.$$
Here $\#_2$ is the count modulo two of the zero-dimensional quotient when it is finite. Quotienting by all $U_i$ leaves the fully blocked multipointed chain complex (the hat chain complex when $k=1$), with terms only from classes satisfying $n_{w_i}=0$ for every $i$; its Alexander-filtered associated-graded complex further retains only classes with every $n_{z_i}=0$. The relative Alexander grading convention is $A(\mathbf x)-A(\mathbf y)=\sum_i n_{z_i}(\phi)-\sum_i n_{w_i}(\phi)$, with an overall additive constant. Each $U_i$ lowers Maslov grading by two and Alexander filtration by one. In a grid diagram, $\Sigma=T^2$, $h=1$, $k=n$, and $m=n$; the horizontal circles are the $\alpha$-curves, the vertical circles are the $\beta$-curves, and the $w$-points and $z$-points are the $O$- and $X$-markings respectively.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be any admissible $2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with transverse attaching curves, product tori, and marked points as specified in the pointed-data definition. Admissibility means every nonzero periodic domain with all $w$-multiplicities zero has both positive and negative region coefficients. There is a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$, constant near its endpoints and chosen among perturbations for which all holomorphic-strip representatives used in the differential have nonnegative local multiplicity at every marked point, such that the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective for every Maslov-index-$1$ strip class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative. Each corresponding moduli space modulo translation is finite. For every Maslov-index-$2$ class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative, the compactification of the one-dimensional moduli space modulo translation has as codimension-one boundary broken pairs of index-one strips meeting at an intermediate generator and disk bubbles whose entire boundary lies on one of the product tori (the boundary-degeneration strata). Gluing gives a collar at every broken end, and the boundary-degeneration contributions cancel modulo two in the differential-square count. No sphere bubbling or escape through a nonzero periodic domain gives an additional codimension-one end. Consequently the disk-count differential in the pointed-data definition squares to zero and preserves its Alexander filtration.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume countable choice. Let $K_0,K_1\subset S^3$ be smooth oriented knots. A smooth oriented knot cobordism from $K_0$ to $K_1$ is a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ whose boundary is $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$, with product collars at both ends. A **generic movie** for $\Sigma$ is obtained by choosing a generic projection of the slices $S^3\times\{t\}$ to the plane and a Morse height function on $\Sigma$, then recording the oriented link diagram at each regular level. Intermediate regular levels may be links with any finite number of components. After choosing the projection and height generically, the finitely many exceptional levels are isolated and distinct: between them the diagrams change by planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move, and at them the surface height has one nondegenerate minimum (a birth), one nondegenerate maximum (a death), or one index-one critical point (a saddle band move). A movie includes its ordered list of frames and these elementary changes; no claim that two movies of the same cobordism are equivalent is part of this definition.

Assume countable choice. Fix $\infty\in S^3$, put $A=\{\infty\}\times[0,1]$, and identify its complement with $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$. Let $S_0,S_1$ be compact smooth oriented link cobordisms disjoint from $A$, with the same fixed boundary parametrizations and product collars. If they are ambient isotopic in $S^3\times[0,1]$ relative to those collars, then their comparison factors into finitely many ambient isotopies supported in the Euclidean complement and finitely many local sheet passages through $A$. Each sheet passage occurs at a regular surface-height point and gives the sweep-around move: in planar movies, a closing arc for a one-interval tangle travels over the tangle to the opposite side and returns underneath, or the inverse, retaining its orientation. All end collars remain fixed. No assertion that a sweep-around is generated by the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito moves, or that any homology map respects it, is made.

Assume countable choice. Let two finite generic planar movies represent compact smooth oriented surfaces in $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$, with the same parametrized boundary and product collars. If their embedded surfaces are ambient isotopic with compact support relative to those collars, then the two movies are related by a finite sequence of the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito local types, distant interchanges of disjoint elementary movie events, and planar isotopies. All orientations and omitted-coordinate crossing orders are retained. This statement concerns Euclidean isotopies; it supplies no sweep-around relation.

Use coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$ on Euclidean space-time, with projection $(x,y,z,t)\mapsto(x,y,t)$; $z$ records the crossing order. A local movie move replaces the movies on the two sides of an isolated value $\lambda=0$ in a one-parameter deformation of a projected surface, with the surface and its collars unchanged outside the indicated region. Coordinates and cutoffs are chosen so the two movies have identical boundary frames. The following list specifies the fifteen Carter–Saito types, with their usual numbering. Include both directions, reflections, all compatible strand orientations, and every crossing order allowed by distinct $z$-coordinates. The quadratic and higher-order formulas specify the local topological models; sufficiently small perturbations with the same nonzero derivative signs give the same type.

| Type | Local change of the movie |
|---|---|
| MM1, MM2 | A pair of inverse R1 events is created or removed. In regular-height source coordinates $(v,t)$ the projected curve has local form $(v^2,(t^2-\lambda)v+c v^3)$, $c\ne0$; the two signs of $c$ relative to the quadratic term give the two types. |
| MM3, MM4 | A pair of inverse R2 events is created or removed. After the two projected branches are made graphs, their normal difference is $x^2+t^2-\lambda$ or $x^2-t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM5 | A pair of inverse R3 events is created or removed. With the intersection of two strands continued as the reference point, the signed displacement of the third strand is $t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM6 | An R3 event passes an R2 event: at the projected triple point exactly two projected tangents become parallel, with nonzero quadratic contact and nonzero relative deformation velocity. |
| MM7 | An R2 event meets a branch endpoint of the double-curve locus of an R1 picture. In projected coordinates use $(v^2,tv+\lambda v^3+v^5)$; its double pairs have $r=v^2\ge0$ and $t=-\lambda r-r^2$, so a critical point of the double-curve height enters or leaves through $r=0$. |
| MM8 | A third strand passes the branch point of an R1 picture; superpose a transverse strand on the ordinary cusp unfolding and move its displacement across zero. |
| MM9 | Two R2 critical levels merge and disappear, or are created, at a cubic inflection of the double curve: the branch-difference model is $x^3+\lambda x-t$. |
| MM10 | Four sheets meet at one projected point, with distinct omitted heights. Resolving the quadruple point in the two deformation directions gives the tetrahedral pair of R3 movies. |
| MM11 | A cancelling pair of surface Morse critical points is born or dies. The surface-height model is $u^2+v^3-\lambda v$, allowing both signs of the nondegenerate square and time reversal. |
| MM12 | At an extremum of surface height the projection of its tangent plane has rank one. A local embedded model is $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2+v^2)$; the two movies interchange the extremum with its adjacent R1 picture. |
| MM13 | The corresponding interaction at a saddle, with embedded model $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2-v^2)$. |
| MM14 | A projected strand passes a surface minimum or maximum: superpose an independently displaced regular sheet on the extremum picture. |
| MM15 | The corresponding projected strand passage across a saddle band. |

A **distant interchange** exchanges the order of two elementary movie events with disjoint spatial supports, including Reidemeister events and Morse events; it is not restricted to two critical points of the smooth surface-height function. A planar isotopy of a whole movie and the insertion or removal of stationary frames do not count as additional local types. Sweep-around is a separate spherical operation, absent from this Euclidean list.

The comparison is a finite sequence of Euclidean isotopies and isolated sweep-around events, with the same parametrized boundary. At the intermediate cuts choose generic movies fixed on the retained collars; the same finite-jet construction in [F3] applies with these cuts protected.

On each Euclidean isotopy interval, [F3] replaces its comparison by finitely many of the fifteen local moves, distant interchanges and planar isotopies. Every retained frame is a regular frame of a generic traced surface, and every elementary replacement has its stated oriented local trace with the same outside and boundary data. Consequently all intermediate movies have the prescribed parametrized knots and collars. The total sequence starts and ends at the given movies and proves the claimed spherical comparison.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

Let an object be a finite disjoint union of smooth embedded circles in the oriented plane $\mathbb R^2$, including the empty union. A cobordism from $C_0$ to $C_1$ is a compact smooth orientable surface properly embedded in $\mathbb R^2\times[0,1]$, with boundary $C_0\times\{0\}\sqcup C_1\times\{1\}$, product collars at those boundaries, and no other boundary. Surfaces are identified up to ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary collars. Compose cobordisms by gluing along their common boundary circles; the identity of $C$ is $C\times[0,1]$, and disjoint union gives the monoidal product.

Take the free abelian group on these isotopy classes as each morphism group, and extend composition bilinearly. Let $\mathsf{Cob}_3$ be the resulting preadditive monoidal category before local relations are imposed. Quotient its morphism groups by the following local relations, which are required to hold inside every surrounding cobordism. A sphere component is zero (the S relation). Adding a disjoint torus component multiplies a cobordism by $2$ (the T relation). For four disjoint disk patches numbered $1,2,3,4$, write $S_{ij}$ for the surface obtained by deleting the interiors of patches $i,j$ and joining their boundary circles by an orientable tube; the four-tube relation is $S_{12}+S_{34}=S_{13}+S_{24}$. The resulting preadditive monoidal quotient category is denoted $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$.

derivations.claim: By the assumed functoriality of $F$, gluing cobordisms is sent to composition of maps and disjoint union is sent to tensor product. Thus the only additional relations to check before factoring through the quotient are the three local relations in [F2].

A sphere is evaluated by $\epsilon\eta$, and $\epsilon(\eta(1))=\epsilon(1)=0$. A torus is evaluated by $\epsilon m\Delta\eta$; on the generator $1$, $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, then $m\Delta(1)=2X$, and $\epsilon(2X)=2$. These are exactly the S and T relations, including when glued into any surrounding cobordism because the TQFT respects composition and tensor product.

In the four-tube relation, each side consists locally of two ways to attach one tube. Applying the TQFT to the local four-disk input $1$, either side gives
$$
X\otimes1\otimes1\otimes1+ 1\otimes X\otimes1\otimes1+ 1\otimes1\otimes X\otimes1+ 1\otimes1\otimes1\otimes X.
$$
This follows by applying $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$ at each tube attachment and $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$ at the two cut disks. The equality on the local input implies equality as maps: tensoring with identity maps and composing with the maps for the unchanged part of the surface preserves equality. Thus the four-tube relation is respected.

Every generating local relation of $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$ is respected by steps 1.2 and 1.3, while the Frobenius identities respect the isotopy and gluing presentation by step 1.1. Therefore the TQFT factors through the quotient defining $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$, as asserted.

With these paths, compatible coherent source-dependent polygon perturbations can be chosen generically, relative to their faces and any regular parameter endpoints. Assume Countable Choice. Fix finitely many labelled attaching-circle families on a closed oriented surface with positive area form, finitely many protected points off all circles, and one witness point in every complementary region. Circles within a family are disjoint. Circles in different families are transverse, so their labelled pair intersections are finite; common points of three or more families are initially permitted.

Arbitrarily small smooth Hamiltonian isotopies of the individual families, supported away from all the protected and witness points, give pairwise transverse representatives with NO point on three curves from different families. Their pair intersections are canonically followed through the small isotopies, without birth or death. When the corresponding product tori have common POSITIVE rank $m>0$, no point belongs to three DISTINCT torus labels. At rank zero the empty product tori all equal the point of $\operatorname{Sym}^0\Sigma$; no exclusion of their triple intersection is claimed, and their source-dependent target transport is the identity. The complete disk-cut and based-link data can be transported by the family isotopies; no topology of the underlying handlebodies is changed.

Full-curve periodic-domain lattices and their sublattices generated by pairwise periodic domains transport bijectively by the swept annuli. All coefficients at the original witness and protected points are unchanged. Consequently any strict weak or strong admissibility criterion witnessed by these coefficients is preserved, when its indexing and linear evaluation are transported under this lattice map. Identification of that evaluation with a geometric Spin-c or Fredholm quantity is a separate topological assertion, not part of this lemma.

For an actual boundary-marked polygon source, the relative map spaces with fixed corresponding corner labels are homeomorphic by an actual smooth source-dependent target isotopy. It is the identity near protected incidence divisors and the diagonal and is fixed in the longitudinal coordinate on each far end. This induces bijections on literal continuous relative homotopy classes, without quotienting by a fundamental-group action. No symmetric power of a nonholomorphic surface map is used as a global smooth target map. For smooth fixed-end reference maps the transported actual Fredholm index is unchanged. These are class and admissibility transports, not an equality of holomorphic counts or an isotopy-invariance theorem.

Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma$ be an oriented genus-$h$ surface, let $k\ge1$ and $m=h+k-1$, and give $q\ge3$ balanced attaching systems $\boldsymbol\eta^0,\ldots,\boldsymbol\eta^{q-1}$ of $m$ circles. Supply their disjoint compression disks in oriented handlebodies $U_i$, their compatible Morse functions with $k$ index-zero and $m$ index-one critical points, and $k$ distinct points $\mathbf w$ with one in each cut component of every system. Distinct systems meet transversely and finitely. Use the usual product tori in $\operatorname{Sym}^m\Sigma$. Let $W$ be the oriented polygon cobordism obtained from the polygon times $\Sigma$ by attaching $e_i\times U_i$ along $e_i\times\Sigma$, with rounded corners. A realized Whitney polygon is a continuous disk map with these successive torus edges and specified corner generators; no holomorphic representative is assumed.

The finite Morse construction below assigns such a class $u$ a Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s_{\mathbf w}(u)$ on $W$, restricting to the specified Morse labels of its corners. If $u,v$ have the same corners, their domain difference $P=D(u)-D(v)$ has boundary an integral sum of full attaching circles. Capping those circles with the supplied disks along polygon legs gives a class $H(P)\in H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$. With the common source/surface orientations, their Spin-c difference is
$$\mathfrak s_{\mathbf w}(u)-\mathfrak s_{\mathbf w}(v)=j\operatorname{PD}_W H(P),$$
where $j:H^2(W,\partial W;\mathbb Z)\to H^2(W;\mathbb Z)$. The sign is fixed by the positive index-one/index-two gradient modification having determinant degree $+2$ on a positive transverse disk.

In particular, if the two Spin-c structures and every $w$-multiplicity agree, then $P$ is a sum of actual doubly-periodic domains for the adjacent Heegaard pairs, each with all $w$-multiplicities zero. For a triangle these are the $\alpha\beta$, $\beta\gamma$ and $\alpha\gamma$ pairs. Their capped classes need not be zero individually. Fixed all $w,z$ multiplicities imply this hypothesis without any extra normalization convention.

The construction is compatible with gluing polygons along a common Heegaard boundary. Compatible Spin-c structures on the pieces have the usual extension orbit under the image of $H^1$ of that common boundary in $H^2$ of the glued cobordism; no unique extension is asserted. Along an actual continuous class-preserving family and its actual neck-smoothing, the assigned total Spin-c structure is constant, and the glued pieces recover that total extension, not an arbitrarily chosen member of the orbit. Point-divisor multiplicity vectors at every supplied $w,z$ mark add under these actual gluings. These assertions do not supply an analytic compactification or a gluing existence theorem. For supplied small attaching-curve isotopies away from the marks, transport the compatible Morse data in the actual handlebody collars and supply a continuous transport of the polygon maps. On the unchanged cobordism this carries their Spin-c labels and capped periodic classes, including torsion information. If one witness point in every old region misses the swept curves, all coefficients at those witnesses are unchanged. Hence strict strong admissibility, and the corresponding sector or global weak witness conditions, pass to the transported lattice. No existence of the continuous polygon-map transport is inferred from the mere isotopy of its boundary curves.

The statement does not identify all literal Whitney classes with their domains, divide genus-two classes by a sphere action, assert finiteness of classes with one domain, or supply any analytic count or Maslov-index formula. The point target $m=0$ has only the constant map and the domain conclusion is zero.

Assume countable choice and the actual finite balanced polygon data, a Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s$ on $W$, and one realized reference polygon $u_0$. Let $L$ be the lattice of formal integral periodic region chains $Q$ with $j\operatorname{PD}H(Q)=0$, and let $G\subset L$ impose zero multiplicity at every $w_l$. On $G$ put $\ell(P)=\langle c_1(\mathfrak s),H(P)\rangle/2$. The values of $\ell$ are integers. Assume the strict strong-admissibility condition
$$0\ne P\in G,\quad\ell(P)=N\ge0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\max_R P(R)>N.$$
Then the relative-index functional
$$\nu(Q)=\langle c_1(\mathfrak s),H(Q)\rangle+2\sum_l n_{w_l}(Q)$$
is strictly positive on every nonzero nonnegative direction in $L$. The nonnegative domains of actual same-corner, same-Spin-c polygons have a finite lower relative-index bound. For every integer $K$, only finitely many such nonnegative integral domains have relative index at most $K$. These statements concern domains, not the number of literal homotopy classes or holomorphic maps with one domain. They apply to actual Fredholm indices when the fixed-cap relative-index identification has been supplied.

For a boundary-pair sector the same conclusions hold with $L$ the FULL pair-periodic lattice, $G$ its all-mark-zero sublattice, and the Chern evaluation taken on its capped class in $Y$. Thus every nonempty fixed-end strip sector has a lower actual index bound $L_0$ and finitely many nonnegative domains of indices in $[L_0,K]$. For fixed attaching curves, marks and labels these bounds and finite sets are independent of the Cauchy–Riemann coefficients, auxiliary family parameters and source conformal parameters satisfying the same index conventions; they depend only on the finite domain lattice and Chern functional. No uniformity under an unspecified change of attaching curves is asserted.

There is also a weaker fixed-index statement. If every nonzero $P\in G$ with $\ell(P)=0$ has both signs, then at a fixed entire mark vector and any fixed finite set of relative indices there are only finitely many nonnegative domains in the fixed Spin-c sector. For supplied actual strip classes the pair version also holds under the separate weaker condition testing mixed signs only on REALIZED normalized index-zero periodic classes. Ordinary weakness for a specified Spin-c sector instead tests ALL formal normalized periodic domains with Chern evaluation zero, even when that sector has no generators; whenever an actual generator is supplied, the actual periodic index formula shows that ordinary specified-sector weakness implies this weaker realized-class condition. This proves a finite-domain statement only for supplied actual classes; it neither establishes invariance under moves nor supplies a generator in an intended sector whose generator set is empty. It does not give an unrestricted lower index bound. Any separately supplied uniform positive area bound also bounds every nonnegative component domain and hence its index, by its finite region coefficients.

There is a separate all-Spin-c zero-mark conclusion. If every nonzero formal periodic domain with all $w$ multiplicities zero has both positive and negative coefficients, then for fixed corners and fixed zero $w$ multiplicities there are only finitely many nonnegative domains, without fixing a Spin-c structure or an index. This global multi-periodic hypothesis is not inferred from strong admissibility for one Spin-c structure or from pairwise weak admissibility. No existence or winding construction of either type of diagram is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Supply finite balanced polygon Morse data of rank $m=h+k-1\ge1$, with common $w,z$ marks, and no triple intersection of the product tori. Fix a Spin-c structure on the polygon cobordism and use the STRICT all-$w$ normalized strong admissibility condition of the named geometric lattice theorem. Use the same condition for its relevant boundary-pair sectors. The boundary systems have their actual complete $k$-ball cuts, and nearly symmetric geometry has exact constant product-angle generator charts. No $S^3$ or torsion restriction on the intermediate three-manifolds is made.

In the smooth topology, the genuine constant-collar end paths having no nonconstant strip of index at most zero and regularity for every actual index-one strip in the relevant sectors form an open dense subset of the allowed protected end paths. With these paths, compatible coherent source-dependent polygon perturbations can be chosen generically, relative to their faces and any regular parameter endpoints. Their count-dimension-zero total sets are finite, and their count-dimension-one spaces compactify to actual compact one-manifolds. All nonnegative $w,z$ degrees are retained. These conclusions hold for the fixed total Spin-c label, across all its literal realized classes; they also hold for fixed degree vectors or fixed actual classes. The boundary consists exactly of the label-compatible rigid polygon–polygon faces and strip–polygon breakings, with additive marked vectors and actual exhaustive gluing collars. No sphere or one-torus disk bubble occurs in these polygon dimensions. This includes $k=1$.

For triangles the fixed count index is $\mu$, so rigid counts have $\mu=0$ and the chain-map boundary has $\mu=1$. In a generic one-parameter triangle family with fixed regular end data the universal count index is $\mu+1$: the index-minus-one universal counts are finite, and universal index-zero spaces have the parameter endpoints and strip–triangle boundaries. Thus the finite actual counts satisfy the weighted triangle chain-map equation and its auxiliary-data chain homotopy over $\mathbb F_2$. They may be specialized to the two-color ring by sending every $w$ variable to $U$ and every $z$ variable to $V$. No top-generator cycle, handle-map inverse, arbitrary diagram invariance or absolute grading is part of this assertion.

Assume countable choice and put $R=\mathbb F_2[U,V]$. The following principle applies to free $R$-modules with specified bases and $R$-linear maps whose matrix coefficients count finite sets, each point carrying a weight $(a,b)\in\mathbb N^2$ and contributing $U^aV^b$. Require finite support for every input basis vector, so these are polynomial maps, not unspecified infinite sums. Suppose that for each input, output and total weight there is an actual compact smooth one-manifold whose boundary is in a specified weight-preserving bijection with the disjoint union of the products of counted sets occurring in an asserted identity. Product weights are the sums of the two factor weights. Additional boundary points are allowed only when equipped with a weight-preserving fixed-point-free involution. Then that identity, with every displayed term added over $\mathbb F_2$, holds coefficientwise.

In particular the principle proves $d^2=0$ when the unpaired boundary is exactly the twice-broken count defining $d^2$; proves $d_BF+Fd_A=0$ when the unpaired boundary is exactly those two broken types; and proves $F_1+F_0=d_BH+Hd_A$ when the boundary is exactly those four types. With three complexes it proves $F_{12}+F_2F_1=d_CH+Hd_A$ under the corresponding four-type boundary description. These are, respectively, the square-zero, chain-map, chain-homotopy and composition-up-to-homotopy identities. The statement assumes the actual compact manifolds, finiteness and exact boundary bijections; it supplies no analytic regularity, compactification, gluing, exhaustion or naturality theorem.

derivations.claim: Treat rank zero directly. The target and all empty product tori are one point. The fixed-map operator is the zero map from the zero section space to the zero forcing space; it is onto of index zero. The three-marked source has no conformal parameter or automorphism. Hence its unique map is a regular isolated triangle with all marked degrees zero, in its assigned constant-class Spin-c extension. With another prescribed label or a nonzero degree vector the relevant set is empty. A fixed index-one triangle or universal index-minus-one triangle cannot occur. A matching one-parameter family is exactly its compact parameter interval, with its two identical endpoint counts; there are no nonconstant strips, spheres or boundary disks. Thus its differential is zero and its triangle and parameter-boundary identities hold directly. No strip translation is divided out and no empty tuple is claimed to supply a constituent surface point.

Now suppose that $m>0$ and apply [F1] with the marked points and one witness in every original region protected. The resulting representative has no triple torus intersection and has the same followed pair generators. [F2]'s actual collar extension carries the compression disks and Morse data, identifies the actual Spin-c lift and capped classes, and preserves every old strict witness coefficient under the swept-annulus lattice isomorphism. Thus the new triple has the same required strict admissibility and Spin-c indexing. Its polygon spaces represent exactly the transported literal continuous classes, not classes modulo a sphere or fundamental-group action. A constant triangle would lie in all three tori, so none occurs. This explicitly permitted auxiliary curve choice is necessary: at a constant triangle the almost-complex parameter derivative vanishes because $du=0$, so no J-only universal argument can be substituted for it.

Apply [F3] to this actual triple and its restricted pair sectors. The geometric strict-domain theorem first supplies a finite lower strip index and finite nonnegative domains in every upper-index band. Its actual auxiliary all-index regular path and bubble budget then produce the open dense good genuine-collar end data with no nonconstant index at most zero and index-one regularity. Hence the ensuing polygon limits have the required regular strip levels; a claim of index-one regularity alone would not justify that conclusion. The source-local Hilbert perturbations give actual fixed-data and one-parameter universal transversality at every nonconstant triangle, preserving the protected divisors, tori and exact product-angle end charts. There are no constant triangles by step1.2.

A triangle has three marked ends and no conformal modulus or translation action. Its fixed count index is therefore $\mu$, and a one-parameter universal count has index $\mu+1$. The domain bounds in [F2] and actual domain-area inequality in [F3] give one energy bound for each required low-dimensional set, across all its literal classes and all nonnegative degree vectors. Every limiting nonconstant strip has positive index. Every nonconstant disk bubble contributes at least two, every sphere at least $2k$, and every regular triangle vertex has nonnegative count dimension. The unconditional determinant index budget of [F3] thus excludes all bubbles in count dimensions zero and one. The only broken one-dimensional ends have one rigid triangle and one rigid strip. The same calculation with the family parameter counted ONCE gives rigid universal index-minus-one triangles and the stated universal index-zero ends. This retains $k=1$ and general intermediate $Y$; it does not borrow a knot-in-$S^3$ disk theorem outside its scope.

The actual product-chart, correction and exhaustion proof in [F3] supplies exactly one collar for every such compatible broken pair. Its global tail estimate promotes compact-core convergence to the true Sobolev chart, so a rigid total set is compact discrete and finite under Countable Choice. Its explicit Hausdorff collar compactification of a one-dimensional space is a compact one-manifold with finite boundary. Degree vectors and the actual total Spin-c structure are carried by each neck smoothing; restricting either these labels or an actual class gives the corresponding open-and-closed part. Thus neither multiple classes with the same domain nor the Spin-c extension orbit creates a missing or an extra end.

Count the boundary of this actual compact one-manifold over $\mathbb F_2$. Writing $F$ for the bilinear triangle count, the strip breaks give $dF+F(d\otimes1)+F(1\otimes d)=0$. The marked vectors add at each actual gluing, so the component weights multiply, with every $w,z$ exponent retained. For a fixed-end one-parameter family its universal one-manifold also has the two parameter endpoints; the universal index-minus-one counts $H$ give $F_1+F_0=dH+H(d\otimes1)+H(1\otimes d)$. These are finite weighted equations, also after specializing every $w$ color to $U$ and every $z$ color to $V$. If the intermediate input $\Theta$ is an actual cycle, substituting it removes the $F(1\otimes d)$ term and gives the required one-input chain map and homotopy. Together with the direct point model in step1.1 and the raw convention [F4], this proves exactly the analytic identities. No existence or cycle property of a distinguished top input, elementary cobordism-map construction, or movie-invariance theorem has been assumed to obtain them.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with finite balanced Heegaard data satisfying the strict strong-admissibility condition normalized at all $w$-marks for each specified Spin-c sector. For positive-rank triangle pieces choose the divisor-compatible nearly symmetric regular end paths and generic source-dependent almost-complex perturbations used for the full-marked triangle counts; at rank zero use the empty-product point model. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For an elementary triangle piece with four-dimensional cobordism $W_r$ represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s|_{W_r},\\ n_{w_i}(\phi),n_{z_i}(\phi)\ge0\ \text{for every marked point}}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{\sum_i n_{w_i}(\phi)}V^{\sum_i n_{z_i}(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class on $W_r$, and all marked multiplicities in the sum are nonnegative. The restriction $\mathfrak s|_{W_r}$ is taken under the identification of this elementary cobordism with its Kirby piece. The other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

derivations.claim: Send the w-regions and z-regions of the given surface to the two colors $U,V$. The source ring is now exactly $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and its variable-power filtration is exactly the specified two-coordinate filtration. The curvature vanishes by the two-color identity. Hence [F1] applies to the actual maps of [F3] as genuine filtered equivariant chain maps, not merely as hat homology maps or uncolored counts.

For different endpoint diagrams first use [F1]'s canonical transition chain-homotopy equivalences to compare maps on the same chosen endpoint representatives. Theorem A then gives a filtered equivariant chain homotopy for any two admitted decompositions and regular auxiliary choices. The source's fourteen Cerf moves include the band, basepoint and quasi-stabilization relations; §12.5 additionally handles components missing one or both ends. Boundary-fixed ambient isotopy preserves the given decorations and induces precisely the required diffeomorphism of decorated cobordisms, so it is covered by the same theorem.

Apply [F2] to the actual gluing and the two specified structures $\mathfrak s_1,\mathfrak s_2$. Restriction of each summand to the two pieces is exactly the condition displayed in the Statement; no unmarked or total-Spin-c map has replaced these maps. The two-color specialization respects the composition and homotopies, giving the displayed formula over $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$.

Finally $H^2(S^3\times[0,1];\mathbb Z)=0$ and the product is spin. Its nonempty Spin-c torsor therefore consists of one element. If the chosen structures on the pieces restrict from this unique product structure, the extension set has that one element; otherwise it is empty. In the compatible case the law reduces to ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy. The argument imports the established naturality/composition theorems, not an unproved assertion that the local triangle identity checks all movies.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume countable choice and fix a generic movie $M$ of a smooth oriented surface cobordism $\Sigma$ from an oriented link $L_0$ to an oriented link $L_1$. For each regular frame $D$, let $Kh(D)$ be the normalized integral Khovanov homology group. The empty frame has the one-term complex $\mathbb Z$ in both gradings zero, using the empty resolution and the zero-fold tensor product. Associate to a birth the unit map $\eta:\mathbb Z\to\mathcal A$, $\eta(1)=1$; associate to a death the counit $\epsilon:\mathcal A\to\mathbb Z$, $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$; and associate to a saddle the multiplication $m:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ when two resolution circles merge, or the comultiplication $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$ when one splits. Each local map is tensored with the identity on unaffected circles. Associate to planar isotopy the induced identification of the cube complexes. For Reidemeister moves, use the following fixed Bar-Natan constructions: the kink retractions $F_+=v-\Delta$, $G_+=e$, $F_-=u$, $G_-=w-m$; the two inverse-crossing strong retractions with degree-zero inclusion $(1,ut)^T$ and projection $(1,-se)$, with their specified reverse-order cube signs; and the third-move equivalences obtained by the explicit source- or target-cone retractions onto the common six-point residual complex. Here $u,e$ are circle birth/death, $v,w$ are punctured-torus birth/death, and the saddle letters denote the actual local bands in these constructions. Use their specified inverses for the reversed moves. Insert these formal surface matrices into the fixed planar outside of the diagram, then apply the integral Frobenius cobordism functor. Normalize a state $v$ to cochain degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum shift $|v|+n_+-2n_-$. Fix the local coordinate identifications and orientation cases once, with the Koszul crossing-order correction $(-1)^{v(a)v(b)}$ when crossings $a,b$ are interchanged. These local maps are chosen once; composing them with an arbitrary automorphism of a complex is not an allowed change of representative. Compose the induced maps on homology in movie order and denote the result by $Kh(M):Kh(L_0)\to Kh(L_1)$, considered modulo multiplication by $-1$. This definition fixes a movie; independence from changing the movie is not included in the definition.

Assume countable choice. Let $P$ be a single arc in a disk and let $Z=P\sqcup O$ add a small disjoint circle next to it. Let $m:Z\to P$ merge the circle into the arc by an elementary saddle and let $\Delta:P\to Z$ be the reversed saddle. In the open Bar-Natan category the two normalized kink complexes $C_+=(Z\{1\}\xrightarrow{m}P\{2\})$ in cochain degrees $0,1$, and $C_-=(P\{-2\}\xrightarrow{\Delta}Z\{-1\})$ in degrees $-1,0$, both have explicit internal degree zero strong deformation retractions onto the one-term complex $P$ in degree zero. These retractions are preserved by insertion into an arbitrary planar surrounding complex.

Assume countable choice. In the open Bar-Natan category on four boundary points of a rectangle, let $I$ be the vertical two-strand identity pairing and let $E$ be the pairing consisting of a top cap and bottom cup. Let $t:I\to E$ and $s:E\to I$ be the elementary saddle surfaces. Define the formal crossing complexes $K_+=(I\{1\}\xrightarrow{t}E\{2\})$, in cochain degrees $0,1$, and $K_-=(E\{-2\}\xrightarrow{s}I\{-1\})$, in degrees $-1,0$. Then both planar stackings $K_+K_-$ and $K_-K_+$ have explicit internal degree zero strong deformation retractions onto the one-term complex $I$ in degree zero, with no grading shift. All maps and homotopies can be inserted into an arbitrary planar surrounding complex. Consequently adjoining either of these crossing complexes preserves simplicity in both directions.

Assume countable choice. Put six points on a disk boundary in clockwise order $1,2,3,4,5,6$, at northwest, northeast, east, southeast, southwest and west. Consider diagonal arcs $a$ from $1$ to $4$ and $b$ from $2$ to $5$, and an arc $c$ from $6$ to $3$. In the left diagram $c$ bows above the intersection of $a,b$; in the right it bows below. In both diagrams $c$ passes over both diagonals. Either $a$ passes over $b$ in both diagrams, or $b$ passes over $a$ in both. These are the two local third Reidemeister variants considered here. More precisely one can use the diameters $y=-x,y=x$ for $a,b$ and the curves $y=\pm h(1-x^2)$, $0<h<1/2$, for $c$, with fixed radial collars near the six boundary points.

Use the local smoothing chart in which the over-strand joins southwest to northeast and the under-strand joins northwest to southeast. The A-smoothing joins the left pair and right pair, and the B-smoothing joins the top pair and bottom pair. An A-first cube uses $0=A,1=B$; a B-first cube uses $0=B,1=A$. For either convention, the raw formal cube of an ordered diagram has term $\bigoplus_{|v|=s}S_v\{s\}$ in cochain degree $s$ and edge saddle coefficient $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$ in coordinate $j$. For any choice of strand orientations, put this term in degree $s-n_-$ and shift it internally by the additional $n_+-2n_-$.

For each of these two smoothing conventions, the formal cubes of the two diagrams admit internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences, with explicit maps given below. The displayed smoothing table and cone calculation use A-first cubes: turning right from an entering underpassing half-line gives the A-smoothing. The B-first maps are obtained from the raw A-first maps by complementing every bit and reversing surface time, without spatial reflection, with the explicit vertex sign correction below; only after this operation are the same given $n_+,n_-$ normalizations applied to both sides. All these maps and homotopies can be inserted into any planar surrounding complex.

Assume countable choice. In the open Bar-Natan category, let $P$ be a smoothing consisting of $k$ arcs and no circles, including $k=0$. The map $\mathbb Z\to\operatorname{End}^0(P)$ sending $n$ to $n\operatorname{id}_P$ is an isomorphism of rings. Consequently the one-term complex $P$, with any common grading shift, is simple.

In the open Bar-Natan categories, planar totalization defines operations on bounded complexes and on their homotopy categories, preserving internal degrees and homotopy equivalences. Simplicity is invariant under an internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalence. In particular let $A$ and $B$ be the operations of adjoining a fixed boundary crossing complex and its proposed inverse, each using precisely two adjacent boundary legs. Suppose local internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences of their two possible composites with the straight two-strand identity complex have been supplied. Then a complex $C$ is simple if and only if $A(C)$ is simple. This is a conditional assertion about these local inverse equivalences; it does not assert Reidemeister invariance or provide crossing complexes or their inverse maps.

Assume countable choice. Assign to births, deaths and saddles their elementary formal surfaces, and to the Reidemeister kink, inverse-crossing and third-move constructions the explicit formal retractions specified below. Then the two sides of each Euclidean Morse movie relation MM11, MM12, MM13, MM14 and MM15 induce chain maps equal up to an overall sign. This includes both directions, reflected models, all compatible orientations, and insertion into a fixed planar surrounding complex. It asserts the five Morse movie identities for those choices; it asserts no spherical sweep-around identity.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg1=1$, $\deg X=-1$, and structure maps $m,\eta,\Delta,\epsilon$ given by $\eta(1)=1$, $\epsilon(1)=0$, $\epsilon(X)=1$, $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, and $\Delta(X)=X\otimes X$. There is an additive symmetric monoidal functor $F$ from the category of closed Bar-Natan smoothing cobordisms before local relations to finite free graded abelian groups. Here closed means that objects consist of circles, including the empty collection, and there are no vertical side intervals. The target has all integral linear maps, graded by their homogeneous degrees, and its symmetry is the ordinary interchange of tensor factors, without a Koszul sign from quantum degrees.

Explicitly, $F(C)$ is the free group on the labelings of the finite circle set of $C$ by $1,X$, graded by the sum of the label degrees. For a connected surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g$, with $p$ incoming and $q$ outgoing circles, its map in any temporary ordering of those circles is $F(\Sigma)=\Delta_q H^g m_p$, where $H=m\Delta$, $m_0=\eta$, $m_1=1_{\mathcal A}$, $m_p$ is iterated multiplication for $p\ge2$, $\Delta_0=\epsilon$, $\Delta_1=1_{\mathcal A}$ and $\Delta_q$ is iterated comultiplication for $q\ge2$. For a disconnected surface, take the tensor product over its connected components and route each factor to its actual boundary circle. The empty surface is sent to $1_{\mathbb Z}$. This construction is independent of all temporary orderings, respects embedded isotopy, stacking and disjoint union, sends the elementary birth, death, merge and split to $\eta,\epsilon,m,\Delta$, and sends a surface to a homogeneous map of degree $\chi(\Sigma)$. It respects S, T and four-tube and therefore descends to the closed Bar-Natan quotient category.

Let $\mathsf{Cob}_3$ be the preadditive monoidal category of cobordisms before the S, T, and four-tube relations are imposed, and let $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$ be its quotient by those relations. Suppose $F:\mathsf{Cob}_3\to\mathsf{GrAb}$ is an additive symmetric monoidal functor to finite free graded abelian groups with all integral linear maps, graded by homogeneous degree, with a circle sent to $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, a cup to $\eta(1)=1$, a cap to $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, a merge pair of pants to $m$, and a split pair of pants to $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\ \Delta(X)=X\otimes X$. Then every sphere component is sent to zero, every disjoint torus component acts by multiplication by $2$, and the two sides of the four-tube relation induce the same map. Therefore $F$ factors through an additive symmetric monoidal functor on the preadditive quotient category $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$.

Use coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$ on Euclidean space-time, with projection $(x,y,z,t)\mapsto(x,y,t)$; $z$ records the crossing order. A local movie move replaces the movies on the two sides of an isolated value $\lambda=0$ in a one-parameter deformation of a projected surface, with the surface and its collars unchanged outside the indicated region. Coordinates and cutoffs are chosen so the two movies have identical boundary frames. The following list specifies the fifteen Carter–Saito types, with their usual numbering. Include both directions, reflections, all compatible strand orientations, and every crossing order allowed by distinct $z$-coordinates. The quadratic and higher-order formulas specify the local topological models; sufficiently small perturbations with the same nonzero derivative signs give the same type.

| Type | Local change of the movie |
|---|---|
| MM1, MM2 | A pair of inverse R1 events is created or removed. In regular-height source coordinates $(v,t)$ the projected curve has local form $(v^2,(t^2-\lambda)v+c v^3)$, $c\ne0$; the two signs of $c$ relative to the quadratic term give the two types. |
| MM3, MM4 | A pair of inverse R2 events is created or removed. After the two projected branches are made graphs, their normal difference is $x^2+t^2-\lambda$ or $x^2-t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM5 | A pair of inverse R3 events is created or removed. With the intersection of two strands continued as the reference point, the signed displacement of the third strand is $t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM6 | An R3 event passes an R2 event: at the projected triple point exactly two projected tangents become parallel, with nonzero quadratic contact and nonzero relative deformation velocity. |
| MM7 | An R2 event meets a branch endpoint of the double-curve locus of an R1 picture. In projected coordinates use $(v^2,tv+\lambda v^3+v^5)$; its double pairs have $r=v^2\ge0$ and $t=-\lambda r-r^2$, so a critical point of the double-curve height enters or leaves through $r=0$. |
| MM8 | A third strand passes the branch point of an R1 picture; superpose a transverse strand on the ordinary cusp unfolding and move its displacement across zero. |
| MM9 | Two R2 critical levels merge and disappear, or are created, at a cubic inflection of the double curve: the branch-difference model is $x^3+\lambda x-t$. |
| MM10 | Four sheets meet at one projected point, with distinct omitted heights. Resolving the quadruple point in the two deformation directions gives the tetrahedral pair of R3 movies. |
| MM11 | A cancelling pair of surface Morse critical points is born or dies. The surface-height model is $u^2+v^3-\lambda v$, allowing both signs of the nondegenerate square and time reversal. |
| MM12 | At an extremum of surface height the projection of its tangent plane has rank one. A local embedded model is $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2+v^2)$; the two movies interchange the extremum with its adjacent R1 picture. |
| MM13 | The corresponding interaction at a saddle, with embedded model $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2-v^2)$. |
| MM14 | A projected strand passes a surface minimum or maximum: superpose an independently displaced regular sheet on the extremum picture. |
| MM15 | The corresponding projected strand passage across a saddle band. |

A **distant interchange** exchanges the order of two elementary movie events with disjoint spatial supports, including Reidemeister events and Morse events; it is not restricted to two critical points of the smooth surface-height function. A planar isotopy of a whole movie and the insertion or removal of stationary frames do not count as additional local types. Sweep-around is a separate spherical operation, absent from this Euclidean list.

Fix a based closed disk $D$ and a finite even subset $B\subset\partial D$. A smoothing is a compact smooth one-manifold in $D$, with boundary precisely $B$ and fixed radial collars there; it may contain circles. A morphism from $P$ to $Q$ is a compact orientable, not separately oriented, smooth surface with corners in $D\times[0,1]$, with bottom $P$, top $Q$, side boundary $B\times[0,1]$ and fixed product collars. Identify surfaces by ambient isotopy relative to these boundary collars. Take free abelian morphism groups, compose by stacking, and impose the following relations in every surrounding surface: a sphere component is zero; a torus component may be deleted with factor $2$; and $C_{12}+C_{34}=C_{13}+C_{24}$, where $C_{ij}$ attaches a tube between disk patches $i,j$ among four disjoint patches in a ball. Denote the resulting category by $\mathcal C(B)$.

For a surface $C$ set $\deg C=\chi(C)-|B|/2$. Permit formal shifts $P\{a\}$, with a surface of degree $e$ having degree $e+b-a$ as a map $P\{a\}\to Q\{b\}$. Take finite direct sums with matrices of morphisms. A complex is a bounded cochain complex in this additive category, whose differential has internal degree zero. A chain map has cochain degree zero; all homotopies have cochain degree $-1$. Unless specified otherwise, maps and homotopies have internal degree zero. Two chain maps are homotopic when $f-g=dh+hd$. Write $K(B)$ for the category with these complexes as objects and chain maps modulo homotopy as morphisms. Call a complex simple if its invertible endomorphisms in $K(B)$ of internal degree zero are exactly the two maps $\pm\operatorname{id}$ (allowing coincidence when the object is zero).

A planar template is a disk with finitely many numbered input disks removed and a properly embedded one-manifold of arcs and circles in the remainder, meeting each boundary in its prescribed marked points. It acts on smoothings by insertion, and on surfaces by insertion in the template crossed with $[0,1]$. Extend by multilinearity to finite sums. For ordered complexes $C_1,\ldots,C_s$ its totalization has term $\bigoplus_{r_1+\cdots+r_s=r}D(C_1^{r_1},\ldots,C_s^{r_s})$, with shifts added, and differential $\sum_i(-1)^{r_1+\cdots+r_{i-1}}D(1,\ldots,d_i,\ldots,1)$ on that summand. For homogeneous maps $f_i$ of cochain degrees $a_i$, use the sign $(-1)^{\sum_i a_i\sum_{j<i}r_j}$ on $D(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$, evaluated on the input summand of degrees $(r_j)$; this is the usual tensor sign convention, independently of the internal grading.

derivations.claim: **Inverse clips.** For MM1–MM5, a Reidemeister move is followed by its selected inverse, possibly with a planar change of frame between them. The equations in [F2] make the composite homotopic to the identity. All reflections and compatible strand orientations use the corresponding specified local coordinate identification in [F1]; the cochain and internal shifts agree at both ends. Thus the five inverse clips satisfy their formal movie relation before any closed evaluation.

**Simple base frames for the five circular clips.** Each of MM6–MM10 consists solely of Reidemeister moves, so it gives a degree-zero homotopy automorphism of its starting tangle complex by [F2]. The following explicit starting frames of the models in [F7] are simple. For MM7 choose the frame before the small cusp loop: it is a single bent arc, hence a pairing. For MM8 choose the frame before the cusp crosses the third strand: its two arcs have one transverse crossing and no small loop; peeling this sole boundary crossing leaves a pairing. For MM9 choose the frame before the cubic double-curve turn: it likewise has two arcs with one crossing, which peels off at the boundary. The MM6 starting frame is two parallel arcs crossed by a third transverse arc. Its two crossings peel in order from an end of the transverse arc, leaving three disjoint arcs. More explicitly, the outermost crossing has two adjacent free legs in the disk boundary; cut a small collar rectangle containing that crossing and those legs, leaving one boundary-crossing addition to the smaller tangle. After removing it the other crossing has the same property. For MM10 the initial frame is the four small affine strand segments resolving the projected quadruple point, with six pairwise crossings. Choose a linear height not perpendicular to any segment and place upper and lower cuts beyond all six crossings. Each segment is a graph over that height. Order the six crossing heights after a small planar perturbation; the highest crossing is between adjacent outgoing strands, so its two free legs give a boundary-crossing collar rectangle. Remove it and repeat down the ordered list. This peels all six crossings and leaves a pairing, for every retained over/under order. These cuts merely parametrize the local disk and straighten its outside arcs; no crossing change is used. Thus the boundary-crossing equivalences in [F4] and [F2], beginning with [F3], prove simplicity of all five base frames. Starting the same circular clip at a different frame conjugates its endomorphism by a product of equivalences, so [F4] also gives simplicity there.

**The five Morse clips.** For MM11 use the explicit disk cancellation. For MM12 and MM13 use the two columns $D_a-T,D_b-T$ and the integral identity $D_a+D_b=2T$; the upward clips have their separately checked cap/saddle maps. For MM14 use its two circle-birth columns, with the reverse-order RII cube sign retained in both. For MM15 use the residual saddle column $(\alpha,\beta)^T$, or its actual target-retract row in the upward version, with the middle cube permutation and last-vertex sign. These are exactly the five proved calculations of [F5]. Hence the two formal maps agree up to a single sign for every nonreversible clip as well.

**Circular clips.** The degree-zero homotopy automorphism of each MM6–MM10 base frame is therefore homotopic to $\varepsilon1$, where $\varepsilon=1$ or $-1$. This is one scalar in the formal endomorphism group of the whole local complex, not a separate sign on its states. Changing a base frame conjugates that equation by equivalences and preserves the same assertion. A relation presented as two alternative paths is equivalent to its circular clip: compose one path with the selected inverse of the other; its homotopy inverse exists by [F2]. Multiplying the circular equation by the other path therefore makes the two path maps equal up to this one sign. This proves all five circular relations without assuming that arbitrary maps between two homology groups agree up to sign.

**Outside complexes and distant events.** Insert each formal equation or homotopy into the fixed planar outside by [F4]. For two distant elementary events, decompose their disjoint support disks and the outside as one planar operation. Their maps have cochain degree zero; a Morse map can have nonzero quantum degree, but the totalization signs use cochain degree alone. Acting in the first disk and then the second therefore gives the same matrix as acting in the opposite order. The crossing-order changes in [F1] are exactly the signed tensor interchanges of [F7], so the assertion also holds when a Reidemeister event changes the number or order of crossings. In particular it holds for the two distant surface-height critical events in the statement. Now all objects are closed resolutions. Apply [F6] entry by entry; its additivity, gluing and relation factorization preserve each formal chain-map equality and homotopy. The images are precisely the integral maps fixed in [F1], including empty resolutions and the identity on unaffected circles.

Pass to homology in step 3.1. A chain homotopy becomes equality, and the one scalar $\varepsilon$ becomes multiplication by that same overall sign on the full integral homology group. The construction covered MM1–MM5, MM6–MM10 and MM11–MM15, all their stated variants, and the distant interchanges. Thus every relation asserted in the statement preserves the selected map up to one sign. No assertion about spherical sweep-around follows from these Euclidean local computations.
